Deere's 2024 reference lists transmission oil filter LVA16054 and 12.3 L (12.9 US qt) of TY22000 Low Viscosity Hy-Gard, with a 200-hour entry. Do not infer that the entire hydraulic system empties completely during routine servicing; the manual describes drains, filters, safe pressure release and level verification.

Revision warning: a Deere filter overview from February 2019 additionally states that the hydraulic filter is replaced after the first 50 hours and every 200 hours thereafter. The January 2024 document presents its own interval summary. We report these as two different dated Deere documents, not as universally compatible instructions. Resolve first-service questions against the operator manual for your tractor's exact serial and model year.

Fuel filters and the kit-number decision

The 2024 worldwide guide gives inline fuel filter AM116304 and fuel filter element MIU804763, with the 400-hour/annual fuel-filter service note. An older February 2019 overview lists M801101 as the engine fuel filter for a 1025R overview. Because manufacturer documentation can change, do not order a fuel filter solely from an older shared PDF. Check Deere's current parts catalog and the engine/application identifiers.

Deere also lists two multi-filter packages depending on a 1025R serial range: LVA21036 and TA25769. A packaged kit may not cover every system due at 200 hours, and the operator manual — not the kit's name — determines what to service.

Record the work

Write down the current engine-hour reading, date, serial number, service performed, actual part numbers and oil types used. A list of “every 200 hours” items is not a substitute for tracking the previous service: a machine serviced at 120 hours has a different next-service calculation from one serviced at 200 hours. Keep dealer receipts and note any recurring leaks, alarms or unusual wear.

Official Deere documentation

John Deere 1025R Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide, LV609412, January 2024, contrasted with John Deere 1E / 1R Filter Overview, February 2019. Both are manufacturer documents. For the final procedure, serial-specific instructions and approved fluids, use the current operator manual for your machine.

records.title: John Deere 1025R Air Filters: M131802 vs LVU34503 Serial Numbers
records.excerpt: John Deere's 2024 1025R parts guide lists M131802/M131803 through JJ153036 and LVU34503/LVU34504 from JJ153037. Check both primary and secondary filters before buying.
records.content:
Two primary air filter numbers are commonly associated with the John Deere 1025R: M131802 and LVU34503. They are not the same catalog reference. Deere's own January 2024 replacement-parts guide identifies a serial-number boundary between the two. The document also names different secondary air elements for those ranges.

1025R air filter serial number comparison

Manufacturer-listed serial applicabilityPrimary air cleanerSecondary air cleaner
Through JJ153036M131802M131803
Beginning JJ153037LVU34503LVU34504

These boundaries and component numbers appear in the Deere Worldwide 1025R Replacement Parts Guide, document LV609412, issued January 2024. The letters are part of the manufacturer's serial notation in this guide. Do not assume you can identify the correct air filter merely from the tractor's advertised production year, hood shape or a product photo.

What do primary and secondary air elements do?

The primary element provides the first stage of air filtration to protect the diesel engine from airborne contaminants. The secondary, or safety, element offers additional protection inside the intake-filter arrangement. Both matter for proper engine protection. A filter that fits into the canister is not necessarily the correct part: airflow specification, sealing and correct service procedures also matter.

How to identify the correct version

  1. Identify the tractor as a Deere 1025R and record the full model/serial information from the manufacturer-designated identification location.
  2. Consult the January 2024 Deere parts guide for the JJ153036/JJ153037 air-cleaner change.
  3. Check the official Deere electronic parts catalog using the complete machine identifier for any additional serial, market or engine restrictions.
  4. Confirm whether the individual component has been superseded since the PDF's publication date.
  5. Order the matched primary and secondary parts required by your actual service task, not a mixed set assembled from search snippets.

Which 1025R filter kit contains which primary element?

For certain 1025R serial ranges, John Deere's US parts store lists the LVA21036 Filter Pak (including primary M131802) and the TA25769 Filter Pak (including primary LVU34503). The manufacturer describes these as generally compatible kit applications. The bundle is not itself proof that every part inside it matches a modified, repowered or unusual-market tractor.

Also note that the primary air filter kit lists do not automatically prove that a secondary element is included. Check each package's official itemized contents. Deere's 2024 guide distinguishes M131803 and LVU34504 as the secondary elements, separate from the primary filter identifiers.

When should you inspect or change them?

The January 2024 guide displays a 200-hour and annual replacement note next to the primary and secondary air elements. An earlier February 2019 filter overview uses a different general air-filter interval description and emphasizes checking restrictions. These are dated manufacturer publications, not an instruction to replace filters on every tractor in every condition. Dusty operating environments, service-indicator behavior and operator-manual directions can justify a different inspection or replacement plan.

Do not blow compressed air through a filter element unless the operator manual explicitly permits the procedure, pressure limits and direction. Never run the engine without its specified air filter or with a damaged housing seal. If there is evidence of dirt ingestion on the clean-air side, obtain professional guidance before continued operation.

What if the numbers in your manual differ?

Operator manuals and parts catalogs sometimes reflect manufacturing revisions, markets and service substitutions made after older PDFs were issued. If your tractor's complete serial number returns a different current part than the 2024 guide, do not attempt to reconcile the difference by dimensions or web forum pictures. Ask the dealer for the correct factory application and any official supersession chain.

Original documentation

Primary technical reference: John Deere Worldwide 1025R Replacement Parts Guide (LV609412, January 2024). Context: Deere 1E and 1R filter overview (February 2019). Exact part fitment requires the current electronic parts catalog and the machine's complete identification.

records.title: John Deere 1025R Fluid Capacities: Engine Oil and Transmission
records.excerpt: Official Deere 1025R reference values: engine oil with filter 2.7 L (2.9 US qt), transmission/hydraulic oil 12.3 L (12.9 US qt), plus notes on older guide versions.
records.content:
Before servicing a John Deere 1025R, confirm the fluid capacity for the specific system. Engine crankcase oil, transmission/hydraulic oil, cooling-system fluid and front-axle lubricant are not interchangeable. The amount shown on a manufacturer's capacity chart may also differ from the quantity actually required after a routine partial drain.

2024 Deere 1025R fluid references

Fluid systemPublished quantityManufacturer reference
Engine oil with filter2.7 L / 2.9 US quartsDeere January 2024 Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide, TY26669 PLUS-50 II 10W-30 listed
Transmission / hydraulic oil12.3 L / 12.9 US quartsDeere January 2024 guide, TY22000 Low Viscosity Hy-Gard listed

The January 2024 reference uses rounded metric and US values in its equipment listing. A quantity given in liters alongside a rounded US-quart value is not a precision fill target; follow the operator manual's level check. The manual governs the particular oil grade for your climate, usage and model/serial configuration.

What about coolant, the fuel tank and front axle?

Deere's earlier February 2019 1E/1R filter overview includes approximate figures for the platform: 21.2 L (5.6 US gal) fuel tank, 3.7 L (0.98 US gal) cooling system, 2.8 L (0.74 US gal) front axle, and 12.3 L (3.3 US gal) transmission/hydraulic system. The older overview groups the 1023E, 1025R and 1026R, so it is not proof that every machine in every year has identical capacities. We preserve that document context instead of presenting all values as current specifications for every 1025R.

For coolant and front axle service, always verify the exact machine's operator manual and current Deere lubricant recommendations before buying fluid or calculating refill quantities. Do not mix old and new coolant types based solely on color.

Engine oil: don't mistake the capacity for a service procedure

The 2024 guide reports 2.7 liters with filter and names the engine filter as M806418. Actual filling and final level verification are separate from the published nominal amount. A correctly performed oil change requires the machine to be shut down and secured, suitable oil-handling containers, a proper filter replacement procedure, and final level and leak checks according to the manual.

Engines in extreme heat, dust, prolonged idling or other harsh conditions may require special maintenance consideration. Use the manufacturer-approved viscosity for the expected ambient temperature rather than assuming that one grade listed on an overview PDF suits every US climate.

Transmission oil and hydraulics

The published 12.3 L (12.9 US qt) figure is a transmission/hydraulic system reference and is associated with Low Viscosity Hy-Gard in the 2024 parts guide. It does not establish that 12.3 liters must be poured after every routine filter change. Reservoirs, hoses and hydraulic components can retain oil. The LVA16054 filter is identified in the same guide, but service must follow the manual's draining, pressure release, filtering and refill sequence.

High-pressure hydraulic injury hazard: never search for a pinhole leak with your hand or attempt to disconnect a pressurized line. Lower implements and follow approved lockout/safe support procedures first. Seek emergency care immediately if pressurized fluid is injected through skin.

2019 vs 2024 documentation: why dates matter

The February 2019 filter overview provides a broader approximate capacity chart and lists a first-50-hour hydraulic filter replacement. The January 2024 worldwide replacement-parts guide lists current component references and its own service notes. These are different revisions. Do not combine one document's intervals with another's part numbers without checking the operator manual and the complete tractor serial.

Practical service preparation

  • Write down the exact model, complete serial identifier and current hour meter reading.
  • Confirm the system being serviced: engine, transmission/hydraulics, front axle or cooling.
  • Find the current manufacturer lubricant table and any temperature-dependent options for the tractor.
  • Use documented filters and check for supersessions; see the 1025R filter-kit lookup.
  • Follow the proper level checks after refilling, and retain the date/hours/part numbers in a maintenance record.

For a model-wide checklist, see our 1025R 200-hour service guide. The information above is independently summarized from Deere's own documents, not a substitute for a safe model-specific procedure.

Manufacturer documents

John Deere Worldwide 1025R Replacement Parts Guide, LV609412, January 2024 and Deere 1E and 1R Filter Overview, February 2019. Verify any later official service bulletins or operator-manual revisions before servicing.

records.title: Kubota BX1880 Specifications: Engine HP, PTO and Hitch
records.excerpt: Kubota BX1880 US specifications: 16.6 gross engine horsepower, 13.7 PTO horsepower, 4WD hydrostatic drive, Category I hitch and manufacturer-listed 6.6 US-gallon fuel tank.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: Kubota USA BX80 series; 4WD high/low HST. Engine gross and PTO ratings are for BX1880 in the BX80 technical brochure, not the new BX90 series. The published 680-lb rear hitch lift is a BX Series figure; confirm the precise test point and attachments in the serial-specific manual. Hydraulic flow, loader lift and actual equipped weight omitted without comparable model-specific conditions.

records.content:
The Kubota BX1880 is a sub-compact, four-wheel-drive diesel tractor in Kubota's BX80 family. It targets mowing, property maintenance, light landscaping and snow removal where maneuverability is valuable. This reference uses the BX80 model designation and separates engine horsepower from usable PTO horsepower rather than mixing them together.

BX1880 engine horsepower

Kubota identifies the BX1880 with a D722 three-cylinder diesel. Kubota's US BX80 information lists 16.6 gross engine horsepower. Gross engine power describes output under the manufacturer's test conditions, not the amount of power a rear-mounted mower necessarily receives. For buying decisions, compare the exact implement's requirements with the tractor's relevant rating.

Rear PTO and HST transmission

The BX1880's published PTO power is 13.7 hp. Its rear PTO is rated at 540 rpm and the BX series also offers a separate mid PTO for compatible mower equipment. PTO power, shaft speed and implement geometry are all distinct requirements. An implement that physically connects is not automatically safe or suitable.

The BX80 tractor family uses four-wheel drive and hydrostatic transmission with a high/low range. The hydrostatic control may be useful where the operator frequently changes speed and direction, such as lawn maintenance and material handling. For slopes, soft ground or loaded attachments, traction, tire choice, ballast and manufacturer safety limits matter at least as much as transmission style.

Three-point hitch and attachments

Kubota lists the BX series with a Category I rear three-point hitch and a published 680-lb hitch lift figure. That number is a source-specific BX series rating, not a promise that every 680-lb attachment can be safely transported in every configuration. The test point, attachment center of gravity and tractor ballast are important. Our hitch capacity guide explains why ratings at different load positions cannot be directly compared.

Fuel, storage and operating choices

The BX80 technical specifications list a 6.6-US-gallon fuel tank. Tank capacity does not predict operating duration without knowing the load, engine speed and conditions. Kubota also highlights the foldable rollover protective structure for fitting these tractors into restricted storage space. Always observe the manufacturer's rollover protection and seat-belt instructions and verify real machine height with the tires and any installed attachments.

BX1880 versus other sub-compacts

The BX2380 has a published 21.6 gross engine hp and 17.7 PTO hp; the BX2680 is listed higher still in Kubota's current US BX80 series information. A smaller model may meet a property owner's needs without additional bulk or price, but the choice depends on required PTO output, ground clearance, attachments and dealer support.

For a new-generation comparison, Kubota has also announced the BX90 series. Do not confuse a BX1880 with a BX2190: the product family, configuration and announced features differ. Review our BX80 versus BX90 analysis.

What to verify before buying a used BX1880

  • Check the complete model identification and serial number, and obtain the matching operator manual.
  • Inspect the tire type, hydraulic connections, mower-deck mount and PTO equipment fitted to the actual tractor.
  • Ask for maintenance records and confirm the service schedule based on hours and calendar time.
  • Confirm the selected implement's minimum PTO power, hitch category, load rating and guarding.
  • Check the tractor's actual weight with attachments before planning transport.

Official manufacturer reference

Kubota USA BX80 Series product page, checked 2026-11-23. Detailed brochure revisions and regional or year-specific options can differ; this page intentionally leaves uncertain measurements blank rather than substituting figures from another configuration.

records.title: Kubota BX2680 Specs: 23.3 Gross HP, 19.2 PTO HP
records.excerpt: US Kubota BX2680 reference using the current BX80 series listing: 23.3 gross engine HP, 19.2 PTO HP, hydrostatic 4WD and Category I hitch. Confirm exact model-year brochure for additional figures.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: Current Kubota USA BX80 Series product presentation gives 23.3 gross engine hp as series maximum, 19.2 PTO hp as BX series upper figure. Historical Kubota US full-line brochures have reported different BX2680 power ratings. Confirm serial and year before selecting implements. Weight and individual loader ratings deliberately omitted from standardized fields pending test-point and exact brochure validation.

records.content:
The Kubota BX2680 is a sub-compact diesel tractor in the US BX80 family. Kubota currently presents it as the higher-horsepower model among the three BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 choices. Published figures need to be read with care: different Kubota USA brochures from different revisions have reported different horsepower values for a similarly named BX2680.

What is the BX2680 engine horsepower?

On its current US BX80 Series page, Kubota presents the BX2680 at 23.3 gross engine horsepower. The same BX80 product-family information gives the series PTO-power range as 13.7–19.2 hp, with the highest figure associated with the top of the series. This reference records 19.2 PTO hp and explicitly associates these values with the current BX80 listing.

Older Kubota full-line brochures may show a different rated power for the BX2680. A higher number in another official brochure is not necessarily a mistake: model-year, emissions and product revision context may differ. We do not silently combine one publication's engine horsepower with another publication's weight or hydraulic figures. For a used tractor, the year and complete serial are more important than assuming every internet table describes the same configuration.

Engine and power take-off

The BX2680 is associated with the Kubota D1005 three-cylinder diesel. The BX80 family offers both rear and mid power take-off connections, with a published 540-rpm rear PTO. Engine horsepower and PTO horsepower are different ratings. An attachment's minimum PTO power requirement must be assessed against the relevant PTO figure, not the tractor's gross engine rating.

For a mower or tiller, also check the correct PTO shaft size, operating speed, attachment mass, hitch geometry and safety guards. A manufacturer-approved mower deck does not establish that every third-party deck will fit. Our engine versus PTO horsepower guide describes the distinction.

4WD hydrostatic drivetrain

The BX2680 uses four-wheel drive and hydrostatic transmission in the BX80 platform. A hydrostatic drive can be convenient for repeated speed adjustments and directional changes in property maintenance, landscaping and front-loader tasks. It does not independently determine loader capacity or safe slope performance: weight distribution, tires, ballast, operator technique and ground conditions remain critical.

Hitch, loader and hydraulic ratings

Kubota lists the BX family with a Category I three-point hitch and a series-level 680-lb hitch capacity. Before buying a heavy rear implement, compare ratings at matching measuring points. Do not equate a hitch rating with a loader bucket, pallet-fork or front-loader rating.

The BX series offers loader quick-connection options and compatible mower decks. Loader capacities differ with loader model, quick-attach hardware, lift height and the point at which the load is measured. We have intentionally not placed a single loader lift number into this tractor's standardized comparison record without a verified matching test condition.

Fuel and equipment mass

Kubota's BX80 technical literature lists a 6.6-US-gallon fuel capacity. Published bare-tractor weights may depend on options or source edition; verify the exact machine and count the loader, filled tires, ballast and implements for transport. Do not use a sales brochure's unconfigured weight as the safe tow weight.

BX2680 versus BX2380 and BX1880

The BX1880 sits lower in the BX80 range at 16.6 gross engine hp and 13.7 PTO hp. The BX2380 is listed at 21.6 gross engine hp and 17.7 PTO hp in Kubota documentation. The BX2680's higher published power may make a difference when a PTO implement's required power approaches the lower model's rating; it is not evidence of proportionally greater lift or towing capacity.

What to ask the dealer

  • Which exact BX2680 model year and serial-number range do these specifications apply to?
  • What is the complete weight of the quoted tractor including loader, tire fill and rear ballast?
  • Which loader and mower configurations are officially supported, and at what measured test points are their lift ratings stated?
  • Does the implement's specified minimum PTO hp fall within this exact variant's published value?
  • Can the dealer supply the serial-specific operator manual, maintenance schedule and parts lookup?

Original technical reference

Primary source: Kubota USA — BX80 Series, checked 2026-11-23. For historical BX2680 units, consult the exact-year official brochure and manual. We omit uncertain model-specific weight and hydraulic figures rather than provide an apparently precise but potentially mismatched number.

records.title: Kubota BX1880 vs BX2380 vs BX2680: Which Sub-Compact?
records.excerpt: Compare Kubota BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 engine and PTO horsepower, attachments and buying tradeoffs without mixing different brochure versions.
records.content:
Owners shopping for a Kubota BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680 usually want more than a horsepower list. They want to know whether the smaller machine can run the mower they already own, whether a bigger model helps with loader tasks, and whether a particular used tractor's price is justified. A model-specific comparison starts with clearly sourced ratings and ends with the requirements of the actual attachment.

Kubota BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 power comparison

BX80 modelGross engine hp (current US BX80 source)Published PTO hpTypical focus
BX188016.613.7Smaller-scale property maintenance and compatible mowing
BX238021.617.7General mowing, loader and light landscaping tasks
BX268023.319.2Greater published PTO output within this BX80 source version

The figures here are drawn from the current Kubota USA BX80 Series presentation and corresponding BX80 documentation. Some older full-product-line brochures list a different engine rating for the BX2680. Do not mix those figures or infer a tractor's exact engine from the model name without its serial and model year.

Is 16.6 horsepower enough for mowing?

That depends on the deck, cutting width, vegetation and terrain. The BX1880 is not automatically unsuitable because it has less engine power. Check the specific deck manufacturer's recommended tractor and PTO horsepower, mounting arrangement and operating speed. A 48-inch deck intended for one sub-compact platform is not necessarily interchangeable with a different mower just because the nominal width matches.

If the property has long, thick grass, slopes or conditions where operating speed must be reduced, consider how the selected deck loads the tractor. Running a cutting implement below the required PTO speed can affect performance and protection. Follow the attachment manual rather than assuming the largest engine model always permits a larger deck.

Does the BX2680 lift more than the BX1880?

Engine horsepower is not loader capacity. The lift rating of a front loader depends on the specific loader model, pivot-pin or forward measurement position, lift height, attachment weight and ballast. A manufacturer series overview may show a maximum figure that is not equal to the capability of every model/attachment combination. Ask for loader-specific test charts taken at the same locations before comparing a BX1880 with a BX2680 for pallet forks or soil handling.

Three-point hitch and implements

The BX80 series is listed with a Category I rear hitch. For a rear rotary cutter, ballast box or tiller, verify the implement's weight, required PTO power, hitch dimensions and safe transport configuration. The published lift capacity does not determine how a long or rear-heavy attachment will affect the tractor's stability. Our lift-capacity measuring-point guide illustrates the difference.

Why transmission style isn't the differentiator

All three models in the BX80 family use four-wheel drive and hydrostatic transmissions. Rather than comparing a manual against an HST, focus on power rating, controls, mower options, dealer support, physical condition and equipment installed. If a manual-versus-HST decision is important to you, compare other compact tractor models where the manufacturer actually offers the two alternatives.

New versus used: verify the year

A used BX2680 listing may quote an engine horsepower value from a historical brochure, while a current Kubota USA page lists another value. The correct question is not which web page has the bigger number. Ask the dealer for the year-specific brochure and serial-specific manual. Check maintenance records, loader mount, quick couplers, hoses, hydraulic leaks, mower spindle condition, tires, pins and guards. A machine that is superficially clean can still have expensive deferred maintenance.

Checklist before making a decision

  1. List your actual jobs and the heaviest intended PTO-powered attachments.
  2. Check the minimum required PTO horsepower and approved deck/implement fitment.
  3. Obtain loader ratings measured at matching lift heights and load positions.
  4. Compare the real tire and ballast configuration and total working mass.
  5. Confirm local parts/service availability and the machine's actual condition.
  6. Use our machine comparison tool with the manufacturer's source notes visible.

Which BX would we choose?

There is no single right answer. The BX1880 may be sufficient for owner-maintained lawns and suitable smaller implements. The BX2380 is worth considering when a little more PTO output or a different equipment package makes sense. The BX2680 adds published power within the current BX80 series but should not be assumed to increase every lifting or hydraulic specification by the same percentage. Judge the purchase based on the actual work, configuration and total dealer quote, not the largest horsepower badge.

Official source

Kubota USA BX80 Series equipment overview and model ratings, checked 2026-11-23. Kubota has announced a separate BX90 family for 2027, discussed in our BX90 vs BX80 guide.

records.title: John Deere 1025R vs Kubota BX2380: PTO, Weight & Hydraulics
records.excerpt: Compare John Deere 1025R and Kubota BX2380 manufacturer specifications: engine HP, PTO HP, hitch category, hydraulic pump figures and published tractor weight.
records.content:
The John Deere 1025R and Kubota BX2380 are frequently considered for mowing, snow removal, landscaping and small-property work. A useful comparison looks beyond the biggest engine-power figure. Transmission layout, PTO rating, attachment interfaces, loader specifications and the tractor's actual equipped weight determine whether a machine suits an owner's work.

Published specification comparison

Manufacturer-listed figureJohn Deere 1025RKubota BX2380
Engine power24 rated HP (SAE J1995 in the US product specification)21.6 gross HP
Rear PTO power18 hp17.7 hp
Transmission typeHydrostatic, two rangesHydrostatic, two ranges
Rear hitchLimited Category 1SAE Category 1
Published hydraulic pump figure6.3 US gpm rated output6.2 US gpm total system output in detailed BX2380 specification
Published machine weight1,556 lb (base machine)1,455 lb (base tractor in the selected detailed specification)
Rear hitch lift at 24 inches behind pointsNot established by the referenced Deere product page680 lb in the detailed Kubota source

These are independently summarized manufacturer figures, not results of our own dynamometer, loader or hydraulic testing. Different source documents may use different rating conditions. The Deere and Kubota figures must not be treated as perfectly matched tests simply because both are displayed in US units.

Engine power vs PTO power

The Deere product information lists 24 hp engine power and 18 hp PTO power. Kubota's detailed BX2380 specification gives 21.6 gross engine hp and 17.7 PTO hp. The nominal PTO figures are close, even though the stated engine ratings are farther apart. For a rear rotary cutter or tiller, check its minimum PTO hp, rated 540-rpm connection, safe attachment geometry and manufacturer requirements rather than deciding based only on gross engine horsepower.

The underlying methods matter as well: not every engine-power rating uses the same laboratory conditions. Compare the original footnotes in the documents before making conclusions about real-world fuel use or field productivity.

Hydraulic flow numbers are not directly equivalent

John Deere's 1025R product listing provides a rated pump output of 6.3 US gpm. Kubota's BX2380 detailed specification lists a total system flow of 6.2 US gpm, composed of separate implement and steering pump figures. A published combined number does not mean a grapple, loader auxiliary port or other hydraulic attachment can receive the entire amount. Ask for circuit-specific flow and pressure information for the exact installed valve and attachment.

Hitch category and loader compatibility

Deere labels its hitch limited Category 1; Kubota lists Category 1. Those labels do not guarantee identical full-size implement geometry, lift height or usable capacity. Confirm the required PTO shaft length and angles, implement hitch clearances, ballast and actual lift position. Loader ratings are even more sensitive to the bucket, quick-attach system, lifting height and point at which capacity is measured. Do not use the weight or horsepower table above as a loader capacity comparison.

Weight and transportation

The listed 1,556-lb Deere and 1,455-lb Kubota figures are manufacturer-published base weights. They are not transport weights for a tractor fitted with a loader, fluid-filled rear tires, a mower and a counterweight. Use the complete operating configuration for trailer, tow-vehicle, hitch, ramp and tie-down decisions. Real stability depends on ballast, tire pressure, slopes, surface conditions and attachment position.

Which tractor should you test?

For a property used mainly for mowing and seasonal chores, compare the exact mower options, ease of attachment changes, storage dimensions and local dealer service. For frequent loader work, test the controls and quick couplers and ask the dealer for an official loader specification at the same measuring position. For PTO-heavy tasks, use the implement maker's required PTO horsepower. A small difference in brochure PTO power is not a reliable prediction of every job's productivity.

Used tractor buying checklist

  1. Identify the complete serial number and exact model-year configuration.
  2. Inspect transmission response, steering, tires, hydraulic hoses, couplers, PTO guards and visible leaks according to safety instructions.
  3. Confirm all offered attachments are actually compatible, including the mounting system and any additional hydraulics required.
  4. Read service records and verify that the correct model-specific filters, oil and coolant were used.
  5. Compare total machine weight, dealer support, warranty or remaining coverage, and cost of the full equipment package.

Review the separate John Deere 1025R specifications and Kubota BX2380 specifications. You can also open our side-by-side comparison tool and select the two models.

Primary manufacturer references

John Deere USA — 1025R specifications and Kubota USA — BX2380 detailed specifications. Source material checked November 23, 2026. Year, market and model revisions can change the figures; use the current manuals for safety-critical decisions.

records.title: Tractor Hydraulic Flow Explained: Pump GPM vs Available Implement Flow
records.excerpt: Learn why tractor hydraulic pump GPM, total system flow and usable auxiliary circuit flow can be different, with manufacturer examples from Kubota and John Deere.
records.content:
If a tractor brochure says “6.2 GPM hydraulics,” does that mean a hydraulic log splitter, grapple or other implement receives all 6.2 gallons per minute? Not necessarily. The figure may refer to a combined system output, a dedicated implement pump, a steering circuit or another manufacturer-defined rating. Matching an attachment requires the actual flow and pressure available at the correct connection, not just the biggest GPM number on the specification sheet.

What does GPM mean on a tractor?

GPM stands for gallons per minute, a measure of flow rate. For US equipment, the unit usually means US gallons per minute. Flow is distinct from pressure, measured in psi, and from a loader's lifting capacity, measured in pounds at a specified geometry. Two tractors with the same published hydraulic flow can have different implement performance because pressure, valve layout, pump type and machine stability are not identical.

Total hydraulic flow vs main pump flow

A compact tractor can have more than one pump or hydraulic section. One portion may serve power steering while another supplies the implement circuit. A brochure may publish a system total, or show the components separately. Do not interpret a combined total as guaranteed available flow at a rear remote or third-function valve.

Manufacturer examples

TractorPublished figureImportant qualification
Kubota BX23806.2 US gpm totalThe detailed source breaks it into 5.2 US gpm implement-system output and 1.0 US gpm steering output; do not use the total as a universal remote rating.
John Deere 1025R6.3 US gpm rated pump outputThe cited product page reports a rated output; it does not alone establish delivered flow and pressure at a specific accessory coupler.
Kubota L3302 HST6.8 US gpm main pumpKubota's US L02 brochure also lists a separate steering pump. The main-pump figure is not automatically the flow available to every accessory.

These examples explain how specification labels vary. They do not represent comparable independent measurements under a common test procedure. Read the source notes on each machine page.

Why GPM alone does not size a hydraulic implement

For a hydraulic attachment, manufacturers may specify a minimum and maximum permissible flow, a required operating pressure, a compatible valve type and a return-flow arrangement. A device may run too slowly with insufficient flow or be damaged if flow, pressure or plumbing exceed its design. Some attachments also require continuous-flow capability or a case-drain connection. These needs cannot be established from total tractor GPM.

Loader force is a separate question. A lift capacity published at a pivot pin or 500 mm forward is affected by loader geometry and stability, not GPM alone. Raising pressure above official limits is not a safe way to increase lifting capability and can cause hose, component or structural failure.

How to choose a compatible hydraulic attachment

  1. Find the attachment maker's documented flow and pressure range and any valve or return requirements.
  2. Identify the tractor's exact model, year, serial range and installed hydraulic options.
  3. Ask for available flow and pressure at the specific circuit that will power the attachment, not just a brochure's system total.
  4. Confirm connector size, valve control, continuous-flow compatibility, hose routing and pressure-relief protection.
  5. Verify that the tractor and attachment are stable with appropriate ballast and within all load and axle limits.
  6. Use the factory procedures or qualified service for installation; never work on a pressurized hydraulic line.

Can two machines be compared by pump GPM?

The figure can be one useful screening criterion when the manufacturer states the same kind of measurement. It is not an independent performance rating. For a better comparison, record whether each value represents total system, main/implement pump or remote available flow and check the pressure measurement. Our comparison tool stores published figures and configuration notes, but it does not infer unknown remote flow.

Safety warning for hydraulic troubleshooting

Pressurized hydraulic oil can penetrate skin through a tiny opening and cause severe injury. Never use your hand to locate leaks. Lower supported equipment, follow the correct machine's pressure-release procedure and seek professional service if the circuit condition is uncertain. Hydraulic injection injuries require emergency medical attention.

Sources

Kubota USA — BX2380 detailed specifications, John Deere — 1025R US product specification, and the Kubota USA L02 specification brochure. Sources checked November 23, 2026. Always defer to serial-specific manufacturer information and the attachment's installation instructions.

records.title: John Deere 1M 25 Specs: 24 HP, PTO Power, Weight and Hitch
records.excerpt: Official US John Deere 1M 25 specs: Yanmar 3TNV80F-NCJT, 24 rated engine HP, 18 PTO HP, two-range hydrostatic transmission, limited Category 1 hitch, 6.3 gpm pump and 1,556 lb base weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US 1M 25 product page (SAE J1995 rated engine power). Manufacturer lists 6.3 gpm rated pump output; do not assume flow at individual hydraulic remotes. 1,556 lb is base tractor weight, not a configured lift/transport weight. Hitch is LIMITED Category 1, not universal full-size Cat 1 fitment. Specs may vary by market, year and attachments.

records.content:
The John Deere 1M 25 is a US-market sub-compact tractor intended for property maintenance, mower work and compact implement use. Deere's official product specification gives 24 rated engine horsepower, 18 PTO horsepower and a two-range hydrostatic transmission. Its headline power and base weight may resemble other Deere sub-compact models, but matching numbers are not proof that every mower deck, loader or part interchanges.

Engine and rated power

Deere identifies a Yanmar 3TNV80F-NCJT, three-cylinder, naturally aspirated diesel with a displacement of 1.267 liters (77 cubic inches). The stated 24 hp engine rating uses SAE J1995. When comparing it with a competitor whose listing says gross or net power, check the standards before treating the values as equivalent measurements.

18 PTO hp and rear PTO speed

The US listing states 18 rated PTO hp. The available rear PTO speed is 540 rpm, with a separate mid-PTO figure of 2,100 rpm described on the manufacturer specification. An attachment's shaft-speed requirement, maximum permitted power and PTO driveline arrangement should be confirmed separately from the tractor's engine horsepower.

PTO ratings are particularly relevant to mowers, snowblowers and powered tillers. The engine-versus-PTO horsepower guide explains why a 24-hp engine does not mean a 24-hp output at the attachment.

Two-range hydrostatic transmission

John Deere lists a hydrostatic two-range transmission and a wet-disc clutch. Hydrostatic travel controls can help with changing ground speed and direction in tight spaces, though the correct operating range, safe handling, ground traction and operator experience remain important. Do not assume a particular loader duty cycle or slope capability from transmission style alone.

Hydraulic pump and hitch

The source reports 6.3 US gpm rated pump output and a limited Category 1 three-point hitch. The first value is a manufacturer pump rating, not a verified continuous-flow rating at a third-function valve. The second is a more restrictive hitch description than a blanket promise of every full-size Category 1 implement fitting and lifting safely. Check hitch geometry, PTO driveline clearance and implement demands.

Published base weight

Deere lists 1,556 lb as base machine weight. That does not describe the actual mass of a tractor after a front loader, mower, ballast, filled tires or other equipment is added. Use the real total machine configuration to make towing and trailer decisions, and follow the manufacturer's ballast and load-handling guidance.

Comparing with another sub-compact

The John Deere 1025R is worth reviewing because its present Deere listing also reports 24 rated engine hp, 18 PTO hp, 6.3 gpm pump output and limited Category 1 hitch. Similar top-line data does not establish that frame components, loader hookups, serial-specific parts or optional equipment are interchangeable. The factory parts catalog and actual machine configuration still govern those choices.

The Kubota BX2380 is another sub-compact alternative, but the manufacturer's hydraulic-flow labels and testing conditions are not identical. Our tractor comparison retains the source notes and leaves unverified figures blank.

What to inspect before buying

  • Complete product identifier, production version, serial and correct operator manual
  • Actual front-loader, mower deck and quick-connection hardware included with the tractor
  • Rear hitch category, lift-point geometry and appropriate attachment ballast
  • Service access, nearby dealer support and warranty details for the actual US machine
  • Storage clearance and true loaded transport weight rather than bare tractor weight

Official reference

John Deere USA 1M 25 manufacturer specifications, checked November 23, 2026. The official page notes that features, availability and equipment packages may change. Always defer to the correct serial-specific manual for service, safety and parts.

records.title: John Deere 5050E Tractor Specs: 50 Engine HP, 38 PTO HP
records.excerpt: John Deere 5050E US factory specs: 50 rated engine HP, 38 rated PTO HP, 9F/3R SyncShuttle, Category 2 convertible to 1 hitch, 18.2 gpm two-pump rating and 5,335-lb base machine weight.

specs.fms_engine_make: John Deere PowerTech 3029 EWR turbocharged diesel
specs.fms_configuration_notes: Deere US 5050E listing; 50 HP rated engine, 38 HP rated PTO; SyncShuttle 9 forward / 3 reverse; 18.2 gpm pump rated output is explicitly TWO engine-mounted pumps and is not a remote-valve flow guarantee; listed 5,335 lb base weight depends on configuration. Category 2 hitch convertible to 1; confirm exact hardware and attachment limits.

records.content:
The John Deere 5050E is a utility tractor that sits in a substantially larger equipment class than Deere's 1M 25 or 1025R sub-compacts. Deere's US product page identifies a 50-hp diesel engine, 38 rated PTO horsepower and a 9-forward / 3-reverse SyncShuttle transmission. These manufacturer figures make the model worth considering for heavier property, livestock and agricultural tasks, but the actual implement requirements and tractor configuration remain decisive.

Engine: 50 rated horsepower

Deere specifies a PowerTech 3029 EWR three-cylinder diesel with 2.9 liters (179 cubic inches) displacement and a turbocharger. The manufacturer lists 50 rated engine horsepower. Engine power is not a loader lifting rating and does not establish how many acres the tractor can work in a day. Tractor traction, ballast, speed, implement width, soil and operating conditions all matter.

38 PTO horsepower and PTO type

The US specification gives 38 rated PTO hp and a 540-rpm rear PTO. This helps when reviewing PTO-driven implement requirements. Deere identifies mechanical-lever engagement on the referenced specification. For balers, brush cutters, tillers or other driven equipment, confirm the implement's horsepower range, safety guarding, shaft length and hitch or drawbar requirements.

Transmission and operator controls

The listed SyncShuttle 9F/3R transmission has nine forward and three reverse ratios. It is not equivalent to a continuous hydrostatic drive with speed controlled by a single pedal. Operators who regularly switch direction or perform loader jobs should test the controls and operating procedure on the actual tractor, not assume that a larger engine means a faster loader duty cycle.

Hitch category: 2, convertible to 1

Deere calls the rear hitch Category 2, convertible to Category 1. That description does not promise every Category 1 or Category 2 attachment will clear the tires, PTO shaft, linkage or drawbar. Correct spacers, balls, quick-hitch geometry, required PTO power and implement mass still have to match. The published hitch designation is not itself a lift-capacity figure.

Hydraulics: what 18.2 gpm means

The manufacturer lists 18.2 US gpm rated pump output and specifies two engine-mounted pumps. Do not enter this value as verified flow at a single hydraulic remote. Equipment requiring a hydraulic motor or continuous-flow coupler needs a check of actual flow and pressure at the installed circuit. The hydraulic GPM guide explains this distinction.

Published base weight and transportation

Deere lists 5,335 lb base machine weight. A front loader, ballast, liquid-filled tires, cab, attachment or full fuel tank changes actual operating and transport weight. A 5,335-lb brochure figure is not sufficient on its own to choose a trailer, tow vehicle, ramp or tie-down arrangement.

Compared with smaller compact tractors

The difference between this utility tractor and a Kubota L3902 HST is not simply 50 versus 37.5 engine horsepower. The machines also differ in transmissions, hitch systems, overall mass, and likely handling needs; their ratings come from different manufacturer publications. Begin by matching the heaviest real implement and property work rather than selecting solely on price or maximum power.

Before purchasing

  1. Identify whether your tractor quote covers the exact US 5050E configuration and current equipment generation.
  2. Review the full serial-specific owner's manual and official attached-implement compatibility documents.
  3. Obtain the correct rated loader lift at the appropriate measuring point.
  4. Check the hydraulic flow, pressure and couplers at the circuit the implement will actually use.
  5. Budget for tire/ballast selection, safe transport, maintenance and local parts availability.

Manufacturer source

John Deere USA 5050E product technical specifications, checked November 23, 2026. Specifications depend on production and market options and are subject to change. This independently prepared reference is not an operator's manual or an endorsement of any particular attachment.

records.title: Compact Tractor Overheating While Mowing: Radiator and Cooling Checks
records.excerpt: A compact tractor runs hot while mowing? Safely investigate radiator screens, cooling airflow, coolant level and work load without opening a pressurized hot cooling system.
records.content:
A compact tractor that overheats while mowing should not be ignored or treated by simply continuing at higher engine speed. Grass clippings, chaff and dust can accumulate around the radiator screen or cooling fins, reducing airflow during prolonged PTO work. John Deere's operator-manual guidance specifically identifies dirty cooling screens and fins as an overheating risk. Kubota's maintenance guidance likewise includes daily cleaning of radiator screens and cores, with model-specific procedures in the appropriate manual.

First: what does “overheating” mean on your tractor?

Record the exact symptom. Is the temperature gauge entering a warning zone? Is a coolant warning light on? Does the machine lose power, emit steam, smell of coolant or shut itself down? A warm hood or radiator after mowing is not, by itself, a verified overheating fault. The machine's dashboard warnings and operator manual take priority over touching parts or guessing a temperature.

Observed symptomUseful first distinctionSafe response
Gauge rises during high-grass mowingAirflow restriction and sustained load are possibilities, not a diagnosisFollow the model's stop/cool-down instructions; inspect screens only after moving parts stop
Temperature warning or shutdownMay indicate a more serious cooling or sensor issueStop safely and follow the official warning procedure, not repeated mowing attempts
Visible coolant leak or steamCooling system may be hot and pressurizedKeep clear, shut down as instructed and obtain qualified service
Overheats soon after recent serviceCheck the repair/service history and coolant specificationDo not open a hot cap; ask a technician to verify the work and correct the fluid level

Why mower work exposes blocked cooling screens

Cutting dry grass, weeds or dusty vegetation can deposit light debris onto the tractor grille and radiator screen. A blocked screen reduces the air that the fan can pull through the cooling system. John Deere's Service Engine operator-manual section identifies both grille/side screens and radiator fins as items to keep clean.

The airflow problem may be worse when a mower is working in vegetation that generates abundant fine particles. Slow movement through heavy material can still put sustained demand on the engine. But engine overload, cooling-system leaks, incorrect coolant or a mechanical fault can also cause temperature warnings. A clean screen is a useful inspection, not proof that the engine is otherwise healthy.

Safe inspection: grille, screen and fins

  1. Follow the tractor's stop procedure. Move to a safe location, lower the implement, disengage the PTO and secure the machine as the operator manual requires.
  2. Wait for complete stop and cooling. Keep hands, clothing and tools away from fans, belts and other rotating components.
  3. Visually inspect the grille and removable screen. Note grass, dust and chaff packed into visible openings. Follow your exact manual's approved removal and cleaning methods.
  4. Protect the radiator fins. John Deere warns that pressure washing and angled compressed-air jets can bend cooling fins. The Deere manual cited here specifies a maximum cleaning air pressure for its machine; do not transplant that number to a different tractor unless its manual agrees.
  5. Reinstall guards and screens. Do not operate the machine with protective components removed or with dirt blown into the engine intake.

Coolant level: never open a hot pressure cap

A radiator and its pressurized cap can cause severe burns if opened while hot. Kubota's tractor safety guidance warns against adding coolant while the engine is hot; Deere's manual likewise requires cooling before pressure-cap service. Use the coolant recovery bottle as directed by your exact model's manual, and determine which mark applies when cold or warm. Do not open the cap just to “check quickly” after mowing.

If coolant is repeatedly disappearing, the machine may have a leak or another cooling-system problem. Simply topping off a leaking system before every mowing session is not a responsible fix. Follow the proper diagnostic and repair process.

When cleaning the screen is not enough

Repeated temperature alarms with a clean screen call for further inspection. A qualified technician may investigate coolant concentration, radiator core restriction, fan/drive condition, thermostat function, hoses, water pump, sensors or the effects of a high engine load. The exact sequence depends on the tractor's cooling-system design and service manual. Avoid replacing a thermostat or radiator on symptoms alone.

How to prevent repeat problems

  • Include the radiator screen, grille and intake openings in pre-operation inspections during dusty or grassy work.
  • Inspect coolant level, hoses and visible leaks at the intervals and under the conditions specified by your tractor's manual.
  • Use the correct mower and PTO setup; do not ignore sustained overload or dashboard warnings.
  • Maintain air filters and cooling components without damaging seals, fins or guards.
  • Record when overheating occurs: operating hours, ambient temperature, vegetation type, attachment and any warnings.

For a wider routine, see our compact tractor pre-season maintenance checklist. For mechanical issues unrelated to temperature, start with our diesel crank/no-start guide.

Primary references and limitations

John Deere operator-manual Service Engine section: cooling screens, fins and coolant safety; Kubota USA Maintenance Check Points; Kubota Tractor Safety. Checked November 23, 2026. The Deere manual describes a specific tractor family and is used here to support general principles, not as a service procedure for every compact machine.

records.title: Tractor Hydraulics Slow When Cold: Safe Oil and Filter Checks
records.excerpt: Slow loader or three-point hitch action in cold weather? Distinguish fluid temperature, model-specific oil viscosity, engine speed and filter issues from a hydraulic-system fault.
records.content:
A loader or three-point hitch that seems slow on a cold morning is not automatically a failed hydraulic pump. John Deere's operator-manual troubleshooting pages specifically include hydraulic oil too cold among potential hydraulic performance problems. Deere's hydraulic-fluid information also explains that oil becomes more viscous in low temperatures. That makes fluid selection and safe warm-up relevant, although a serious delay or loss of lifting ability still requires model-specific diagnosis.

Start by defining what is slow

Observed symptomInformation to recordWhy it matters
All hydraulic functions respond slowly only just after a cold startAir temperature, correct oil grade, time since start and approved warm-up procedureTemperature-related fluid behavior may be involved
Only one loader function is slowExact cylinder movement, controls and installed couplersA circuit-specific problem differs from a whole-system issue
Lift is slow even when warmed upEngine speed, current warning lights, service history, fluid/filter conditionPersistent poor performance needs further inspection
Fluid leaks, loud noises or unpredictable movementWhere observed, symptoms and work already performedCan be unsafe; stop and obtain professional service

This is a symptom organizer, not a definitive fault table for a particular loader, valve or tractor model. Do not raise hydraulic pressure or adjust relief settings to compensate for unexplained slowness.

1. Check the operator manual's cold-start instructions

Hydraulic oil and transmission oil may share a reservoir in some compact tractors, but that does not mean every machine uses the same fluid. The exact operator manual specifies any warm-up sequence, appropriate idle operation, safe control movement, allowed ambient temperatures and suitable viscosity class. Never repeatedly cycle an attachment against a relief stop or hold a loader at full pressure to “force it warm.” This can overheat or damage components.

2. Confirm the correct hydraulic/transmission fluid

John Deere's transmission and hydraulic oil guidance distinguishes Hy-Gard and Low-Viscosity Hy-Gard and describes oil viscosity changes with temperature. Choosing the correct fluid is a matter of the tractor's required specification and climate, not simply selecting the thinnest product at a store. An unsuitable or contaminated oil can create wear, noise and operating problems.

Do not assume the same product applies to a Kubota, KIOTI or another tractor solely because both use a hydrostatic transmission. Read the model-specific service literature and, if uncertain, obtain a dealer's confirmation before adding or changing fluid.

3. Verify the level using the manufacturer's procedure

Oil quantity should be inspected in the correct parking position and at the temperature stated by the manual. A system that is low or overfilled may perform poorly or be damaged. Never unscrew a pressurized hydraulic fitting or filter to see whether oil is circulating. Dirt entering an open hydraulic system can also cause expensive damage.

4. Service history and filters

Record the last hydraulic filter change, hour-meter reading and specific filter number. Some Deere maintenance tables identify an inline or transmission-hydraulic filter and service intervals that vary by model. A plugged filter or contaminated fluid is a possible cause of poor hydraulic performance, but that conclusion should be reached through inspection and the correct diagnostic procedure, not by bypassing a filter.

For the John Deere 1025R specifically, our 200-hour service guide records the parts referenced in Deere's January 2024 document. That is a separate source and should not be applied to an unrelated tractor.

5. Differentiate operating speed from hydraulic failure

Hydraulic pump output may change with engine speed, pump design and the path through a control valve. A slow response while operating below the manual's recommended engine speed is different from a machine that has stopped lifting under normal conditions. Check the prescribed operating range; do not try to overcome a malfunction by revving the engine or overriding safety limits.

When to stop operating

Stop work and obtain qualified service if attachments drift unpredictably, fail to remain supported, move without a control command, leak high-pressure fluid, or produce abnormal noises and warning messages. Never check a suspected pinhole leak with your skin. Pressurized fluid injection can cause severe injury even when the opening is barely visible.

Safe information to gather before contacting a technician

  • Exact machine and loader model, serial number and installed hydraulic options
  • Ambient temperature and whether the behavior changes after an approved warm-up
  • Which functions are slow: loader boom, bucket curl, rear hitch or external attachment
  • Recent fluid/filter changes, visible leaks and any fault or temperature warning
  • Any unusual noises, fluid appearance or recent attachment installation

If the machine also behaves poorly when hot, the diagnosis may involve additional testing for pressure, leakage, pump or valve condition. These tests require the correct pressure range and equipment; do not improvise them.

Official sources

John Deere operator-manual troubleshooting table, which lists oil temperature among potential hydraulic performance factors; John Deere Hy-Gard hydraulic/transmission fluid reference; and Kubota USA daily maintenance checks. Checked November 23, 2026. This guide summarizes general issues, not a specific tractor's diagnostic certification.

records.title: John Deere 1M 25 vs 1025R: Specs and Attachment Questions
records.excerpt: Deere lists 24 engine HP, 18 PTO HP, 6.3 gpm pump and 1,556-lb base weights for both 1M 25 and 1025R; learn what those matching numbers do not establish.
records.content:
Two current US John Deere product pages display remarkably similar top-line figures for the 1M 25 and 1025R: 24 rated engine horsepower, 18 PTO horsepower, a two-range hydrostatic transmission, a limited Category 1 hitch, 6.3 US gpm pump output and a published base machine weight of 1,556 lb. These similarities make a side-by-side evaluation worthwhile. They do not, by themselves, prove that the tractors use every identical part, implement mount, control or production option.

What do the factory specification pages actually agree on?

US factory listingJohn Deere 1M 25John Deere 1025R
Engine modelYanmar 3TNV80F-NCJTYanmar 3TNV80F-NCJT
Rated engine horsepower24 hp (SAE J1995)24 hp (SAE J1995)
Rated PTO horsepower18 hp18 hp
TransmissionHydrostatic, two rangesHydrostatic, two ranges
Hitch designationLimited Category 1Limited Category 1
Published hydraulic pump output6.3 US gpm6.3 US gpm
Base machine weight1,556 lb1,556 lb

These are the manufacturer-provided figures from the cited US pages, checked November 23, 2026. They are published ratings, not independently measured field test results. Model options and specification revisions may change.

Does this mean they are identical tractors?

No. Similar powertrain and category numbers are an incomplete basis for declaring full machine interchangeability. A tractor may have different model identifiers, factory accessory packages, loader brackets, mower-deck mounts, electrical harness options, decals, controls or serial-specific replacements. Only the OEM parts catalogue, attachment compatibility chart and machine serial can establish exact fitment.

Do not order a 1025R loader, mower gearbox or engine service kit for a 1M 25 just because the engine model and advertised PTO horsepower match. Confirm the factory part number, mounting hardware and applicable serial range through the current manufacturer system.

What is the practical PTO difference?

Within the values displayed in the current US listings, there is no stated rated PTO horsepower difference — both list 18 hp. It would be misleading to claim the 1M 25 is stronger or weaker on PTO solely because one model name is newer or appears alongside different promotional offers. The implement's minimum required PTO horsepower and compatible shaft speed still need checking in the exact attachment manual.

Are the hydraulics directly comparable?

Both source pages report 6.3 US gpm rated pump output. That is a pump rating, not a guarantee of identical cylinder speeds, loader lift or auxiliary port flow. Installed valve design, loader dimensions, pressure setting, hose routing and attachment weight can affect the usefulness of a hydraulic system. To compare loader work, ask Deere for loader-specific capacities at the same defined measuring point and configuration.

Could transport weight be identical?

The two factory pages list a 1,556-lb base machine weight, but the actual operating machines could be equipped differently. Fuel, tire type, wheel weights, liquid ballast, mower, front loader, backhoe and counterweight all change transport mass. Verify the complete equipped weight for trailer selection; don't calculate a safety margin from the base figure alone.

How to choose between an actual dealer quote

  1. Request a full list of installed equipment and the complete model/serial information for each quote.
  2. Compare the mower, loader and three-point equipment you actually need, including hardware and hydraulic options.
  3. Check service availability, current warranty, potential parts substitutions and operator controls.
  4. Test the machines safely with a demonstrator and compare maneuvering around your property.
  5. Ask for total out-the-door costs including ballast, attachments, delivery and documented support rather than comparing just the tractor-only advertised price.

Official references

John Deere 1M 25 US product specifications and John Deere 1025R US product specifications. Data checked November 23, 2026. See our individual 1M 25 record and 1025R record for ownership context and the comparison tool for their recorded figures.

records.title: Used Compact Tractor Inspection Checklist: 20 Things to Check
records.excerpt: Before buying a used tractor in the US, check the complete serial, tires, leaks, safety systems, loader mounts, PTO, service records, hours and attachment compatibility. Printable-style checklist.
records.content:
A used compact tractor can be a good way to obtain a loader, mower and other useful equipment without buying every component new. But the question is not whether it looks freshly washed. The real questions are whether it is the correct machine for your jobs, whether its condition is understood, whether safety systems function and whether repair and replacement parts can be identified by the complete model and serial number.

John Deere's Certified Used equipment program describes an inspection process that includes operating checks, machine systems, hydraulic cycle and performance checks. That program is not a checklist for every secondhand compact tractor, but it offers a useful reminder that a serious inspection goes beyond paint, hours and a seller's description. Kubota's owner maintenance checklist likewise stresses leaks, tires, fluid condition and safety controls.

20 checks before you agree to buy

#Inspection itemWhat to establish
1Complete model and serialFactory identification matches the listing, paperwork and applicable manuals
2Hour meterDisplayed hours, any history of meter replacement, and records that support usage
3Service recordsDates, hour readings, documented fluids, filters and maintenance gaps
4Engine startupCorrect cold-start behavior observed safely and without smoke or warning concerns
5Engine warningsNo unexplained oil-pressure, coolant or controller alerts
6Visible fluid leaksEngine, transmission, axle and hydraulic areas inspected for fresh leaks
7Cooling screensRadiator and grille clear of heavy chaff, packed dust or bent fins
8Fuel conditionCorrect fuel, visible water-separator problems or contamination history
9Tire conditionCracks, uneven wear, tire type, pressures and ballast arrangements
10Wheels and fastenersRim condition, visible damage and proper wheel hardware check in the manual
11BrakesService and parking brakes tested under appropriate safe conditions
12Steering and travelUnusual play, hesitations, leaks or abnormal transmission operation
13Safety interlocksOperator-presence, PTO and starting interlocks work as the manual states
14ROPS and seat beltStructure and restraint present, not visibly modified or damaged
15Three-point hitchLower arms, pins, stabilizers, controls and lift response inspected
16PTO systemCorrect shaft, guarding, engagement and attachment requirements
17Loader frameMounts, welds, pins, cylinders and any signs of poor repairs or distortion
18Hydraulic hosesVisible abrasion, deterioration, leaks and correct hose/coupler configuration
19Included implementsExact mower, loader or backhoe models, mount compatibility and accessory completeness
20Manuals and supportCorrect operator/parts manuals, dealer access and a current quote for major wear items

What can you check without operating the machine?

Start with the model plate, visible hours, paperwork, tire and wheel condition, obvious leaks, broken guards and attachment identification. Verify the seller's claims about service in written records. If a machine has been repainted, ask what prompted the work; refinishing alone neither proves nor disproves a defect.

A cold start can reveal conditions that are hidden when a machine is presented already warmed up, but it should be attempted only with the seller's permission and according to the manual's safety instructions. Do not try an unfamiliar transmission or loader control on a slope or near bystanders.

Hydraulics and loader: what a short test cannot prove

A loader that moves a bucket during a demonstration is not proof of certified capacity, long-term reliability or adequate hydraulic pressure. Real loader ratings depend on the exact loader model, height, distance from pivot pins, attachment and ballast. Check for hose abrasion, visible seal leakage, damaged loader mounting brackets and abnormal operation. A professional inspection may include hydraulic pressure, pump flow and cycle-time measurements using manufacturer-prescribed test equipment.

Never use your hand to look for hydraulic pinhole leaks or work underneath unsupported raised implements. If something appears unsafe, stop the inspection and request a qualified technician.

Serial-specific parts and surprises

The same tractor model may use different replacement parts in different serial ranges. For example, the John Deere 1025R filter-kit reference shows why the serial number matters even for routine maintenance. Before buying, confirm that the engine, filters, transmission parts and major implements can be identified from the OEM documentation, and obtain current dealer estimates for expensive wear components.

What the hour meter does not tell you

Low hours do not necessarily mean light use; an infrequently maintained machine can have serious problems. High hours alone do not prove poor condition if inspection and maintenance records are strong. Consider how the tractor was used: mower work, frequent loader cycles, rental use, dusty environments, storage conditions and previous repairs. Look for consistency between the seller's description, records and observed wear.

Budget beyond the advertised price

Include any necessary service, tires, fluids, filters, safety repairs, ballast, attachment mounts, transport and dealer support. For an unknown-condition tractor, an independent pre-purchase inspection by a qualified technician may be more valuable than guessing repair costs from classified ads. Do not rely on a single generic resale formula when the equipment package and condition differ.

Useful owner resources

Our manufacturer-sourced equipment directory can help identify the model and published specifications. Read the pre-season maintenance checklist and hydraulic-flow explainer to better understand what must be verified. Use the correct operator manual and local rules for operating the actual machine.

Sources and scope

Inspection categories were informed by John Deere Certified Used Equipment inspection and testing descriptions and Kubota USA daily maintenance checkpoints. Checked November 23, 2026. This is an independent buyer's checklist, not a claim that the tractor has passed an OEM inspection or that the checklist replaces professional service.

records.title: John Deere 3025E Specs (2026): 24.7 HP Engine & 19.4 PTO HP
records.excerpt: US John Deere 3025E 2026 official factory spec: 24.7 gross engine HP, 19.4 PTO HP, 4WD HST, 540-rpm rear PTO and 5.3 US gpm implement pump output. Older 3025E editions differ.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: Deere US factory configuration 1355LV dated 5 April 2026, 24.7 gross HP (SAE J1995) @ 2,500 rpm and 19.4 PTO HP. 4WD HST two ranges, 540-rpm rear PTO. Pump ratings: 5.3 gpm implement, 4.0 gpm steering, 9.3 gpm total (NOT guaranteed remote output). A Deere dealer lists 1,356 lb rear hitch lift at 24 in, but dealer pages may refer to earlier production. Earlier Deere publications list other engine/PTO ratings for 3025E: verify exact year and serial before using specs or ordering attachments.

records.content:
The John Deere 3025E is a 4WD compact utility tractor for mowing, grading, landscaping and property maintenance. Deere's April 2026 US factory equipment listing, code 1355LV, specifies 24.7 gross engine hp (SAE J1995) and 19.4 PTO hp. These values refer to that dated US configuration; earlier 3025E publications and some dealer pages show different ratings. Do not equate gross engine power with usable power at a mower or tiller.

3025E engine and horsepower ratings

The Deere April 2026 specification identifies a Yanmar three-cylinder liquid-cooled Tier 4 diesel with 1.642 L displacement. Engine power is listed as 24.7 gross hp at 2,500 rpm. Other 3025E engine or PTO figures seen online may describe earlier production years. For a used machine, check the exact serial and correct manual before selecting attachments.

The Deere table lists a 19.4 hp PTO rating. For a rotary cutter, tiller, snowblower or other shaft-driven implement, find the maker's approved PTO horsepower range and rear shaft speed instead of sizing it from gross engine power. See our engine-versus-PTO horsepower guide.

Hydrostatic transmission and four-wheel drive

The 3025E is equipped with four-wheel drive and a hydrostatic transmission in the current US 3E configuration. Hydrostatic travel pedals allow varying ground speed within an appropriate drive range. That can be convenient for repeated forward/reverse movement during front-loader work, but tractor stability, ballast and tire selection still determine safe handling. Follow the owner's manual for operating ranges and cold-weather use.

Category 1 hitch and published lift capacity

John Deere's 3025E dealer specification lists a Category 1 three-point hitch and a 1,356-lb capacity at 24 inches behind the link arms. That location is important because a hitch rating measured directly at the lift points can be substantially higher and is not directly comparable. This figure is not a promise that every rear attachment weighing less than 1,356 lb will be safe: load position, ballast and hitch geometry remain critical. For a practical explanation, read how three-point lift positions change ratings.

Hydraulic pump flow: steering versus implements

The detailed Deere dealer record separates 4.0 US gpm steering and 5.3 US gpm implement hydraulics. A combined total of 9.3 gpm is not the same as guaranteed available flow through one auxiliary valve. If an attachment requires a continuous-flow hydraulic motor, confirm the actual remote-circuit capacity, pressure, case-drain needs and couplers before purchasing. Read the hydraulic flow guide for the distinction.

Is the 3025E suitable for a small farm?

It depends on the jobs. The compact dimensions and hydrostatic controls may suit property maintenance and loader tasks, while the published 19.4 PTO hp places an upper constraint on the size of some driven implements. Compare the requirements of each intended mower, chipper or tiller before selecting a tractor. For heavier PTO work, the John Deere 3032E offers a higher published PTO power rating, but it may not automatically be a better fit in limited space.

Buying a used 3025E: verify these details

  • Check the complete machine model and serial number, matching Deere parts catalog and operator manual.
  • Verify the installed loader and bucket/mower/quick-hitch interface rather than assuming interchangeable 3E mounts.
  • Inspect documented service history, transmission behavior, engine warnings, radiator screens and high-pressure hose condition.
  • Confirm the actual transport mass including tires, ballast, loader, implements and any optional equipment.
  • Do not substitute parts based solely on another 3E model with the same engine family or PTO speed.

Original manufacturer references

Primary model/year reference: John Deere USA 3025E factory specifications, April 2026 (1355LV). A separately dated Deere dealer specification supplies the hitch rating at 24 inches and may describe a different edition. Checked 2026-11-23; verify exact production year before relying on older figures.

Source-edition note: Source figures shown on this page follow the 2026 Deere US factory option list. Older model-year brochures and individual dealer listings can state different ratings; always match the complete tractor identification before selecting PTO attachments, hydraulics or service components.

records.title: John Deere 3032E Specs (2026): 31.1 HP, 25 PTO HP & Hitch
records.excerpt: US John Deere 3032E 2026 factory configuration: 31.1 gross engine HP, 25 PTO HP, 4WD HST, 540-rpm rear PTO and 5.3 gpm implement-pump output.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: John Deere US factory spec 1475LV dated 5 May 2026: 31.1 gross engine hp SAE J1995 and 25.0 PTO hp. 4WD HST with two ranges, independent rear 540-rpm PTO. 5.3 gpm implement + 4.0 gpm steering = 9.3 gpm total pump rating, not guaranteed remote flow. Earlier Deere dealer data displays 31.2 hp gross and a rear hitch lift of 1,356 lb at 24 in; separate published revisions/configurations must not be silently mixed.

records.content:
The John Deere 3032E is a compact tractor for property maintenance and small-farm work. Deere's May 2026 US factory listing, code 1475LV, specifies 31.1 gross engine hp (SAE J1995) and 25 PTO hp. Earlier dealer tables sometimes show a 31.2-hp gross rating, so comparing equipment requires attention to the source edition and the machine's serial number.

Engine and rated output

Deere's May 2026 US factory specification identifies a Yanmar liquid-cooled Tier 4 diesel with 1.642 L displacement, 31.1 gross engine horsepower and a rated speed of 2,500 rpm. Do not mix this configuration's engine rating with older dealer figures unless the model year and rating method are aligned.

25 PTO horsepower

The manufacturer lists 25 hp at the rear power take-off, compared with 19.4 hp for the 3025E in the same Deere 3E specification set. This difference may matter when a rotary cutter, tiller or other implement has a minimum PTO horsepower requirement close to the lower model's available rating. An implement's gearbox rating, connection, shaft speed, hitch weight and guarding still must all match.

Deere lists a 540-rpm rear PTO in its 3E configurations. The PTO operating speed is not the same as engine RPM. Consult the operator manual for the correct engagement procedure and required shielding.

Four-wheel-drive hydrostatic transmission

The 3032E uses four-wheel drive and a hydrostatic transmission. This can suit work where speed must change frequently, such as loader cycles or maneuvering around buildings. It does not establish safe loader lift or towing ability; tire choice, ballast, working surface and the specific loader's tested geometry remain decisive.

Hitch specification and practical limits

Deere's product information identifies a Category 1 three-point hitch. Its dealer technical specifications report 1,356 lb lift capacity at 24 inches behind the lower lift arms. This figure uses a specified measuring point: it is not necessarily comparable with an advertised lift-point maximum in another brand's brochure. A long rear implement can place its center of mass well behind the hitch, affecting stability and available capacity.

Separate hydraulic pump outputs

The Deere dealer specification lists 4.0 US gpm for steering and 5.3 US gpm for implement hydraulics. It would be misleading to combine them and claim that every auxiliary coupler supplies their sum. If a hydraulic brush cutter, grapple or other accessory is being considered, confirm flow, pressure, return line and hydraulic control requirements at the exact installed valve.

How does 3032E compare with 3025E?

Manufacturer 3E rating3025E3032E
Gross engine power24.7 hp31.1 hp
PTO horsepower19.4 hp25.0 hp
TransmissionHST, 4WDHST, 4WD
Three-point hitchCategory 1Category 1

Horsepower is not the complete buying decision. Ask for the exact loader lift ratings at a common measured position, tractor mass with ballast and loaded tires, and the manufacturer-approved implement fitment for the intended work. See our comparison tool and used-tractor inspection checklist.

Primary sources

Primary model/year reference: John Deere May 2026 US factory 3032E listing (1475LV). A separately dated John Deere dealer specification documents hitch lift at 24 inches and may describe an earlier model configuration. Source checked 2026-11-23.

Source-edition note: Source figures shown on this page follow the 2026 Deere US factory option list. Older model-year brochures and individual dealer listings can state different ratings; always match the complete tractor identification before selecting PTO attachments, hydraulics or service components.

records.title: John Deere BXX10240 3rd Function Kit: 3E Tractors MY22 and Older
records.serial_scope: Deere lists BXX10240 as generally applicable to MY22 and older 3E tractors, including 3025E, 3032E and 3038E. Confirm year, 300E loader, existing controls and official serial-specific fitment.
records.excerpt: OEM John Deere BXX10240 third-function SCV reference for certain 3E tractors through model year 2022. Not a guaranteed fit; verify tractor, loader and valve configuration.
records.content:
John Deere BXX10240 is an original third-function selective control valve (SCV) attachment.
