Deere's US parts listing describes it for model year 2022 and older 3E-series tractors, with the 3025E, 3032E and 3038E named in the compatibility information. It is intended to add a set of mid-mount hydraulic couplers so compatible loader attachments can use an additional hydraulic function.

Which tractors does Deere list?

Manufacturer familyPublished applicability
John Deere 3EMY22 and older, subject to the exact factory configuration
Named models3025E, 3032E and 3038E in the product description
Also shown in general equipment list300E loader and additional equipment; an equipment-name listing alone is not proof of fit
MY23 or later 3EDo not assume BXX10240 fits; see BXX10808 reference

John Deere labels compatible equipment as general fit. For a purchase, verify complete tractor serial, exact loader and control valve, hydraulic connections, existing options and dealer parts information.

What a third-function valve does

A standard loader joystick often commands boom rise/lower and bucket curl/dump. A third-function hydraulic circuit can control an additional attachment movement, such as opening and closing a compatible grapple. The hydraulic motor or cylinder on the implement still requires its own permitted flow, pressure, valve arrangement, hoses and couplers. Adding a kit does not increase the machine's certified loader lift or rated pump output.

Why “MY22 or older” matters

Deere's product notes distinguish third-function kits for different 3E model-year generations. That means a 3025E model badge is not enough to order a valve. Check the tractor's complete serial/model information against the official catalogue, and determine whether the loader, joystick control, hoses and mounting hardware already include any required components.

Do not simply substitute a kit because another owner posted that it worked on a related model. Factory configurations and aftermarket modifications can differ. An authorized dealer can verify the current official kit and whether a superseded part number applies.

Safe installation and operation

Hydraulic controls should be installed and tested by a qualified person following Deere's kit instructions. Never open or disconnect a pressurized hydraulic line. Lower loader attachments, secure the machine and use the manufacturer-prescribed pressure-release procedure before any inspection or work. High-pressure fluid can penetrate skin and cause a medical emergency. After installation, check hose routing, secure couplers and guarding before using attachments.

How to check a used tractor

  1. Record the full tractor model/year and serial from the factory plate.
  2. Identify the installed loader, attachment carrier and joystick-control configuration.
  3. Check the Deere BXX10240 part listing for current applicability and any supersession.
  4. Confirm the attachment maker's flow and pressure requirements against the actual tractor circuit.
  5. Obtain the proper kit installation instructions; do not treat this reference as an assembly guide.

Original source

John Deere US original BXX10240 Third Function Selective Control Valve Attachment, checked November 23, 2026. For more recent 3E model years, compare Deere BXX10808. This is an independent parts reference, not a compatibility guarantee.

records.title: John Deere BXX10808 3rd Function Valve: 3E MY23 and Newer
records.serial_scope: Deere lists BXX10808 for MY23 and newer 3E compact tractors. Verify the 3025E/3032E/3038E model year, actual loader and hydraulic control configuration and current serial-specific parts catalogue.
records.excerpt: John Deere BXX10808 third-function SCV kit is listed for MY23 and newer 3E tractors. Read fitment limits and official source before ordering loader hydraulics.
records.content:
The original John Deere BXX10808 is a third-function selective control valve kit that Deere's US store describes for model year 2023 and newer 3E compact tractors. This source-defined cutover makes it different from BXX10240, which Deere associates with earlier production years. Both are hydraulic accessory references rather than proof of universal fitment.

Model-year applicability

John Deere describes the BXX10808 as a third-function SCV attachment designed for MY23-and-newer 3E tractors. The 3E family includes familiar compact models such as the 3025E, 3032E and 3038E. The manufacturer's general compatibility list does not remove the need to verify the complete model and serial number or loader-specific plumbing.

CheckWhy it matters
MY23 or newer 3E productionDeere states this model-year scope for BXX10808
Actual tractor serial and marketProduction changes and supersessions may affect installation
Loader model and installed controlsSome machines already include additional SCVs or different joysticks
Grapple or other attachment requirementsMatch permitted flow, pressure and hydraulic connection type
Factory installation instructionsHydraulic repairs and adjustments are safety-critical

What does BXX10808 add?

It provides an extra hydraulic function for compatible attachments that need an additional movement beyond loader boom and bucket tilt. Depending on the implement, that could be an open/close grapple control. This does not automatically add lifting capacity, change a loader's structural rating or make an attachment safe without ballast.

What about BXX10240?

Deere lists BXX10240 for MY22 and older 3E tractors. The two manufacturer-listed year scopes are a guide for the initial lookup, but they are not a substitute for current fitment validation. Do not assume the two kits can be used interchangeably or that every machine of the same model name shares identical hydraulic equipment.

Hydraulic safety before inspection

A high-pressure hydraulic system may retain stored energy after the engine is stopped. Never loosen couplers or hoses to “test whether there is pressure.” Lower attached equipment, secure the tractor and follow Deere's approved pressure-release instructions. Only qualified technicians with the proper kit documentation and diagnostic equipment should install or modify the valve circuit. Hydraulic fluid injection can cause severe injury and requires emergency treatment.

Before ordering

  1. Identify the complete model, machine serial and production year.
  2. List the loader and all existing hydraulic valve or joystick options.
  3. Confirm the current official Deere BXX10808 fitment and any part-number supersession.
  4. Confirm third-function circuit compatibility with the intended implement.
  5. Obtain a complete installed-price quote and factory kit instructions from an authorized dealer.

Official source

John Deere original BXX10808 third-function SCV kit, checked November 23, 2026. This page is an independent informational summary. Its general model-year notes do not guarantee safe fit on an individual tractor.

records.title: John Deere 3025E vs 3032E (2026): PTO HP, Hydraulics and Hitch
records.excerpt: Compare Deere 3025E and 3032E using dated 2026 factory specs: 24.7 vs 31.1 engine hp, 19.4 vs 25 PTO hp, and the same listed 5.3 gpm implement pump.
records.content:
Should you choose the John Deere 3025E or 3032E for a small farm, wooded property, landscaping or loader chores? The meaningful distinction is the manufacturer's documented power and the requirements of your actual implement. Using Deere's dated 2026 US factory listings, the 3025E provides 24.7 gross engine hp and 19.4 PTO hp, while the 3032E lists 31.1 gross engine hp and 25 PTO hp. Both offer 4WD hydrostatic travel and a published implement-pump rating of 5.3 US gpm.

2026 Deere 3E specifications compared

Specification (US factory configuration)3025E (1355LV)3032E (1475LV)
Gross engine hp, SAE J199524.731.1
PTO horsepower19.425.0
Transmission4WD, 2-range HST4WD, 2-range HST
Rear PTOIndependent, 540 rpmIndependent, 540 rpm
Steering pump4.0 US gpm4.0 US gpm
Implement pump5.3 US gpm5.3 US gpm
Deere's summed total pump rating9.3 US gpm9.3 US gpm
Rear three-point hitchCategory 1 (dealer specification)Category 1 (dealer specification)

The core engine, PTO, transmission and pump figures come from Deere's April 2026 3025E factory option listing and May 2026 3032E listing. The 24-inch hitch lift values sometimes quoted by dealers are from separately dated documents. Do not silently combine model revisions.

How much extra PTO horsepower do you get?

In the cited factory data, the 3032E has 5.6 more PTO horsepower than the 3025E (25.0 vs 19.4). That difference could determine whether a rotary cutter, snowblower or other driven implement meets its maker's minimum required PTO rating. It does not establish a universal maximum mower width. Vegetation density, working speed, PTO gearbox requirements, terrain and cutting height all affect whether the tractor-implement combination is appropriate.

Does a higher-powered 3032E lift more?

You cannot derive loader capacity from engine horsepower. The 3E tractors can be paired with Deere's 300E loader, but the loader's published ratings depend on loader version and measurement location. Deere reports 1,186 lb at the pivot pins at full height and 845 lb at 500 mm forward for the referenced non-self-leveling setup. A mechanical-self-leveling loader variant may differ, and rated capacity does not erase the need for correct rear ballast, safe ground conditions or stable positioning.

Both 3E tractors have a Category 1 rear hitch in dealer data. A quoted 1,356-lb lift capacity 24 inches behind the arms is a hitch rating at a specific load point, not a loader rating and not a safe limit for every rear implement. Check the exact manual, attachment center of mass and ballast requirements before deciding on heavy rear equipment.

What if hydraulic speed is your main concern?

Both Deere factory configurations list the same 5.3 US gpm implement pump rating and a separate 4.0 gpm steering pump. Adding them to 9.3 gpm does not mean 9.3 gpm flows through an auxiliary hose. A hydraulic motor, third-function grapple or rear remote requires the actual circuit's supported flow, pressure, return path and controls.

For 3E-series hydraulic attachments, the model year matters: Deere associates third-function SCV BXX10240 with MY22 and older and BXX10808 with MY23 and newer. These are starting references, not guarantees of fit on a particular serial or loader combination.

Which model makes more sense?

If you already have implements whose documented PTO requirements fit the 3025E, the smaller power figure may be sufficient. If your intended attachments require more PTO output, the 3032E's published 25 hp may be useful. But do not buy solely on a horsepower difference: inspect actual equipment condition, dealer service options, tire type, ballast, loader equipment and the complete price of implements.

For individual source notes, see 3025E specifications, 3032E specifications and our interactive comparison tool. Older 3025E/3032E machines may use different component generations and rated horsepower, so compare the year and serial of the actual offer.

Manufacturer references

John Deere US 2026 factory documents for model codes 1355LV and 1475LV, and John Deere 300E loader official specifications. Product notes reviewed November 23, 2026. The correct operator and loader manuals remain authoritative for safety, fitment and service.

records.title: John Deere 300E Loader Lift Capacity: 1,186 vs 845 lb Explained
records.excerpt: Understand Deere 300E non-self-leveling loader ratings: 1,186 lb at the pivot versus 845 lb 500 mm forward at full height, plus ballast and 3E compatibility checks.
records.content:
A John Deere 300E loader may appear to have two different lift capacities: 1,186 lb at the pivot pin and 845 lb at a point 500 mm (about 19.7 inches) forward, both measured at full height in Deere's referenced non-self-leveling loader specifications. The numbers do not contradict one another: the test load is placed at different positions relative to the loader boom. A load farther forward places greater leverage on the loader structure.

300E front loader capacities from the manufacturer

Deere 300E non-self-leveling figurePublished ratingInterpretation
Lift capacity at full height, measured at the pivot pin1,186 lbTest load position is at the bucket pivot
Lift capacity at full height, measured 500 mm ahead of pivot845 lbTest load is placed farther forward, changing leverage
Tractor compatibility list3025E, 3032E, 3038E and specified 3D tractorsModel listing is a starting point, not a complete mount/serial guarantee

These values are taken from the John Deere USA 300E loader technical specification, checked November 23, 2026. They describe the cited non-self-leveling loader configuration, not every 300E loader variant or bucket.

A visual comparison of the two measured load positions

At pivot pins
1,186 lb
500 mm forward
845 lb

The graphic scales the two manufacturer-listed ratings to the larger one. It is not a new certified load test, a safe-lifting calculator or a prediction of a tractor's stability.

Why the forward load position matters

Bucket contents, pallet forks and odd-shaped objects do not necessarily place their full load at the pivot pins. For example, the center of mass of a pallet carried on forks may be noticeably forward of the loader's pins. The farther-forward rating is often more relevant than the maximum at-pivot number, but neither figure replaces the actual attachment-specific data or operating limits.

Do not extrapolate a safe maximum load at an arbitrary distance using a simple percentage. Loader geometry, hydraulic pressure limits, mechanical strength, structural deflection, operating height and the tractor's stability all matter.

Which Deere tractors can use a 300E?

The manufacturer's compatibility listing includes 3025E and 3032E, along with additional specified 3D and 3E models. This should not be interpreted as a blanket guarantee that every serial number, hydraulic control package, mounting frame, hose or quick-carrier variant interchanges. Ask the dealer to validate exact year, loader model and option code.

Non-self-leveling versus mechanical-self-leveling loaders

John Deere also promotes a mechanical-self-leveling (MSL) option for compatible loader families. Loader models or boom options with different self-leveling mechanisms can have different published capacities. Do not apply the two numbers above to a mechanical-self-leveling loader without checking the correct official specification table for that specific option.

What about ballast, front axle and tire loads?

The lift numbers above describe the loader under published conditions, not the entire tractor's certified capacity to transport or hold a particular load safely. Correct rear ballast is essential to control stability, steering and axle loading. Deere's 2026 factory option listings for 3E loaders explicitly call for three-point hitch ballast and reference the tractor ballast requirements. Never lift above the manufacturer’s permitted conditions or use a raised bucket to carry people.

Five checks before buying a grapple or pallet forks

  1. Find the precise 300E loader boom, bucket carrier, tire, mount and tractor model/year combination.
  2. Use the attachment's own weight and load-center information: the attachment itself consumes lift capacity.
  3. Compare at the same height and load position; distinguish pivot-pin and 500-mm ratings.
  4. Confirm hydraulic valve, third-function controls and permitted coupler pressures if the attachment needs extra hydraulic action. For 3E models, Deere lists different kits for MY22 and earlier versus MY23 and later.
  5. Verify ballast, tire/axle ratings and the manufacturer's safe operation instructions for the machine and implement.

Sources and limitations

Primary technical reference: John Deere 300E front-end loader specifications and compatible tractors. Cross-check Deere's 2026 3025E and 3032E factory documents for the installed configuration. Reviewed November 23, 2026. This guide cannot certify an individual tractor/loader/attachment combination.

records.title: KIOTI CK3520 Specs: 34.9 HP Gear Tractor, PTO & Weight
records.excerpt: Official KIOTI CK3520 manual transmission specifications: 34.9 engine hp, 30.9 PTO hp, 12 forward/12 reverse speeds, 11.7 gpm pump, Category 1 hitch and 2,678 lb published weight.

specs.fms_configuration_notes: US KIOTI CK3520 MANUAL transmission: 12 forward/12 reverse, dry dual-stage clutch. Manufacturer lists rear hitch lift 1,631 lb without identifying a comparable 24-inch load location, so no 24-inch field populated. 11.7 gpm published pump capacity is not a verified auxiliary remote flow. 2,678 lb listed weight depends on tire and equipment configuration.

records.content:
The KIOTI CK3520 is a compact tractor with a 12-forward/12-reverse mechanical transmission. KIOTI's US technical page gives a 34.9-hp diesel engine and 30.9 PTO horsepower. It is important to distinguish this gear-drive model from the CK3520H: the hydrostatic version is rated at a different PTO power and published tractor weight, even though its engine rating is the same.

Engine and driveline

KIOTI names the 3H-TM4A diesel, with 1,826 cc of displacement and rated power of 34.90 hp at 2,600 engine rpm. The fuel tank is listed as 9 US gal. Fuel capacity describes the tank, not guaranteed hours of operation or gallons consumed per acre.

Manual transmission and PTO

The manufacturer describes a manual 12F/12R transmission and a dry dual-stage clutch for the CK3520. The rear PTO is 540 rpm, and a 2,000-rpm mid PTO is optional. Reported rear PTO output is 30.9 hp. Confirm the implement maker's PTO horsepower range, shaft speed, guarding and driveline geometry; the engine's 34.9 hp is not the same rating.

Hydraulic pump and hitch

The manufacturer lists a gear-type pump with 11.7 US gpm published pump capacity, plus a Category 1 three-point hitch with position control and a 1,631-lb manufacturer lift rating. The source does not define that hitch value as measured 24 inches behind the lift points. Therefore, our standardized 24-inch comparison field is intentionally empty. Do not interpret 11.7 gpm as guaranteed continuous flow through an accessory coupler.

Loader, backhoe, tire fluid and ballast change actual equipment and transport weight. Do not base a trailer or axle-load decision on the tractor-only number.

CK3520 or CK3520H?

The gear model publishes 30.9 PTO hp while the CK3520H hydrostatic version publishes 28.9 PTO hp. The comparison is based on separate official model pages, not an assumption about generic HST loss. The manual version may appeal to owners who prefer fixed gear ratios; the HST version may be convenient for frequent directional changes. Test the actual controls and match your heaviest implement to the correct PTO specification.

Before buying

Check the complete serial and the correct operator's manual; identify the loader model, tires and ballast; verify the hydraulic circuit used by your attachment; and compare local dealer service and the all-in equipment quote. Both are sold with a published 34.9-hp KIOTI diesel engine, but the CK3520H's listed PTO power is 28.9 hp, compared with 30.9 hp for the gear-drive model. That distinction can matter for PTO-powered implements operating near a manufacturer's minimum recommended power.

Engine and HST drivetrain

PTO horsepower

KIOTI specifies 28.9 PTO hp, a 540-rpm rear PTO and an optional 2,000-rpm mid PTO. Do not size a rotary cutter, snowblower, tiller or chipper using gross engine power alone. Verify the implement's shaft speed, gearbox requirements, tractor PTO rating, driveline length and safety guards. See engine hp versus PTO hp.

Hydraulics and three-point hitch

When is hydrostatic drive useful?

For repeated forward/reverse movement in loader work or detailed positioning around fences and buildings, an HST control layout may be convenient. Fixed gear selection may be preferred for other work. Neither transmission choice replaces safe operation, proper ballast or model-specific attachment compatibility. records.content:
The Massey Ferguson GC1723E is a sub-compact tractor listed in the manufacturer's US equipment comparison table with 22.5 engine horsepower and 18.3 PTO horsepower. The same official table provides an unusually useful matched set of figures: implement hydraulic flow, three-point lift measured 24 inches behind the hitch and base tractor weight. This makes it easier to compare like measurements, but the real equipment package still matters.

Engine horsepower versus PTO horsepower

Massey Ferguson publishes 22.5 engine hp and 18.3 PTO hp for the GC1723E in the US sub-compact category table. Engine hp is not the same rating as PTO hp. A mower, snowblower or tiller must be compatible with the specific available PTO output, shaft speed and attachment geometry. The official comparison table does not identify the engine model or PTO rpm, so our database does not guess those details.

Transmission and implement flow

The GC1723E uses a two-range hydrostatic transmission. Massey Ferguson calls its listed 6.3 US gpm specifically implement hydraulic flow. That description is more precise than an unspecified total-pump number, but it still does not prove a particular hydraulic coupler can support every attachment's continuous flow, pressure and return requirements. For hydraulic tools, verify the installed circuit and the implement manual.

Rear lift capacity at a stated location

The official US table lists 661 lb measured 24 inches behind the rear hitch lift points. This should not be compared directly with another tractor's at-the-hitch-pin maximum, which is measured at a different distance. The actual attachment's center of mass, ballast and tractor stability also matter. Read our lift-capacity measurement guide.

Published base weight

Massey Ferguson lists 1,466 lb base weight. A mower deck, loader, backhoe, filled tires, rear counterweight, fuel and implements change the real weight you haul or operate. Do not select a trailer based on 1,466 lb alone; confirm the complete equipment and transport configuration.

For a higher-power alternative, Massey Ferguson lists the GC1725M with 24.5 engine hp and 18.5 PTO hp, along with slightly higher implement flow in the same official table. For buying decisions, compare compatible mower and loader packages, local parts support and total delivered price rather than engine ratings alone.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson GC1725M is a sub-compact tractor that the manufacturer's US specification table lists at 24.5 engine horsepower and 18.5 PTO horsepower. It shares a two-range hydrostatic drivetrain category and the published 661-lb 24-inch-behind hitch lift rating with the GC1723E. The GC1725M has a different engine rating and a higher listed implement hydraulic flow.

Engine and PTO values

Massey Ferguson publishes 24.5 engine hp and 18.5 PTO hp. These numbers should not be combined with an older brochure's engine displacement or PTO speed if that document describes a different production edition. The current comparison table does not identify the exact engine model, so we intentionally leave that detail to the serial-specific operator manual.

Hydrostatic drive

The official listing identifies a two-range HST transmission. Hydrostatic drive can make frequent forward/reverse positioning convenient for loader and landscaping work. The tractor's tire selection, ballast, actual attachment mass and ground conditions remain critical to stable operation. HST does not independently establish loader capacity or maximum safe grade.

Hydraulic implement flow

The US model table lists 6.9 US gpm implement hydraulic flow for the GC1725M. That is higher than the 6.3 gpm stated for the GC1723E. The manufacturer describes the numbers as implement flow, not a simple sum of steering and main pumps, but the actual installed remote circuit, pressure and valve requirements still need confirmation for a powered grapple or other attachment.

Three-point hitch at 24 inches behind

The published rear lift rating is 661 lb at 24 inches behind the hitch. A load mounted farther rearward can create additional leverage; safe lifting and transport are governed by stability, geometry and ballast as well as hydraulic power. The 24-inch reference location makes the value useful for comparisons with similarly labeled figures, but it does not certify every attachment weighing less than the number.

Weight and handling

The factory table shows a 1,477-lb base weight. A front loader, deck, backhoe, wheel weights, loaded tires or ballast will change the real mass, axle loads and transport needs. Avoid using the bare tractor number to select a towing vehicle, trailer or tie-down equipment.

Which Massey Ferguson sub-compact is better?

The GC1723E offers 22.5 engine hp and 18.3 PTO hp. The GC1725M's extra 2 engine hp amounts to only 0.2 more published PTO hp in the manufacturer's table. That does not automatically justify higher cost for every property owner. Consider the actual implements, hydraulics, mower package, dealer support and total equipment condition. See the direct GC1723E versus GC1725M guide.

records.content:
Two KIOTI CK-series tractors can have the same advertised 34.9 engine horsepower yet differ in everyday operation and available PTO output. The CK3520 uses a 12-forward/12-reverse gear transmission; the CK3520H uses a three-range hydrostatic transmission. KIOTI's own US product pages report 30.9 PTO hp for the manual version versus 28.9 hp for the HST model.

Official CK3520 versus CK3520H specs

Engine power34.9 hp34.9 hp

Transmission12F/12R manualThree-range HST

Both columns come from KIOTI's individual US product pages checked November 23, 2026. The weights are not guaranteed transport masses after loader, ballast, tire liquid, backhoe or other installed equipment is added.

Is the manual tractor more powerful?

The engine power is the same in both manufacturer tables. The documented 2.0-hp PTO difference matters for implements that need a particular minimum PTO rating. It does not mean the manual tractor has more rated hydraulic pump capacity or guaranteed loader lift. Work rate, soil conditions, traction and operator technique also influence results.

If your attachment needs at least 30 PTO horsepower, the CK3520 gear-drive listing is above that threshold and the CK3520H listing is below it. That observation is not a compatibility recommendation by itself: shaft speed, implement mass, driveline geometry and the implement maker's approved model list must also be checked.

Hydrostatic control versus 12F/12R gearing

A gear-drive tractor provides discrete ratios. That may suit an owner comfortable with manual selection for repeatable field tasks, although actual clutch and shift procedures must follow the CK3520 manual. The CK3520H varies ground speed within three HST ranges, a potentially useful arrangement for loader cycles, landscaping or maneuvering around buildings. Neither system automatically determines safe operation on a slope or trailer weight.

Do they lift the same at the rear hitch?

KIOTI lists 1,631 lb for the rear hitch of both models. The US pages do not state that this is a rating measured 24 inches behind the lift points, so you should not compare it directly with a Kubota or Massey Ferguson 24-inch measurement without matching test positions. Learn why measurement locations matter in our three-point hitch rating guide.

Loader and hydraulic equipment

The same published 11.7 US gpm pump capacity does not establish actual flow at a particular loader valve or auxiliary remote. A grapple or hydraulic implement may require a separate compatible control circuit, flow and pressure rating and approved ballast. Read our hydraulic-flow explainer before comparing third-function options.

What to test at the dealership

  1. Ask for the exact tractor model, year/serial and transmission option on each quote.
  2. Try controlled forward/reverse moves on flat, safe ground with a trained demonstrator.
  3. Match the highest-PTO-demand implement to the actual PTO horsepower specification.
  4. Check loader rating at the same measurement point and lift height for both packages.
  5. Confirm ballast, tires, total operating weight, warranty support and parts availability.

Open the KIOTI CK3520 model reference or the CK3520H HST model reference to see the individual source notes. Our interactive tractor comparison retains only data that can be compared without guessing missing values.

Primary sources

KIOTI USA CK3520 factory specifications and KIOTI USA CK3520H factory specifications. Checked November 23, 2026. Figures may vary with tire and attachment configurations.

records.title: Massey Ferguson GC1723E vs GC1725M: PTO & Lift Capacity
records.excerpt: Massey Ferguson US GC1723E and GC1725M both list 661-lb hitch lift at 24 inches. Compare 22.5 vs 24.5 engine hp, 18.3 vs 18.5 PTO hp and 6.3 vs 6.9 gpm implement hydraulic flow.
records.content:
The Massey Ferguson GC1723E and GC1725M look similar in the manufacturer's US sub-compact tractor table, but their published horsepower and implement hydraulic-flow ratings are not identical. For a buyer, the most important detail may be that an extra 2 engine horsepower on the GC1725M corresponds to only 0.2 more published PTO horsepower in this particular source. If your main goal is a larger PTO-powered mower, that distinction deserves attention.

Official US GC1723E versus GC1725M table

Manufacturer specificationGC1723EGC1725M
Engine power22.5 hp24.5 hp
PTO power18.3 hp18.5 hp
Travel transmission2-range hydrostatic2-range hydrostatic
Implement hydraulic flow6.3 US gpm6.9 US gpm
Rear hitch lift, 24 in behind661 lb661 lb
Published base weight1,466 lb1,477 lb

The table is based on Massey Ferguson's US sub-compact model comparison, checked November 23, 2026. It is a comparison of the named models as presented by the manufacturer, not a measurement we conducted independently.

Why doesn't more engine HP mean much more PTO HP?

Power at the engine and power available at a PTO shaft are measured in different locations in the drivetrain. The GC1725M's 24.5 engine hp compared with 22.5 for the GC1723E may look like a substantial advantage, but the source lists only 18.5 compared with 18.3 hp at the PTO. The distinction means buyers should size driven implements using the stated PTO number and the implement manual, not the hood's engine-power badge.

Hydraulic flow is different

In the same official table, Massey Ferguson specifies 6.9 US gpm of implement hydraulic flow for the GC1725M versus 6.3 gpm for the GC1723E. These figures specifically refer to implement flow rather than an unlabeled combined pump total. But neither value alone establishes the pressure or suitability of a particular remote circuit. For hydraulic motor attachments, check flow and pressure at the actual installed outlet.

Identical 24-inch rear hitch lift rating

Both models list 661 lb at 24 inches behind the lower hitch points. That is a precisely labeled measurement location. Do not mistake it for the maximum lift directly at the hitch-pin centers. A box blade, tiller or ballast box may put its center of mass farther rearward and change stability demands. See our rear hitch measurement explainer.

Weight and actual work configuration

The published base weights are 1,466 and 1,477 lb. That 11-lb difference is not enough information to estimate the total mass of either machine with a front loader, mower deck, liquid-filled tires or backhoe. The actual combination and load distribution must be checked for trailer selection, slope safety and ballast planning.

Which would be the better purchase?

If a matching mower, attachment package and dealership support are available at better terms with the GC1723E, the small PTO power difference may not justify a higher tractor cost. If hydraulic attachment performance and installed options are more important, examine the GC1725M's higher published implement flow alongside actual attachment compatibility and price. Neither tractor is guaranteed suitable for a particular implement based only on the table above.

Used tractor checklist

  1. Confirm the complete model and serial; inspect the correct-year factory manuals.
  2. Identify exactly which loader, mower, attachment carrier and ballast accompany the tractor.
  3. Check the operator's documented maintenance intervals and any serial-specific parts revisions.
  4. Compare engine-hour readings with service records and wear, not just advertised hours.
  5. Obtain local dealer support information and an independent inspection if machine history is uncertain.

Read GC1723E specifications, GC1725M specifications and the used tractor inspection checklist before making a decision.

Original manufacturer source

Massey Ferguson US sub-compact model comparison, checked November 23, 2026. Features and specifications can change; the appropriate serial-specific manual remains authoritative.

The 2026 Kubota L3302 DT 4WD is the gear-drive version of the Standard L compact tractor. The official Kubota 2026 Full Line Brochure specifies 33.0 gross engine horsepower and 28.0 PTO horsepower for its four-wheel-drive DT column. The DT version uses an 8-forward/8-reverse synchronized shuttle, while the L3302 HST version has a three-range hydrostatic drive and a different PTO rating.

Engine horsepower and the PTO difference

The 2026 factory table reports a vertical, direct-injection, water-cooled diesel engine with 111.4 cubic inches of displacement for both L3302 variants. Its 33.0 gross hp rating is stated under SAE J1995; the 28.0 PTO hp figure applies specifically to this gear-drive configuration. Do not select an implement using only gross engine power.

8F/8R synchronized shuttle transmission

Kubota lists eight forward and eight reverse gear ratios for the 2026 L3302 DT 4WD. A synchronized shuttle differs from the infinitely variable ground speed of an HST. This transmission may suit owners who prefer choosing repeatable ratios for field work, while repeated loader reversals may feel different from an HST machine. Test the actual controls and follow the model-specific manual's shift procedure; a synchronized shuttle is not an invitation to change direction unsafely at speed.

Hitch lift rating measured 24 inches behind

The manufacturer's 2026 table specifies an SAE Category I rear hitch and 1,435 lb lift measured 24 inches behind the lift points. This is a defined measurement position rather than a maximum at the lower-link ends. It does not guarantee that any 1,435-lb attachment will be stable or safe. Load center, ballast, terrain and the exact implement manufacturer's instructions still govern. See our hitch rating guide.

The Kubota L3902 DT 4WD is the gear-drive Standard L tractor in the manufacturer's 2026 Full Line Brochure. It has a documented 37.5 gross engine hp and 32.1 PTO hp, with an eight-forward/eight-reverse synchronized shuttle. The HST version uses a three-range hydrostatic drive and lists 30.3 PTO hp in the same 2026 factory table.

37.5 gross hp is not 37.5 PTO hp

Kubota lists a vertical, water-cooled, direct-injection diesel engine with 111.4 cu in displacement, rated at 37.5 gross hp under SAE J1995. Its DT transmission configuration delivers a manufacturer-listed 32.1 hp at the PTO. Use the PTO figure when evaluating PTO-driven implements such as rotary cutters and tillers, along with the specific attachment's shaft, hitch, gearbox and ballast requirements.

Gear-drive transmission

The 2026 L3902 DT has a synchronized-shuttle gearbox with eight forward and eight reverse selections. Gear ratios and shuttle controls produce a different operating experience from the three-range HST option. A prospective owner should consider loader cycles, transport paths, repeated reversing, ground conditions and operator experience, not only the published PTO rating. The correct operator manual defines safe shifting and clutch use.

Hitch lift and hydraulic constraints

The official 2026 data specifies an SAE Category I three-point hitch with 1,435 lb lift capacity at 24 inches behind the lift points. That is a precisely defined location; it cannot be directly compared with another manufacturer's headline capacity taken at the lift pins. This source does not provide a matched auxiliary remote flow figure, so our standardized hydraulic field is blank rather than populated from a different brochure.

A tractor with a loader, bucket, rear counterweight, loaded tires and full fluids will have a different transport mass and balance. The official bare tractor weight is only one input when sizing a tow vehicle, trailer, brakes and tie-down equipment.

Does it lift more than the L3302?

The 2026 brochure uses the same 1,435-lb hitch rating at 24 inches behind for both the L3302 DT and L3902 DT. A stronger engine therefore does not imply a stronger rated three-point hitch. The L3902 DT does provide a higher published PTO power figure (32.1 vs 28.0 hp), which can expand the set of implements whose minimum power requirements it meets.

Front loader and related models

Kubota's Standard L page identifies the LA526 front loader for the L3302 and L3902. Loader ratings vary with lift height and load-center distance and must be checked with installed bucket or forks. Read our LA526 lift measurements guide. For a direct comparison of the DT and HST variants, see gear versus hydrostatic L3302/L3902 specs.

records.title: Kubota LA526 Loader Lift Capacity: 1,144 vs 1,506 lb Explained
records.excerpt: Kubota's Standard L front loader ratings depend on height and tractor: LA526 1,144 lb at maximum height, versus 1,446 or 1,506 lb measured at 1.5 meters. Learn what these numbers mean for buckets and forks.
records.content:
Why does one description of the Kubota LA526 front loader show 1,144 lb, while another says 1,506 lb? These numbers do not refer to an identical operating position. Kubota's US Standard L Series overview lists 1,144 lb at the pivot pin at full height for the LA526, then provides a separate load rating at 1.5 meters lift height that depends on the attached Standard L tractor.

Official LA526 lift figures

Manufacturer configuration and test positionPublished rating

LA526 on L2502, pivot pin 1.5 m above ground1,446 lb
LA526 on L3302 / L3902, pivot pin 1.5 m above ground1,506 lb

Source: Kubota USA Standard L Series — Performance-Matched Front Loader, checked November 23, 2026. The higher 1.5-meter figures cannot replace the full-height 1,144-lb figure, and none is a guaranteed fork-tip or far-forward load capacity.

Why does a loader have multiple ratings?

A loader's mechanical leverage changes as its arms rise and the hydraulic cylinders move through their travel. Manufacturers therefore publish capacities at named heights and locations. Capacity at the bucket pivot is usually not equivalent to capacity at a load center farther forward, such as the center of a pallet on forks. Those are different geometries and often produce different maximum values.

This diagram simply scales the official figures. It does not represent a certified lifting calculation for a particular tractor and attachment configuration.

Does a bigger tractor automatically mean more loader lift?

Even among machines using the same loader family, a manufacturer may publish different ratings for a given test configuration. Kubota gives the L2502 a lower listed 1.5-meter pivot-point figure than the L3302 and L3902. The correct conclusion is that the specified combinations have these ratings, not that engine horsepower alone sets lift capacity. Tires, ballast, hydraulic design, loader position and front-axle limits matter.

What about a grapple or pallet forks?

Forks or a grapple weigh something before any material is added. Their weight uses part of the loader's capacity, and their load center may be forward of the pivot. Confirm the actual attachment's weight, carrier, couplers, rated load center, cylinder requirements, and Kubota's complete loader/tractor manual. Do not calculate a safe pallet weight by subtracting bucket weight from a pivot-pin maximum alone.

Optional quick coupler

Kubota lists an LA526 package with a standard two-lever quick coupler and another without it. A quick coupler is helpful when changing buckets, forks or other tools, but its presence can affect mounting dimensions and the total mass of the attachment. Verify exact package and implement interface before ordering aftermarket equipment.

Hydraulic circuit requirements

A hydraulic grapple may require an additional valve and appropriate pressure/flow connections. The tractor's total hydraulic pump rating does not automatically prove that a single third-function circuit can deliver all the flow. See how to read hydraulic GPM.

Before lifting or transporting a load

  1. Identify the exact tractor, LA526 option, coupler, tire and ballast configuration.
  2. Read lift ratings at the same height and load-center position as your intended job.
  3. Account for the weight and forward reach of buckets, forks, grapples and the load itself.
  4. Follow the manufacturer's guidance for stability, axle loading and safe ground conditions.
  5. Do not use published pivot capacity as a lifting guarantee on slopes or uneven ground.

See the model-specific L3302 HST, L3902 HST and L3302 DT 2026 pages for their separate engine and PTO ratings.

Primary source

Kubota USA, Standard L Series, performance-matched LA526 front loader. Figures checked November 23, 2026. The actual machine, loader and attachment operator manuals take precedence for safe operating limits.

records.title: Kubota L3302 & L3902 DT vs HST: 2026 PTO HP & Weight
records.excerpt: Official Kubota 2026 Standard L02 comparison of L3302 and L3902 gear-drive vs HST: 28.0 vs 26.1 PTO hp and 32.1 vs 30.3 PTO hp; 24-inch hitch rating and transmission differences.
records.content:
The Kubota L3302 and L3902 are available with either a gear-drive DT or hydrostatic HST drivetrain. The official 2026 Kubota Full Line Brochure gives different published PTO horsepower and weight figures for the two configurations. The comparison below stays within a single dated factory table instead of blending values from older brochures.

2026 L3302 DT versus HST

2026 factory figureL3302 DT 4WDL3302 HST 4WD
Gross engine horsepower33.033.0
PTO horsepower28.026.1
Travel transmission8 forward / 8 reverse shuttleThree-range HST
Rear hitch categorySAE Category ISAE Category I
Rear hitch lift 24 in behind1,435 lb1,435 lb
Published tractor weight2,734 lb2,778 lb

2026 L3902 DT versus HST

2026 factory figureL3902 DT 4WDL3902 HST 4WD
Gross engine horsepower37.537.5
PTO horsepower32.130.3
Travel transmission8 forward / 8 reverse shuttleThree-range HST
Hitch categorySAE Category ISAE Category I
Hitch lift 24 in behind1,435 lb1,435 lb
Published tractor weight2,767 lb2,778 lb

All entries above are from Kubota USA 2026 Full Line Brochure, printed page 12. They apply to the table's 4WD DT and HST configurations. These are manufacturer ratings, not independent dynamometer or trailer-scale results.

Why two official sources may show different weights or hitch figures

Kubota has also distributed an earlier standalone L02 brochure in which some tractor weights and hitch capacities differ from the 2026 Full Line table. For example, existing L3302 HST and L3902 HST records on our site cite a separate manufacturer edition with a 2,921-lb ROPS weight and a 1,433-lb 24-inch hitch rating. These figures must not be silently interchanged with the 2026 Full Line table's 2,778-lb weight and 1,435-lb hitch value. The two records are source-edition-specific, not independent verification of a physical change to all machines.

What does the PTO horsepower difference mean?

For the L3302 the gear-drive figure is 1.9 hp higher than HST. For the L3902 it is 1.8 hp higher. This can matter if an implement has a minimum PTO rating near either tractor's published capability, but it does not mean a gear-drive tractor will lift more weight at the loader. PTO power is only one part of implement fitment: shaft speed, gearbox rating, driveline guarding, tractor stability and the manufacturer's minimum required tractor size must also match.

Gear-shift operation versus hydrostatic travel

Deere and Kubota machines can both be designed for frequent direction changes, but the driver's control method differs. The Kubota DT uses a synchronized shuttle with fixed ratios; the Kubota HST allows variable travel speed within three ranges. If the primary work is loader handling near buildings, test the transmission controls personally. If the job is repetitive field work or a PTO-powered attachment, investigate operating speed, PTO requirements and ergonomics instead of assuming one transmission always wins.

Do the two transmissions change hitch lift capacity?

In this 2026 factory table the 24-inch-behind hitch lift figure is the same for both transmissions within each family: 1,435 lb. Do not conclude that an engine's extra gross or PTO horsepower raises the certified hitch capacity. The weight and center of mass of the actual implement still affect safe operating limits.

Check the front-loader measurements separately

The Kubota LA526 loader guide explains why capacity differs at maximum lift height versus at 1.5 meters and how attachment load center matters. For heavy forks, buckets and grapples, choose the right factory loader/tractor package and consider ballast, slope and pressure limits.

Which combination fits your property?

  • Choose by task: mow, till, grade, landscape or cycle a loader near obstacles.
  • Match the implement: use manufacturer PTO, hitch and hydraulic requirements at the correct measurement conditions.
  • Verify production edition: obtain the precise serial number and year-specific manual.
  • Get a complete quote: tire type, loader, counterweight, couplers and aftermarket options can change the final work-ready package.
  • Assess maintenance: check actual equipment accessibility, service history and local dealer support.

Individual records: L3302 DT, L3902 DT, L3302 HST, and L3902 HST.

Primary source and limits

Kubota 2026 Full Line Brochure, printed page 12, and Kubota Standard L Series US overview. Document checked November 23, 2026. Exact equipment configuration, serial/year and manuals remain authoritative for service and safety decisions.

records.title: Kubota L2502: Why Specs Say 24.8 or 23.3 HP
records.excerpt: Official Kubota US brochures show different L2502 figures: older 24.8 gross / 19.0 HST PTO HP versus 2026 23.3 gross / 18.4 HST PTO HP. Here's how to check the publication and model.
records.content:
Searching for Kubota L2502 horsepower can produce two seemingly contradictory answers: 24.8 gross engine horsepower and 23.3 gross horsepower. The HST PTO rating can also appear as 19.0 hp or 18.4 hp. These differences are visible in official Kubota publications, not merely unsourced dealer listings. Before comparing one tractor to another, identify which brochure edition and model configuration the numbers describe.

Side-by-side: two Kubota factory documents

Published Kubota figureEarlier US L02 spec sheet2026 Full Line brochure
L2502 gross engine power24.8 hp23.3 hp
L2502 gear-drive PTO power20.5 hp19.8 hp
L2502 HST PTO power19.0 hp18.4 hp
HST transmissionThree speed rangesThree speed ranges
L2502 4WD HST listed weight2,833 lb2,833 lb
Three-point hitch lift 24 in behind1,389 lb1,389 lb

Source documents: earlier Kubota L02 US specifications and 2026 Full Line Brochure, printed page 12. The table shows published figures; it does not establish the precise serial-number cutoff for a physical engine change or the reason Kubota revised the ratings.

Does this prove the engine was redesigned?

No. A difference between published figures may reflect a change in model specification, rating test conditions, certification, engine configuration or publication revision. These documents alone do not establish which explanation applies or when an individual machine changed. Do not turn this observation into an unsupported claim that all 2026 tractors differ mechanically from all previous model years. A dealership or manufacturer can confirm the exact machine using its complete serial number.

Why is the PTO difference especially relevant?

Rotary cutters, snowblowers, tillers and other powered implements are selected using available PTO power, required shaft speed and attachment-specific requirements. The HST PTO values in these documents differ by 0.6 hp, and the gear-drive values differ by 0.7 hp. If an implement needs a minimum output close to the published value, verify the tractor's exact rating before buying instead of assuming the higher number applies.

What about the gear-drive versus HST choice?

In both official documents, the gear-drive L2502 has more listed PTO horsepower than the HST variant within the respective edition. Kubota's Standard L overview describes an eight-forward/four-reverse gear-drive arrangement for the L2502 and a three-range hydrostatic option. The operating differences go beyond PTO rating: travel controls, forward/reverse changes, comfort and field use should be considered on a real demonstration.

How to verify the specification for your machine

  1. Write down the complete tractor model and serial number, including the transmission configuration.
  2. Request the correct model/year operator manual and current dealer specification document.
  3. Check whether the advertised engine or PTO rating matches a dated Kubota publication.
  4. Ask the dealer to confirm the approved PTO-powered attachment's horsepower and shaft-speed requirements.
  5. Do not assume a brochure difference establishes that two machines use different replacement parts. Confirm those from the official serial-specific parts catalog.

How our catalog handles older values

Our Kubota L2502 HST reference page records 24.8 gross hp and 19.0 PTO hp from the earlier factory spec sheet. These are document-specific figures, not a claim that every L2502 HST has the same ratings. The current US Standard L presentation and 2026 brochure use 23.3 gross and 18.4 HST PTO hp. For loader work, the LA526 loader lift reference explains height-specific capacities independently of engine horsepower.

Manufacturer references

Kubota L02 Specifications, earlier published edition; Kubota USA 2026 Full Line Brochure, page 12; Kubota Standard L Series US overview. Documents checked November 23, 2026. For an individual tractor's safe operation and service, the correct factory manuals take precedence.

records.title: John Deere 300E vs Kubota LA526: Loader Capacity Compared
records.excerpt: John Deere 300E and Kubota LA526 both publish pivot-pin lift at full height: 1,186 lb Deere vs 1,144 lb Kubota. Learn why maximum lift heights, attachment position and ballast still differ.
records.content:
The John Deere 300E and Kubota LA526 are front loaders associated with popular US compact tractors. On the surface their rated lift capacities seem close: Deere gives 1,186 lb at the pivot pin at full height for its referenced non-self-leveling 300E, while Kubota gives 1,144 lb at the pivot pin at full height for the LA526. Those are similarly named measuring positions but the loaders' maximum lift heights are not identical, nor do the ratings certify a safe load on a particular tractor and attachment.

What the manufacturers publish

FigureJohn Deere 300E (NSL)Kubota LA526
Pivot-pin lift at maximum height1,186 lb1,144 lb
Maximum lift height at pivotAbout 84 in94.2 in
Lift 500 mm forward at full height845 lbNot specified on cited series page
Lift at 1.5 m height, at pivotNot specified on cited US 300E page1,446 lb (L2502); 1,506 lb (L3302/L3902)
Listed tractor familiesSelected 3D and 3E, including 3025E/3032EL2502, L3302 and L3902

Sources are the John Deere 300E front loader specifications and Kubota USA Standard L Series loader section, checked November 23, 2026. No missing figure in the table is inferred from the other manufacturer's rating.

Can we say the Deere lifts 42 lb more?

The simple arithmetic difference at each source's stated maximum-height pivot position is 42 lb, but calling that a meaningful real-world advantage would overstate what these data prove. Maximum height differs, the corresponding tractor/loader combinations differ, and the sources do not represent a common laboratory test across brands. Compare both loaders at the same height, load center and attachment setup for a fair capacity assessment.

Why do pallet forks change the calculation?

The pivot pin is behind the forward load center of many pallet fork or grapple jobs. The John Deere document reports 845 lb at a point 500 mm forward of the pivot at full height, notably lower than its 1,186-lb at-pivot number. Kubota's cited series page does not supply a directly corresponding 500-mm rating, so it would be inaccurate to use the full-height 1,144 lb value as a pallet-fork rating. Ask the dealer for the complete loader/attachment load-center chart.

Does loader height matter?

Yes. Maximum lift height affects clearance when loading a trailer or container, and loader leverage can change with height. Deere's referenced 300E maximum at the pivot is approximately 84 inches; Kubota lists 94.2 inches for the LA526. A higher rated height is not automatically an advantage for every job and does not erase the need for proper ballast. Confirm the measured height of the exact installed loader and bucket configuration.

Which tractors are involved?

The Deere 300E page lists compatibility with 3025E and 3032E, among other 3E/3D variants. Kubota specifies LA526 for its L2502, L3302 and L3902 family. Model-family lists are not serial-specific installation approvals. Loader mounts, hoses, valves, quick-carrier type, tires and recommended rear ballast have to match the actual equipment.

Self-leveling and hydraulic accessory differences

John Deere offers an optional mechanical-self-leveling 300E configuration, which can have different ratings from the non-self-leveling table. Kubota offers LA526 packages with or without a two-lever quick coupler. These options change how a loader is operated and which attachments connect; they should be verified as part of a complete dealer quote. A grapple may also require a correctly sized third-function hydraulic circuit.

Practical buyer checklist

  1. Identify the exact tractor model and year, loader model and self-leveling or quick-attach option.
  2. Ask for capacity at a named lift height and forward load-center distance that match your intended task.
  3. Subtract or account for the weight of the actual fork frame, bucket or grapple using the manufacturer-approved method.
  4. Confirm tractor rear ballast, front axle/tire capacity, hydraulic connections and slope limits.
  5. Never use a pivot-pin brochure maximum as a safe payload guarantee for a moving tractor or elevated pallet.

Related reference pages

See the 300E pivot versus 500-mm capacity explanation and Kubota LA526 height-specific figures. Both include source-edition and load-position notes.

Original references

John Deere 300E official product data and Kubota USA Standard L Series loader data, checked November 23, 2026. This independently prepared comparison is not a lifting or engineering certificate.

Safe service and limitations

Secure the tractor and attachments as prescribed in its operator manual. Never work under hydraulically raised equipment without approved support, and keep hot fluids, rotating parts and pressurized fuel systems away from skin. If the factory procedure is unclear, use qualified service instead of guessing.

Manufacturer sources

John Deere LVU34504 product listing; John Deere 1025R worldwide replacement-parts guide (January 2024 publication). Manufacturer references checked November 23, 2026. Parts may be revised after a guide is published; confirm current dealer fitment before purchase.

records.title: John Deere AT25983 Air Restriction Indicator: 1025R Reference
records.excerpt: John Deere AT25983 air-filter restriction indicator reference for certain 1025R tractors. Understand its function and why exact machine serial fitment still needs the OEM catalog.
records.serial_scope: John Deere's OEM AT25983 air-restriction indicator listing includes the 1025R among generally compatible equipment. Check the full tractor PIN, original intake hardware and current supersession before ordering.
records.content:
John Deere AT25983 is an OEM air-filter restriction indicator listed by Deere for certain compact equipment, including the 1025R under its general compatibility information. The indicator provides a way to monitor air intake restriction without treating every dusty day as proof that the filter must be replaced. The presence of the number in a manufacturer equipment list is not a guarantee that an individual modified or earlier-production tractor has that exact component.

Part identification

OEM numberAT25983
FunctionAir intake / filter restriction indication
General Deere equipment referenceIncludes the John Deere 1025R, subject to exact fitment verification
Primary OEM lookupJohn Deere AT25983 original listing

What the indicator tells an owner

John Deere describes the 1025R air cleaner as having dual elements and a mechanical restriction indicator. Its service guidance identifies the red restriction indication as a reason to inspect or service the air cleaner on specified versions. A restriction signal is evidence that the intake needs manufacturer-directed attention; it does not prove whether the primary filter, secondary element, housing, intake screen or the indicator itself is defective.

Before replacing the indicator

Confirm the complete tractor PIN and the exact fitted air-cleaner arrangement. Check the indicator and air-intake assembly against the model-specific parts diagram and any current Deere supersession record. A used tractor may have a revised intake hose or relocated air-cleaner assembly, so do not select a part based only on matching model name or a photo.

Related service references

For an air-cleaner restriction warning, read our 1025R red restriction-indicator checklist. Deere's documented primary filter part number changes around serial JJ153036 / JJ153037; compare M131802 and LVU34503 only after confirming the actual tractor's full identification.

Safety and manufacturer sources

Only inspect the intake with the tractor shut down and secured as the owner's manual specifies. Never run the engine with filters or intake seals removed to see whether a warning clears. Sources: Deere AT25983 product details and Deere 1E/1R filter reference, checked November 23, 2026. Installation and service procedures must come from the correct operator manual.

records.title: John Deere 1025R Air Filter Restriction Indicator Red: What to Check
records.excerpt: Red air-filter restriction indicator on your John Deere 1025R? Learn how to safely inspect the intake, confirm serial-specific primary/secondary filter numbers, and recognize when professional service is appropriate.
records.content:
What should you do when the John Deere 1025R air-filter restriction indicator shows red? Deere's US product specifications describe a dual-element air cleaner with a mechanical restriction indicator. Its earlier 1E/1R service overview also states that specified 1025R and 1026R air filters should be serviced when the indicator is red. The exact response depends on the tractor and publication edition; it is not a reason to bypass the filter or assume the engine is failing.

Understand the warning before removing anything

The restriction indicator monitors resistance in the intake air system. A red indication can signal that the air-cleaner assembly needs attention. It does not, by itself, identify which part is at fault or prove that the filter is clogged beyond safe use. Record whether the warning appears only during mowing in dusty grass, after the machine is stored, or immediately after the air filter was serviced.

ObservationWhat to check using the proper manualWhy it matters
Red indicator after dusty mowingGrille, intake pre-screen, air-cleaner housing and permitted inspection of the primary elementDust and chaff can reduce airflow
Indicator shows red after filter replacementCorrect element number, fitted housing, sealing and indicator installationA wrong or damaged seal should not be hidden by resetting the indicator
Loss of power, abnormal exhaust or repeated alarmsModel-specific diagnostic codes, engine condition and air intake systemMore than routine filter service may be required
Missing or broken restriction indicatorCurrent original part reference and full tractor PINDeere generally lists AT25983, but a complete fitment lookup is still required

Safe first checks

  1. Move the tractor to a safe location and follow its shutdown procedure: PTO disengaged, implements safely lowered, parking condition secured and moving parts fully stopped.
  2. Note the indicator state before resetting or changing anything. Record the current engine-hour reading, dusty conditions and whether the machine is showing additional warnings.
  3. Inspect accessible exterior intake openings for obvious grass, packed chaff and damage. Follow the manual before opening the air-cleaner housing.
  4. Check the air-cleaner housing, primary element and seals using the exact model's approved procedure. Do not introduce dirt on the clean-air side.
  5. Confirm the correct primary and secondary element numbers from the factory catalog and the complete serial number; the 1025R has a documented air-filter serial break.
  6. Only reset or clear the mechanical restriction indicator as the operator manual describes. If it promptly returns or the engine behaves abnormally, arrange qualified diagnosis rather than repeatedly replacing parts.

Primary air filter numbers change by serial range

For the Deere 1025R HJ100001-and-later worldwide parts guide, the air-cleaner listings distinguish the following ranges:

Factory serial range in the cited guidePrimary air elementSecondary safety element
Through JJ153036M131802M131803
From JJ153037LVU34503LVU34504

This is a guide-specific serial reference, not an unconditional fitment guarantee. The full machine PIN and current OEM catalog should determine what to order, especially if the air cleaner has been replaced or modified. See our detailed 1025R air-filter serial guide for the separate filter numbers.

Does a red indicator replace the maintenance schedule?

No. Deere documents from different publication years include both indicator-based advice and calendar/hour-based filter replacement notes. For example, the 1E/1R filter overview discusses servicing a red restriction indicator, while the January 2024 1025R worldwide replacement-parts guide includes air-element replacement intervals. Do not merge these into a new universal schedule. Use the operator manual for the actual machine, its serial, model year, environment and current official Deere guidance.

What not to do

  • Do not operate the engine with the air filter removed as a test.
  • Do not assume an element is correct just because its dimensions look similar.
  • Do not use aggressive compressed air, liquid cleaning or a reset procedure unless permitted by the manual.
  • Do not continue heavy work with abnormal power loss, major intake damage or repeated warnings.
  • Do not confuse the AT25983 restriction indicator with a primary or secondary air filter.

When to request service

Seek qualified help if the indicator remains red after correct factory-directed inspection, the engine runs abnormally, clean-air duct seals are damaged, or the sensor/indicator and filter housing arrangement is unclear. A professional can check the restriction indication against the actual intake condition without taking unsafe shortcuts.

Manufacturer documents

John Deere USA 1025R air-cleaner specification, Deere 1E/1R Filter Overview, Deere 1025R Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide (2024), and Deere AT25983 product listing. Checked November 23, 2026. Treat all general guidance as secondary to the exact operator manual.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Won't Crank: PTO, Neutral Pedal and Battery Checks
records.excerpt: Kubota BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680 starter not cranking? Use the official BX80 manual to separate a PTO/neutral interlock condition, weak battery, and electrical faults without bypassing safety switches.
records.content:
Turn the key on a Kubota BX2380 and nothing happens, or the starter only clicks? The first job is to distinguish no-crank from an engine that cranks normally but does not fire. Kubota's official operator manual for the BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 identifies required starting-control positions and specific safety interlocks. Those facts are a safer starting point than immediately replacing a starter, bypassing a switch or repeatedly turning the key.

Quick symptom guide

Key on, no starter movementCheck required neutral and PTO positions first, then note lights and battery symptoms
Single click or repeated clicksRecord whether dashboard lights dim; weak battery or poor electrical connection is one possible cause, not a confirmed diagnosis
Starter turns the engine normallyThis is a crank/no-start symptom, not an interlock-only no-crank complaint; investigate using the model's fuel and engine starting sections
Starter works but tractor stops when PTO engagesConsult operator-presence and PTO instructions; do not bypass any protection device

1. Confirm the model-specific starting positions

The factory BX80 operator manual says the engine-start system requires the speed-control pedal in neutral and the PTO clutch lever off. Its starting sequence also directs the operator to set the parking brake, place the high/low range lever in neutral, and, on BX2380/BX2680 models, place the speed-set rod off. These are manufacturer instructions for the manual's documented versions, not interchangeable instructions for every Kubota tractor or later redesign.

Start from the operator's seat on safe level ground. Follow the exact manual rather than attempting to bridge a PTO switch or hold a travel pedal in a position that defeats an interlock. If a start request is blocked by a correctly operating safety device, the appropriate response is to correct the control position—not modify the electrical circuit.

2. Compare the electrical symptoms

ObservationWhat it may suggestSafe next action
No sound, dashboard displays remain normalStarting interlock or control-position issue is possibleVerify the tractor's official neutral/PTO conditions and note all warning indicators
Rapid clicking and dimming lightsInsufficient battery voltage or a poor connection may be involvedInspect the accessible battery area with the engine off; obtain an appropriate voltage/load test if uncertain
Starter turns slowlyWeak battery, cable issues, cold conditions or starter load are possibilitiesCheck safe battery and cold-weather guidance before repeated attempts
Starter cranks steadily but engine never firesA different engine/fuel/preheat problem, not a classic no-crank faultRecord fuel level, temperature and warnings; follow the correct fuel/start procedure

These are diagnostic distinctions, not a manufacturer-certified failure ranking. Multiple faults can create similar symptoms. Replace components only after appropriate checks establish the cause.

3. Battery condition and connections

In the BX80 manual's battery section, Kubota notes that a weak battery can make the engine difficult to start and can cause dim lights. The manufacturer recommends periodic battery inspection and following proper charging instructions. Corroded, loose or overheated connectors are also part of its daily electrical walk-around checks.

Battery systems can contain explosive gases. Do not bridge the battery terminals with a metal tool, create sparks near a battery, or jump-start a frozen battery. If charging or cable removal is necessary, use the exact manual and appropriate protective equipment; otherwise have a qualified technician handle it.

4. What the factory safety-switch checks actually test

In its 50-hour service section, Kubota provides an engine-start-system inspection for the speed-control pedal and PTO-clutch lever. The manual expects the engine not to crank when the appropriate prohibited control is engaged. It specifically tells the owner not to operate the tractor and to consult the dealer if a safety test fails.

This means the absence of cranking in a prohibited gear/PTO position may be evidence that the system is protecting the operator, not evidence that the starter motor has failed. Conversely, an engine that cranks with an unsafe control engaged could indicate a defective interlock and requires service. Do not diagnose by disconnecting, jumpering or shorting seat, neutral or PTO switches.

5. Limit cranking and distinguish cold-weather starting

Kubota's BX80 manual cautions against continuous starter use beyond 30 seconds, and describes a cold-weather start sequence with rest periods. A tractor that fails to start in cold weather may require the correct preheat procedure and battery checks rather than an extended crank or starting fluid. The same manual prohibits using ether/starting fluid in its documented starting instructions.

If an engine is already turning at normal starter speed, do not keep classifying the fault as no-crank. Record when the problem began, fuel level, preheat and warning indications, maintenance and recent repairs. For general diesel troubleshooting, our crank-but-no-start overview is a separate starting point.

6. When to stop and contact a dealer

  • The machine cranks when the manual says an engaged PTO or pedal must prevent starting.
  • Controls are in the correct positions but the tractor repeatedly refuses to crank.
  • Electrical wiring shows overheating, damaged insulation, corrosion or obvious modifications.
  • A battery is cracked, frozen, leaking or giving off unusual odors.
  • There is unexpected tractor movement, an abnormal PTO response, or doubt about operator-presence protection.

Tell the technician the exact BX model and serial number, hour-meter reading, weather, what the starter did, dashboard behavior and whether the controls met the manual's safe start position. This is more useful than ordering a starter or PTO switch without evidence.

Official references

Kubota BX1880/BX2380/BX2680 Operator's Manual: Starting the Engine (printed pp. 37–39), Checking Engine Start System (p. 82), and battery care in Periodic Service. Kubota USA Daily Maintenance Check Points. Checked November 23, 2026. This guide is an independent interpretation of manufacturer guidance, not a substitute for the correct serial-specific manual.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Stalls When You Stand Up or Engage PTO: OPC Guide
records.excerpt: Why a Kubota BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680 engine may stop when the operator stands or uses the PTO. Official BX80 operator-presence control rules and safe troubleshooting steps.
records.content:
Does your Kubota BX2380 stop running when you rise from the seat or when you engage the mower's PTO? The factory BX1880/BX2380/BX2680 operator manual explains an operator presence control (OPC) system designed to stop the engine under certain unsafe operating conditions. A normal safety shutdown is not the same as an engine fuel, injection or battery failure. The right next step is to identify exactly what action triggers the stop and compare it with the correct factory instructions.

Start by identifying the shutdown

SymptomRelevant factory behaviorOwner's safe next step
Engine stops when you rise while the PTO is engagedThe BX80 manual describes operator-presence protection involving the seat and PTO leverConfirm whether the shutdown is expected in that operating mode; do not defeat the seat switch
Engine stops when you rise with the speed-control pedal pressedThe OPC system also monitors the operator seat and travel pedalObserve the trigger with the machine safe and stationary; follow the manual's protection checks
Tractor stops even with PTO off and controls in proper neutral positionsNormal OPC behavior may not explain the complete symptomRecord warning indicators and request service if the behavior recurs
Tractor keeps operating when a factory safety test says it should stopA safety-system malfunction is possibleDo not operate; have the protective system inspected

What the Kubota manual says about the seat and PTO

The official BX80 guide states that the operator-presence system monitors the seat together with the speed-control pedal and PTO-clutch lever. Its periodic-service test expects the engine to shut down quickly if the operator leaves the seat while the travel pedal is operated, or when the PTO is engaged in the tested configuration. It also includes a special procedure for specific stationary rear-PTO applications. That exception has strict requirements and must not be confused with mower operation or used to bypass seat protection.

On this family, a mower or mid-PTO being engaged while the operator stands is therefore not automatically a sign of a broken fuel system. The expected reaction depends on PTO selector position, stationary/rear-PTO configuration and control state, so always read the serial-specific manual instead of applying a generic seat-switch rule from a different tractor.

Why this isn't a safe “jumper the switch” repair

Safety interlocks exist to reduce the likelihood of contact with rotating mower blades, unattended motion and other hazards. Shorting a seat switch, tying down the operator-presence sensor, using an unauthorized jumper wire or altering control wiring can cause the machine to operate when no responsible operator is controlling it. We do not recommend or describe bypass procedures.

Likewise, a machine that fails to stop during an official protective check should be removed from use rather than treated as convenient. Kubota specifically warns not to operate when required start/OPC system tests fail.

Safe observations that help the dealer

  1. Identify your model and entire machine serial number. Some owners refer to multiple BX generations by the same informal model shorthand.
  2. Record whether the tractor stalls when the seat is unloaded, the travel pedal is moved, or the PTO clutch is engaged. Do not test by dismounting a moving machine.
  3. Check warning lamps and whether shutdown is immediate or occurs after an extended period of work.
  4. Visually note any damaged or modified seat, connector or PTO lever arrangement with the tractor secured and engine shut down. Do not probe or bypass live wiring.
  5. Follow only the officially documented operator-presence test with all stated precautions and no bystanders, or ask the authorized dealer to perform it.

What if the engine stops while mowing but nobody stood up?

A shutdown during ordinary seated operation needs a broader diagnosis. It can differ from the expected OPC safety event. Consider any low-fuel indication, engine temperature, air-intake restriction, other warning or recent maintenance, but do not assume that a seat switch is defective or that a fuel filter should be replaced without evidence. Record whether the issue is repeatable, where it occurred and what other symptoms appeared.

Our overheating-while-mowing guide covers cooling-air restrictions. If an engine will not crank afterward, see the BX80 starter/neutral troubleshooting article for the documented start interlocks.

Does the rear-PTO stationary exception apply?

The BX80 manual has a separate section for approved stationary rear-PTO operation under prescribed conditions. It requires exact range/parking/seat and PTO setup and is not a general permission to leave the operator's seat when powered equipment is running. Never improvise a procedure for a chipper, pump, generator or mower; both the tractor and implement manuals must support the use. If any requirement is unclear, consult Kubota service.

How to describe the problem accurately

Instead of telling a mechanic “the engine randomly dies,” record a compact sequence: engine cold or hot; engine hour reading; PTO selector position; PTO clutch state; travel pedal/neutral position; operator seated or standing; attachment connected; warning lights; immediate or delayed shutdown. Those details help distinguish a safety event from a mechanical or electrical fault without removing any protection.

Source and safety limits

Kubota BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 Operator's Manual, sections on PTO use, the engine-start system and checking OPC (printed pp. 58–61 and 82–83). The manufacturer directs owners not to operate tractors that fail required safety tests. Source checked November 23, 2026. Use only the manual for your actual machine and never tamper with the interlocks.

records.title: Kubota BX80 50-Hour Maintenance: Grease Points & Safety Checks
records.excerpt: Kubota BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 50-hour manufacturer checklist: lubricate indicated fittings, inspect engine-start interlocks and OPC, and consult the correct manual for wheel and linkage checks.
records.content:
At 50 hours on a Kubota BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680, don't rely on a vague internet checklist such as “change everything.” Kubota's own BX80 operator manual has a named Service Every 50 Hours section. The documented work includes lubricating specified fittings and checking critical starting and operator-presence safety systems. Other maintenance items have their own intervals; the correct serial-specific manual must determine which apply to your individual machine.

What the BX80 factory manual puts in the 50-hour section

Factory maintenance headingWhy it mattersOwner's approach
Lubricating fittings with greaseLubrication protects the moving fittings shown in the manufacturer diagramsIdentify each fitting from the correct factory illustration; use the specified multipurpose grease and cleaning method
Checking the engine start systemNeutral/pedal and PTO switches must prevent unsafe startingFollow Kubota's exact prescribed test; stop using the tractor if it does not pass
Checking the operator presence control systemSeat/PTO and seat/travel protective behavior must function as specifiedUse the manufacturer procedure with all warnings, clear surroundings and no bystanders
Checking wheel bolt torque and other items in the 50-hour sectionWheel security and component condition affect stabilityUse only the correct torque values and tightening pattern for the actual wheels and tractor
Cleaning the lock-lever shaftFree movement of the named linkage is part of periodic inspectionUse the factory illustration and avoid forcing a seized lever

Grease points: use the factory illustrations

The official BX80 manual shows the grease-fitting locations in its printed pp. 81–82, including the speed-control pedal linkage and other machine pivot/connection points. This is why a written summary cannot replace the factory illustration: the location of a fitting matters as much as the grease quantity. Identify the correct point visually in the approved manual and wipe away excess contaminants according to the manufacturer directions.

Kubota says extremely wet or muddy operation may require greasing more often than the usual 50-hour note. Do not turn the published interval into a guarantee under severe conditions.

Engine start interlocks and OPC checks

The BX80 manual documents two safety groups at this interval. The engine-start switches should block cranking under specified unsafe pedal or PTO positions. The operator-presence system should stop the engine under the prescribed seated/travel/PTO tests.
