If the system behaves differently than the manual requires, do not operate the machine until the issue is corrected. Never bypass an electrical interlock to make a failed test “pass.”

For symptoms during normal use, read BX2380 no-crank checks or engine shutdown and operator-presence guide. Those are owner observation checklists, not factory-authorized electrical repair procedures.

Daily checks are still required

Kubota's separate US maintenance page identifies tire condition, leaks, engine/transmission oil, radiator and coolant, brake, safety switches, unusual noises and cooling screens among the daily checks. Reaching 50 hours does not replace daily inspection or imply that fluids should be changed only at 50-hour milestones. Verify each interval, usage condition and first-service exception in the manual.

How to keep a useful maintenance record

  1. Record the complete model, serial, date and hour meter before any work.
  2. Match each inspection item to the correct diagram and manufacturer's interval.
  3. Record which fittings were greased and the lubricant specified by the operator manual.
  4. Note protective checks performed, whether they passed and any unusual response.
  5. Include the tire/wheel fastener inspection and qualified repair notes if defects are found.
  6. Schedule the next hour-based or annual task according to your actual manual, not by blindly adding 50 hours to every previous job.

Why this is not a 50-hour fluid-replacement instruction

A calendar/engine-hour maintenance plan includes many systems with different schedules. Engine oil and filter, fuel filters, transmission fluid, coolant, front axle and air-cleaner items can have separate specifications or first-service conditions. Do not drain, refill or replace every filter merely because an online checklist groups them under “50-hour service.” Use the model-specific chart and current official dealer guidance.

Useful reference tools

Our preseason inspection checklist and maintenance guides provide additional owner context. For power and attachment specifications, see BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 reference pages.

Factory sources

Kubota BX1880/BX2380/BX2680 Operator's Manual, Service Every 50 Hours (printed pp. 81–83), together with Kubota USA Maintenance Check Points. Sources checked November 23, 2026. The official operating and maintenance instructions for your exact tractor serial always take priority.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 100-Hour Maintenance: Battery, Air Filter & Fuel Checks
records.excerpt: Kubota USA's BX2380 100-hour maintenance video covers battery/electrical, fuel, air-filter checks and adjustments. Use this model-aware planning guide with your U.S. operator manual.
records.content:
Approaching 100 hours on a Kubota BX2380 is a good time to get organized before maintenance. Kubota Tractor Corporation published an official US-focused BX Series 100-hour maintenance video in February 2026. Its stated topics include battery and electrical checks, fuel-system checks, air-cleaner service and key adjustments. This article organizes those topics into a practical planning checklist, without inventing a universal service schedule or a filter number for every BX80 production year.

Watch Kubota's BX2380 100-hour maintenance video

The following video is provided by Kubota Tractor Corporation and plays on this site. It is an official educational video, not an operator manual customized to your serial number.

[fms_kubota_bx_video lesson="100"]

Before beginning a 100-hour check

Record the complete tractor identification, including BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680, the serial/PIN, hour-meter reading, loader and mower options, and the specific US operator-manual edition. The different BX80 machines share some maintenance concepts, but differences in engine, air-cleaner arrangement and installed attachments can change what needs attention.

PreparationReason
Identify full model and serialParts, intervals and procedures may vary by production revision
Read maintenance chart100-hour inspection topics are not automatically replacement instructions
Check previous work recordsFirst-service exceptions and annual requirements may matter
Identify loader and mower accessoriesSeparate attachment maintenance can have different intervals
Secure a clean, level working areaMoving parts, battery acid and fuel handling present risks

1. Battery and electrical condition

Kubota's official video identifies battery and electrical inspection as a 100-hour topic. Before any hands-on service, stop the engine, remove the key and secure the machine according to its operator manual. Check the battery compartment for visible damage, loose parts, cable abrasion, corrosion and other conditions the exact manual instructs you to inspect.

Never bridge terminals with metal tools, create sparks near the battery or attempt to jump-start a damaged or frozen battery. The correct charging and terminal-disconnection sequence depends on the published instructions and the battery fitted. If the tractor repeatedly clicks instead of cranking, our BX80 no-crank symptom guide separates battery symptoms from start-interlock behavior without suggesting unsafe bypasses.

2. Fuel-system checks

The video includes fuel-system checks. Start with fuel level, visible leaks, hose condition and the documented filter-maintenance requirements for the full tractor serial. A fuel filter in another Kubota model, even one using a similar engine, is not proof of the BX2380's original filter part number. Do not order a filter by approximate shape or by another machine's internet parts list.

Do not loosen a running diesel's high-pressure injection components or use your hands to search for fuel leaks. Diesel injection injuries can be severe, and a suspected leak is a reason to stop and seek qualified service. If the engine already cranks but will not start, use the correct starting and low-pressure fuel priming steps only as published in the applicable operator manual.

3. Air filter, dust and radiator-screen observations

Air-cleaner care is another topic of the official Kubota 100-hour video. The machine may operate around fine grass chaff, dry mowing dust and airborne debris, which can affect both engine intake filtration and radiator cooling. Keep the filter housing and clean-air side protected when inspecting equipment. Do not assume blowing compressed air into every paper element is permitted; the replacement or cleaning method is model-specific.

When mower work raises coolant temperature, inspect the cooling screen and grille after the tractor is safely stopped and cooled, as explained in our tractor overheating guide. Never open a hot cooling-system pressure cap to check a level quickly.

4. Controls, belts and adjustment checks

Kubota's 100-hour video also mentions key adjustments. The older published BX80 operator manuals discuss items such as fan-belt inspection and brake-pedal condition in their periodic-service sections. That is useful background, but the exact adjustment method and service interval must be taken from the U.S. manual for your tractor. An incorrect belt adjustment, loosened linkage or unverified brake-pedal setting can make operation unsafe.

For any adjustment involving brakes, mechanical controls or operator-presence equipment, have a qualified technician perform the work if you cannot verify the exact factory process and required measurements. Never jumper the seat, neutral or PTO start-interlock switches.

Do 50-hour checks still apply?

The BX family has recurring checks at different operating-hour milestones. Greasing specified fittings, checking tire/wheel hardware, and ensuring safety devices function can remain relevant between major services. However, a 100-hour video is not a substitute for the chart with the exact intervals and first-service exceptions. See our 50-hour maintenance overview, which includes an edition note about the supporting Australian manual.

Use a service record rather than relying on memory

RecordExample of what to write
Date and hour meterCurrent reading, not merely “100-hour service done”
Battery/electricalCondition observed, testing performed and outcome
Fuel and airVisual observations, official component numbers and work completed
ControlsAny abnormal PTO, brake, interlock or travel response
Next checkpointHour/annual interval from the appropriate US manual

The 200-hour BX80 maintenance guide deals with a different service milestone; do not combine the two lists and assume each task is due every 100 hours.

Official U.S. reference and edition disclosure

Kubota Tractor Corporation: BX2380 100-Hour Maintenance (February 2026) and Kubota USA BX80 maintenance resources are the primary US owner-information sources. A U.S.-edition prior-generation BX80 manual is available through a Kubota dealer, but does not automatically apply to later machines. An additional BX80 operator PDF labeled -AU shows regional maintenance examples; do not apply AU-only instructions to US machines without confirmation. Source details checked November 23, 2026.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 200-Hour Service: Engine Oil, HST Filter & Toe-In
records.excerpt: Use Kubota USA's official BX 200-hour service video to plan engine oil/filter service, HST filter replacement, hydraulic checks and front-wheel toe-in inspection for your serial-specific BX tractor.
records.content:
The 200-hour maintenance point on a Kubota BX2380 is not just an invitation to replace every liquid and filter at once. Kubota Tractor Corporation published an official US educational video, Protect Your BX: 200-Hour Maintenance Done Right, in February 2026. The video description identifies engine oil and filter changes, hydrostatic transmission (HST) filter replacement, hydraulic oil checks and toe-in inspection/adjustment. The correct U.S. operator manual for your exact serial number controls when and how these tasks are performed.

Watch Kubota's official BX 200-hour service video

Play the original manufacturer video here, then compare every procedure and specification with the actual tractor's manual and installed equipment.

[fms_kubota_bx_video lesson="200"]

The service areas Kubota identifies

Service categoryCovered by official US videoCritical limitation
Engine oil and oil filterYesOil quantity and grade can vary by BX1880/BX2380/BX2680 engine and edition
HST / transmission oil filterYesNot the same as replacing all transmission fluid on every machine
Hydraulic oil checkYesCheck fluid level with the model's required conditions, not a guessed fill volume
Front wheel toe-inYesRequires correct measurement procedure and specified adjustment limits
Other calendar/annual itemsConsult factory manualThe video is not an exhaustive list of every service task

1. Oil and engine oil filter: distinguish service from capacity

The engine's published oil capacity describes a specified fill condition, but the actual amount needed after a drain can vary with the filter, temperature and residual oil. Kubota's BX family uses more than one engine size, so never borrow a BX2680 oil-capacity value for a BX1880 without checking its manual. The safe approach is to identify the correct oil specification and filter in the source for that exact machine, follow the approved drain procedure, then verify the correct oil level after filling and as the manual directs.

Used oil can cause burns while hot, and an improperly seated filter seal can leak under pressure. Stop and cool the engine, follow the manufacturer instructions and dispose of oil through an approved collection program. Do not assume “suitable for Kubota BX” on a marketplace listing is equivalent to the exact OEM filter number.

2. HST filter versus transmission fluid

Kubota's official video distinguishes an HST filter replacement from hydraulic oil checks. On certain model editions, transmission fluid replacement has a different service interval from filter replacement. This is a particularly important distinction because a generic “200-hour HST service” article may tell owners to drain all oil when their serial-specific service table does not call for it.

Check the filter part number and installed transmission configuration, then confirm whether the correct manual calls for replacing the filter, draining the system, inspecting a strainer or another separate step. Never loosen hydraulic lines to test fluid flow or work underneath a hydraulically supported loader. If a machine uses a shared HST/hydraulic reservoir, that does not automatically mean it takes the same lubricant as a different tractor model.

3. Hydraulic oil level and visible hose condition

Hydraulic levels are often sensitive to the tractor's parking position, attachment position and whether the engine has cooled. Record the condition when checking; use only the manufacturer's dipstick or sight-glass procedure. If a visible high-pressure leak, damaged hose or unusual cylinder movement is present, stop work and use professional service rather than touching the leak or overriding pressure settings.

Our hydraulic flow reference explains why a pump's brochure GPM rating is not proof that a loader or auxiliary valve is functioning correctly.

4. Toe-in inspection and wheel alignment

Front-wheel toe-in is a steering/alignment measurement, not an engine or PTO setting. The US Kubota 200-hour video includes inspection and adjustment. Incorrect adjustment can affect tire wear and steering, so use the exact measurement points and permitted range in the correct manual. Do not substitute a value found in a different BX generation or adjust tie rods by eye.

A steering wheel that vibrates, erratic handling, uneven tire wear or evidence of impact damage calls for a broader inspection. Wheel bolts, tires, front-axle components and steering linkage may also need attention; obtaining qualified service is appropriate if the cause is unclear.

Keep first-service and yearly rules separate

Many tractors have break-in service items that occur before later repeating intervals. Model-year revisions and annual limits may also shorten a maintenance period even if the hour meter advances slowly. These details must be read from the exact operator manual. For example, an Australian BX80 manual published for BX1880-AU / BX2380-AU / BX2680-AU contains its own 200-hour section and later separate transmission-fluid interval. That supports the general need to distinguish service types, but it is not authority to apply those intervals to an arbitrary U.S. machine.

Checklist before contacting a Kubota dealer

  1. Record BX1880, BX2380 or BX2680 and the complete machine serial/PIN, model year and engine hours.
  2. Read the exact U.S. operator manual and confirm what is due by hours and by date.
  3. Identify the factory-approved engine oil, engine filter and HST filter numbers and any supersessions.
  4. Check prior maintenance logs, especially initial break-in work and previous annual oil services.
  5. List attached mower, loader, front hitch and hydraulic options with separate maintenance requirements.
  6. Bring any visible leaks, unusual noises or steering concerns to a qualified technician's attention.

Related articles: 100-hour battery/air/fuel guide, 50-hour BX80 checks and BX2380 fluid-capacity reference. Never use these summary pages in place of the specific factory manual.

Manufacturer sources and regional caution

Kubota Tractor Corporation: Protect Your BX, 200-Hour Maintenance Done Right (February 2026) and Kubota USA BX80 Series resource page. The separately available prior-generation U.S. Kubota BX80 manual provides an example of a dated edition; a different Australian BX80 manual must not be mistaken for a U.S. serial-specific instruction. All sources checked November 23, 2026.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Maintenance Schedule: 50, 100 & 200 Hour Guide
records.excerpt: A careful Kubota BX2380, BX1880 and BX2680 hour-meter maintenance hub linking factory 50-hour safety checks and official Kubota USA 100-/200-hour videos. Compare manual editions before working.
records.content:
Looking for a trustworthy Kubota BX2380 maintenance schedule? The safest starting point is not a universal internet list of every fluid and filter at 50, 100 and 200 hours. Kubota's own BX80-series literature and US maintenance videos distinguish multiple service milestones, while its operator manuals can vary by region, production year, equipment options and first-service instructions. This index helps you find the right source and the detailed guide for a task without mixing incompatible service editions.

Start with your complete tractor identification

The Kubota BX1880, BX2380 and BX2680 are related sub-compact tractors, but they do not necessarily share the same engine oil volume, filter housing or required attachment service. The Kubota USA BX80-series page offers model details, a maintenance library and links to official how-to videos. Record the exact model, serial/PIN, engine hour reading, transmission and installed loader/mower equipment before deciding that a specific operation is due.

Which source covers each milestone?

Hour-meter topicVerified source scopeWhere to read more
50 hoursA published Australian BX1880-AU/BX2380-AU/BX2680-AU manual includes lubrication and safety-system inspections in its 50-hour section. This is not proof of the US schedule.50-hour source-edition guide
100 hoursOfficial Kubota Tractor Corporation US educational video covers battery/electrical, fuel, air filtration and selected adjustments.100-hour guide with video
200 hoursOfficial US manufacturer video covers engine oil/filter, HST filter, hydraulic oil checks and toe-in.200-hour guide with video
Later or annual checksFluid changes, axle service, air cleaner, coolant and first-service exceptions require the specific correct operator manual.Kubota USA resources

50 hours: don't skip a safety inspection

Kubota's BX80 manual published for Australian configurations describes checking protective starting and operator-presence systems at regular service intervals. A safety switch that works as designed may prevent cranking in a prohibited control position; a failed test is a reason to stop work, not a reason to bridge or disconnect the switch. The US market can use different configurations or publication revisions, so verify the specific test and interval with your own machine's factory manual.

For symptom-specific checks, read BX2380 no-crank diagnostics and BX80 seat/PTO shutdown checks. Both separate potentially normal interlock behavior from faults without offering bypass procedures.

100 hours: inspect air, fuel and electrical systems

Kubota's US 100-hour video identifies battery, electrical, fuel, air-cleaner and adjustment topics. Depending on the equipment, practical inspections may include exterior wiring damage, filter housing seals, chaff around air inlets, leaks and documented service history. Do not replace every air cleaner or fuel filter at 100 hours on every BX machine merely because these systems appear in the video. Check the approved interval, condition-based requirements and correct OEM parts for your specific serial number.

Go to the 100-hour maintenance guide to play the official Kubota USA demonstration directly on our site.

200 hours: oil and HST tasks are not identical

Kubota's US 200-hour video addresses engine oil/filter replacement, an HST filter, hydraulic oil checks and front-wheel toe-in. It is important to distinguish an HST filter change from draining the entire transmission system; the two can have different scheduled intervals depending on manual revision and machine generation. Oil capacity, correct lubricant, filters and tow/attachment options are model-specific. See the 200-hour service guide and factory video.

Build a maintenance log that survives resale

FieldRecord this information
Tractor identificationFull model, year/serial or PIN and installed implements
Service milestoneHour reading, date and specific manual edition used
Items performedSystem checked, official part number, fluid product and amount actually added if applicable
ObservationsWear, leaks, warning lamps, unexpected shutdown, loose hardware or unusual noises
Next due pointHour and/or calendar deadline from the correct factory schedule, including severe-use conditions

Always follow the operator manual's safe shutdown, PTO disengagement, parking and cooling requirements. Never work under unsupported raised equipment, open hot pressure caps or handle a suspected high-pressure fluid leak with your fingers. If a maintenance task calls for a specification or procedure you cannot verify, consult a Kubota dealer.

Do not mix the Australian PDF with a US manual

An online Kubota operator PDF is marked BX1880-AU, BX2380-AU and BX2680-AU. It can show how a Kubota manual organizes service tasks, but its regional edition is not authority for a specific tractor sold in the United States. A prior-generation U.S.-edition operator manual is also available from a Kubota dealership; it should not be silently substituted for the manual supplied with a later model. For safety and warranty purposes, always verify the exact machine and the applicable US publication.

Official U.S. Kubota references

Kubota USA BX80 Series: maintenance resources; Kubota Tractor Corporation 100-hour service video; Kubota Tractor Corporation 200-hour service video. Source details verified November 23, 2026. These guides are editorial overviews, not replacement owner manuals or factory service authorizations.

records.title: New Holland WORKMASTER 25S Specs: 24.7 Engine HP, 17.2 PTO HP
records.excerpt: New Holland USA WORKMASTER 25S: 24.7 gross engine horsepower, 17.2 PTO hp, standard 4WD, two-range hydrostatic drive, and 100LC loader / 160GMS mower attachments.

specs.fms_engine_make: New Holland listed three-cylinder diesel (precise engine identifier requires serial-specific manual)
specs.fms_configuration_notes: Manufacturer US WORKMASTER 25S listing, checked 2026-11-23. Two-range dual-pedal hydrostatic drive with standard 4WD; manufacturer markets an unqualified 992-lb lift capacity, but the model landing page does not establish a measured 24-in-behind hitch position or whether that figure is a specific loader/three-point test. Therefore no standardized lift field is populated. Cab and open ROPS and specific attachment bundles differ. PTO shaft rpm, hydraulic pump GPM, base shipping weight and exact hitch category are not established by this source page and intentionally omitted.

records.content:
The New Holland WORKMASTER 25S is a compact 4WD sub-compact tractor offered to US property owners for mowing, landscaping, snow removal and loader jobs. New Holland currently lists 24.7 gross engine hp and 17.2 PTO hp, with a standard two-range hydrostatic transmission. The engine and PTO measurements serve different purposes: power available at an implement shaft is lower than the manufacturer's published gross engine rating.

Engine output and transmission

The US WORKMASTER 25S page lists a 24.7 hp gross engine rating, four-wheel drive and two hydrostatic ground-speed ranges. New Holland describes independent forward and reverse pedals rather than a clutch-and-shuttle gear-change procedure. Low and high ranges are intended for different operating conditions, but choosing the correct one, managing loads and using the operator-presence and rollover safety equipment still require the exact manual.

17.2 PTO horsepower

New Holland advertises 17.2 PTO hp. Use that value rather than 24.7 gross engine hp when considering a PTO-driven tiller, mower or snowblower. PTO attachment requirements are more than horsepower: the correct shaft speed, mechanical guard, gearbox, cutting or digging load and tractor stability must all be checked. The engine-versus-PTO horsepower guide explains the difference between the two ratings.

Loader, mower and backhoe options

The official US page names the 100LC front loader, 160GMS mid-mount mower with a 60-inch cutting width, and 905GBL backhoe with a stated 79.4-inch digging depth. These are named equipment options, not a claim that every dealer tractor includes them. New Holland specifically says the backhoe option is available for the ROPS configuration rather than the cab-equipped variant. Verify the actual package and attachment-mount requirements in the dealer build sheet.

What does the published 992-lb lift figure mean?

New Holland's US overview calls out 992 lb (450 kg) of lift capacity. However, that headline does not disclose a precise load-center distance or a 24-inch-behind three-point hitch measurement on the page we checked. We do not enter 992 lb as a standardized 24-inch hitch rating or a loader-fork payload. For a safe comparison, request the complete factory specification table for the exact tractor, front loader and rear hitch.

ROPS versus cab configurations

ConfigurationManufacturer-listed distinction
Open ROPS platformStandard four-wheel drive, flat Clear-Thru operator platform, available loader/mower/backhoe options
Cab configurationFactory-described enclosed operator area with heater, doors, lights and visibility provisions; backhoe applicability differs
TransmissionTwo-range hydrostatic drive; actual control options depend on package
PTO power17.2 hp manufacturer listing

Installed mower, loader, cab, ballast and filled tires affect the tractor's actual transported weight. The source page does not give a single standardized machine weight, so no number is entered into our weight comparison.

Compared with the John Deere 1025R

John Deere publishes 24 rated engine hp and 18 PTO hp on its current US 1025R listing, while New Holland reports 24.7 gross and 17.2 PTO hp for the WORKMASTER 25S. These are manufacturer-listed values, not a shared dynamometer test; differing power standards, equipment and PTO testing may affect comparisons. Use our WORKMASTER 25S vs 1025R guide for a closer look at the controls, loader packages and missing hitch-capacity details.

Before ordering parts or attachments

  1. Record the entire tractor model and PIN, transmission and cab/ROPS setup.
  2. Identify the installed 100LC loader, 160GMS mower or 905GBL backhoe and exact model-year package.
  3. Obtain rated lift at a named loading position, height and approved attachment carrier.
  4. Confirm hitch, rear PTO, required ballast and hydraulic attachment circuit from original manuals.
  5. Check current dealer parts availability and any serial-based supersessions before buying filters or repair components.

Primary manufacturer source

New Holland Agriculture USA: WORKMASTER 25S Sub-Compact Tractor, checked November 23, 2026. Manufacturer ratings may be revised and equipment packages vary. This independent reference does not replace the exact original operator/attachment manual.

records.title: New Holland WORKMASTER 35 Specs: 35 HP, 540 RPM PTO & Hydraulics
records.excerpt: New Holland WORKMASTER 35 US compact tractor: 35 gross HP, 540-rpm rear PTO, available 12x12 shuttle or HST, standard 4WD and 8.2-gpm hydraulics by manufacturer series overview.

specs.fms_engine_make: New Holland turbocharged three-cylinder diesel; exact engine identifier depends on serial/edition
specs.fms_configuration_notes: New Holland USA WORKMASTER Compact 25/35/40 series page lists 35 gross HP for WORKMASTER 35; series offers 12x12 synchronized shuttle or hydrostatic gearbox and standard 4WD. Series feature section describes 8.2 US gpm dedicated hydraulic flow (7.9 gpm for WORKMASTER 25). Manufacturer's 1,808-lb three-point figure lacks a verified 24-inch load-location specification on this landing page; standardized hitch field omitted. PTO horsepower, source-edition base weight, fuel capacity and specific PTO configuration are not established by this source; do not guess.

records.content:
The New Holland WORKMASTER 35 is a compact tractor in the manufacturer's US 25/35/40 series. Its US model overview states 35 gross engine horsepower, standard four-wheel drive and an independent 540-rpm rear PTO. New Holland promotes both a synchronized-shuttle gear transmission and a hydrostatic option across the family. Check the exact model code and dealer build sheet to establish which transmission and attachments are on a given tractor.

35 gross engine horsepower

The WORKMASTER 35 is listed at 35 gross hp in the US series model table. New Holland says the 35- and 40-hp three-cylinder engines use turbocharging and electronically managed common-rail direct injection. The source page does not report a verified WORKMASTER 35 PTO horsepower value, so we leave PTO hp blank in the normalized model data rather than infer it from gross power.

Manual shuttle versus hydrostatic transmission

New Holland's series overview describes 12x12 synchronized shuttle and hydrostatic transmission choices, allowing different ways to manage ground speed. The exact hydrostatic range count depends on the configuration, and the factory model/serial manual remains the correct source for operating procedures. A shuttle gearbox's reverse change is not the same as twin-pedal hydrostatic control, especially during repeated loader work.

Rear PTO and implement compatibility

The US manufacturer page says WORKMASTER compact tractors have a 540-rpm rear PTO. It also discusses an optional 2,000-rpm mid PTO on specified transmission configurations. This does not establish that every 35-hp tractor comes with the mid-PTO option or that a 540-rpm implement is always correctly sized. Match the implement's power demand, PTO driveline and guarding, three-point hitch geometry and ballast requirements.

Hydraulic flow interpretation

New Holland calls out a dedicated hydraulic flow of 8.2 US gpm in its WORKMASTER compact series description (with 7.9 gpm for the 25-hp version). It separately mentions a steering pump. This description is more specific than a combined total-pump figure, but it is still not proof of 8.2 gpm delivered continuously at an individual remote valve on every installed tractor. Use the hydraulic-flow guide before choosing a motor-driven or third-function attachment.

Rear hitch: a rating needs a test position

New Holland describes a 1,808-lb three-point hitch lift capacity on the series overview. It does not identify this as measured exactly 24 inches behind the lower hitch arms on the reviewed page. Therefore, our comparison field for “lift at 24 inches” remains unfilled. Comparing the 1,808-lb headline with a measured Kubota or Massey Ferguson 24-inch rating without a matched load position would be misleading.

Specifications summary

FeatureManufacturer publication
Gross engine power35 hp
Engine familyTurbocharged 3-cylinder, electronically managed injection
DriveStandard four-wheel drive
Travel transmission12x12 synchronized shuttle or an available HST configuration
Rear PTO speed540 rpm
Series hydraulic flow description8.2 US gpm dedicated
Rear hitch capacity1,808 lb manufacturer figure, point not confirmed

These values describe a manufacturer model series, not a particular configured tractor. Weight with a cab, loader, fuel, rear implement or tire ballast is not stated in the source table.

New Holland WORKMASTER 35 versus 25S

The WORKMASTER 25S is a smaller sub-compact with 24.7 gross hp and 17.2 PTO hp. The WORKMASTER 35 offers a higher listed gross engine rating, a larger compact-tractor product family and different transmission choices. It is not valid to infer that its PTO is higher by exactly the same percentage as the engines. The source documents do not supply a matched loader, weight and hydraulic flow table for every package.

Pre-purchase questions

  • What is the complete US model code, production year and tractor serial/PIN?
  • Is the tractor the shuttle version or hydrostatic variant, and does it have the optional mid PTO?
  • What is the rated loader lift at a defined height and load-center point?
  • What is the three-point rating measured 24 inches behind the arms, not just at another location?
  • What are the dealer-approved parts, fluids, service intervals and safety procedures for that exact build?

Manufacturer source

New Holland Agriculture USA WORKMASTER Compact 25/35/40 Series. Verified November 23, 2026. This page summarizes source-defined series figures only; check the precise factory/manual edition for individual service or fitment decisions.

records.title: John Deere MIU804763 Fuel Filter Element: 1025R OEM Guide
records.excerpt: John Deere MIU804763 fuel-filter element for specified 1025R machines. Not the AM116304 inline filter; verify official part fitment, the complete PIN and manufacturer service interval.
records.serial_scope: John Deere 1025R worldwide replacement-parts guide HJ100001-and-later (January 2024) lists MIU804763 as a fuel-filter element, separate from AM116304 inline fuel filter. Both Deere filter packs LVA21036 and TA25769 list MIU804763. Confirm current fit by machine PIN.
records.content:
John Deere MIU804763 is the diesel fuel-filter element listed in Deere's January 2024 worldwide 1025R replacement-parts guide for machines in its HJ100001-and-later scope. The same guide identifies a different AM116304 inline fuel filter. Both numbers may be relevant to a complete fuel-system service, but they are separate OEM parts with different installation locations and functions.

Manufacturer part identification

ItemDocumented reference
Fuel filter elementMIU804763
Separate inline fuel filterAM116304
Deere worldwide parts guide1025R from HJ100001, January 2024 publication
2024 guide service note400 hours and annually for listed fuel-filter service; confirm the exact machine's manual
Filter kits whose published contents include MIU804763LVA21036, TA25769

Why one model can have more than one fuel filter

A diesel fuel system can use an in-line prefilter and a separate filter element at another location. Manufacturer filters have different dimensions, filtration characteristics, water-management properties and fitting designs. Deere describes the MIU804763 part in its store as an original fuel-filter element with water-separation media. A similar-looking hose filter is not automatically a correct replacement.

Deere's 1025R Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide identifies MIU804763 and AM116304 separately under the engine fuel-system callout. They are not two names for the same element. Refer to the current original equipment catalog for the correct part diagram and any supersession.

What changes at serial 153036 / 153037?

The manufacturer distinguishes the LVA21036 kit (generally through 153036) and the TA25769 kit (generally from 153037), primarily by the included primary air-cleaner element. Both kit lists include MIU804763. That is useful information, but it does not prove a previously modified or re-engined tractor still follows the original parts diagram.

Before ordering

  1. Record the full model name, production serial/PIN and engine configuration.
  2. Compare the original filter housing and fuel routing with the correct Deere parts illustration.
  3. Check the current MIU804763 product page for updated fitment and superseding part numbers.
  4. Read the actual operator manual before opening a fuel-system connection or replacing a filter.
  5. Keep fuel away from ignition sources and never loosen high-pressure injection lines to look for fuel.

Fuel-system symptoms do not identify a filter automatically

Hard starting, rough running or power loss can involve fuel contamination, air entering the low-pressure system, storage conditions, electrical faults or other issues. Do not order an MIU804763 solely because the engine cranks but does not fire. Our safe diesel crank/no-start guide explains what to record before further service.

Original sources

John Deere MIU804763 original product listing and John Deere 1025R Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide (Jan 2024). Checked November 23, 2026. Model lists are general; verify exact individual serial and the correct operator manual.

records.title: John Deere M131803 Secondary Air Filter: 1025R Early Serial
records.excerpt: Deere M131803 secondary air safety element for the 1025R through serial JJ153036 in the January 2024 guide. Paired with M131802 primary; later models list LVU34504 instead.
records.serial_scope: John Deere 1025R Worldwide Parts Guide (HJ100001 onward, Jan 2024) identifies M131803 as secondary safety air filter through JJ153036, paired with M131802 primary. For JJ153037 onward it lists LVU34504 secondary and LVU34503 primary. Verify full PIN and the correct air-cleaner housing.
records.content:
The original John Deere M131803 is a secondary safety air-filter element. Deere's January 2024 1025R worldwide parts guide lists it for the earlier air-cleaner range, through JJ153036, paired with the M131802 primary element. This serial distinction is essential when ordering filters because the guide lists another primary and secondary pair from JJ153037 onward.

What the official Deere guide states

Serial scope in cited guidePrimary elementSecondary element
Through JJ153036M131802M131803
JJ153037 onwardLVU34503LVU34504

The table comes from John Deere's original 1025R worldwide parts guide for the listed HJ100001-and-later tractors. A machine with a changed intake housing may not follow the original serial arrangement; use its correct OEM diagram to verify.

What does a secondary air filter do?

The secondary element provides an additional barrier against intake contamination inside the specified air-cleaner housing. It is not a replacement for the primary filter, and the two parts are not interchangeable. Dirt introduced on the clean-air side during service can defeat both stages of filtration, which is why housing seals and the correct manual procedure are important.

Does the early-serial filter kit contain M131803?

The official LVA21036 Filter Pak component list names M131802 as its primary air element. It does not list M131803 among the five included components. Therefore, do not assume that buying the pack provides both elements required by the air-cleaner assembly. Check the contents of the specific package currently offered by the seller.

When to inspect or replace

The January 2024 Deere guide gives a published 200-hour and annual replacement note for the air-filter entries. Treat this as edition-specific guidance rather than a universal maintenance instruction for every production year or dusty working environment. Always use the actual serial-specific operator manual and air-restriction indicator guidance, not solely a calendar estimate.

Safe intake service

  1. Identify the complete tractor serial number and air-cleaner configuration before purchasing a part.
  2. Stop and secure the tractor, including the PTO and any powered attachment.
  3. Protect the clean-air side when the housing is open; follow the factory procedure to inspect seals.
  4. Do not run the engine with the primary or secondary filter missing.
  5. Use the current OEM catalog for possible supersessions and the proper replacement technique.

For symptom-based guidance see red air-filter restriction indicator checks and the original 1025R serial-number air-filter guide.

Manufacturer references

Deere M131803 original part listing and 1025R Worldwide Replacement Parts Guide, January 2024, checked November 23, 2026. Confirm actual engine and housing equipment before ordering.

records.title: New Holland WORKMASTER 25S vs John Deere 1025R: PTO & Attachments
records.excerpt: Compare New Holland WORKMASTER 25S and Deere 1025R using official US engine and PTO ratings (24.7/17.2 vs 24/18 HP), HST controls and loader options, without assuming unmatched hitch or load-center measurements.
records.content:
The New Holland WORKMASTER 25S and John Deere 1025R both target US landowners looking for a four-wheel-drive sub-compact tractor to mow, clear snow, move landscaping material and work with smaller implements. Their advertised horsepower ratings are close: New Holland lists 24.7 gross engine hp and 17.2 PTO hp, while Deere's current US 1025R listing gives 24 rated engine hp and 18 rated PTO hp. These figures are useful starting points, not proof that the two machines are identical in real work.

Official manufacturer figures compared

Manufacturer-published itemWORKMASTER 25SJohn Deere 1025R
Engine power24.7 gross hp24 rated hp (SAE J1995)
PTO power17.2 hp18 hp
Travel driveTwo-range hydrostaticTwo-range hydrostatic
Drive wheelsStandard four-wheel driveFour-wheel drive in cited US equipment configuration
Rear hitch capability992-lb manufacturer lift headline, exact test location not stated on overviewLimited Category 1 hitch in Deere's specification
Loader optionNew Holland 100LCDeere 120R (verify exact configuration)
Mid-mount mower option160GMS, 60-inch cutDeere AutoConnect-compatible mower packages (exact deck model varies)

Sources: New Holland WORKMASTER 25S US overview and John Deere 1025R USA product specifications, checked November 23, 2026. An omitted measurement is not inferred from another brand's model or a dealer advertisement.

What does the PTO horsepower difference mean?

Deere lists 18 PTO hp against New Holland's 17.2 hp, a nominal difference of 0.8 PTO horsepower across those manufacturer sheets. It is too small a gap to declare that the Deere always mows faster or runs every attachment better. Implement cutting demand, gearbox, shaft configuration, grass density, blades, ground conditions, and PTO test methods can matter more than a simple horsepower subtraction. Match the actual attachment's minimum PTO rating and manual.

Why engine horsepower doesn't settle the choice

The New Holland source calls its 24.7 figure gross engine power. Deere calls the 1025R figure rated engine power under SAE J1995. Different model years, rating conventions and engine configurations must be aligned before drawing conclusions from a decimal. A slightly higher listed engine rating on one brochure does not establish more loader lift or hydraulic flow.

Two-range hydrostatic controls

Both manufacturers describe two travel ranges, but their operator platforms and exact control packages differ. New Holland emphasizes dual forward/reverse pedals and a Clear-Thru flat deck. Deere offers its own hydrostatic pedal and implement-connection arrangements. Choose a safe dealership demonstration with representative work, not just a stationary walkaround photo, and confirm the transmission in the exact quote.

Loader capacity is not a common single number

The WORKMASTER 25S official overview mentions 992 lb of lift capacity without defining a comparable measured position in the general product text. The Deere 1025R uses loader-specific 120R test ratings that require attention to loader options, load center, lift height and ballast. Those two figures cannot fairly be treated as a side-by-side fork payload comparison. The appropriate source is a measured chart for each installed tractor-plus-loader package at the same test conditions.

Mower, backhoe and cab choices

New Holland names the 160GMS mid mower and 905GBL backhoe for specified WORKMASTER 25S packages. Its website states that the backhoe fits the open-ROPS configuration rather than the cab version. Deere offers AutoConnect mower and compatible backhoe arrangements, with fitment controlled by the exact model, serial, mounts and dealer options. A tractor-only quote does not include all of these attachments by default.

Ownership and service support

Before choosing between two local dealers, compare complete out-the-door configurations including machine serial, tire/ballast setup, loader and quick-attachment system, mowing equipment, delivery, documented maintenance schedule and access to original parts. For a used Deere tractor, our 1025R filter-kit serial guide demonstrates why a model badge alone cannot establish parts compatibility.

Practical buying checklist

  1. Write down all intended implements and their required PTO power, shaft speed, hitch, and hydraulic flow.
  2. Compare current factory data at the same measurement point, not headline loader lifts.
  3. Confirm whether the quote includes the same type of mower, loader, bucket, front hitch and rear ballast.
  4. Ask the dealer to identify warranty, service and serial-specific parts support.
  5. Perform a safe test drive and check visibility, controls and operator access around your actual work.

For individual model source notes see New Holland WORKMASTER 25S specifications and John Deere 1025R specifications. The site's comparison tool displays only figures available in the reviewed dataset.

Original manufacturer references

New Holland WORKMASTER 25S and John Deere 1025R, official US model pages, checked November 23, 2026. This independent article does not certify any particular tractor, loader, mower or attachment combination.

records.title: Tractor ROPS & Seat Belt Safety: Rollover Prevention Checklist
records.excerpt: A practical US tractor rollover safety guide covering ROPS, seat belts, loader stability, hill hazards, pre-use inspections and buying used equipment.
records.content:
A tractor rollover can happen during ordinary work: turning near a ditch, crossing uneven ground, driving with a raised loader, or traveling on an incline. The most important protection is an approved rollover protective structure (ROPS) used together with the appropriate seat belt. The two parts work as a system, but protection depends on the tractor's configuration and the operator following the manual.

What ROPS can and cannot do

ROPS is an engineered protective frame or structure designed to help preserve a survival space in a rollover. It does not prevent every rollover, protect against every injury, or make an unsafe slope acceptable. For tractors equipped with an approved ROPS, OSHA emphasizes using the seat belt to help keep the operator inside the protected area. Never substitute a homemade frame or assume a canopy is certified rollover protection.

Should you wear a seat belt on an older tractor?

On a tractor with an approved, properly deployed ROPS, wear the provided seat belt. A tractor without ROPS presents a different safety situation; do not install or use a seat belt as an improvised solution without the manufacturer's approved rollover protection system. Ask the dealer or manufacturer whether a model-specific ROPS retrofit is available. Consult the manual for foldable ROPS operating positions and belt use; a folded structure is not equivalent to a correctly deployed one.

Before starting: a five-point safety inspection

  1. Check the ROPS for visible bending, cracks, unauthorized drilling, missing hardware, or improper folding. Do not repair structural damage by welding unless the manufacturer explicitly authorizes a repair procedure.
  2. Inspect the belt, buckle, anchorages and retractor for wear and secure operation. Replace damaged components with approved parts.
  3. Verify tire condition and pressure, steering, brakes, working lights and mirrors as appropriate for the site.
  4. Keep PTO shafts and machine guards installed and secure, and ensure people are clear of the equipment.
  5. Walk the work area first: look for holes, soft edges, washouts, debris, low branches and hidden slopes.

Loader work, hills and ditch edges

Keep loads low during travel and use manufacturer-specified ballast. An elevated front loader raises the center of gravity and can reduce stability, particularly during turns. Slow down before turns; avoid sudden braking or steering on uneven ground. Stay away from the edges of banks, culverts and ditches that may collapse under the tractor's weight. Never infer an acceptable working slope from a generic internet angle: tire type, ballast, implement, ground firmness, surface moisture and tractor design all matter.

PTO and dismounting precautions

Before leaving the operator's seat, follow the manual's shutdown procedure: lower attachments, disengage the PTO, set the parking brake, stop the engine and remove the key when appropriate. Wait for moving components to stop. Do not step over a turning PTO shaft or attempt to remove debris from moving equipment. Keep bystanders and children outside the working area.

Buying a used tractor: ROPS questions

QuestionWhat to verify
Is the frame a certified ROPS?Check manufacturer identification, model-specific documentation and mounting hardware.
Has the tractor rolled over before?Inspect for deformation and ask for repair records; a compromised structure may require replacement.
Is the belt serviceable?Examine webbing, buckle, anchors and correct approved replacement parts.
Can ROPS be retrofitted?Check the manufacturer or an authorized retrofit program for this exact model.
Does the loader change operation?Review approved ballast, load limits and operating instructions for the installed loader.

Questions owners often ask

Does four-wheel drive prevent a rollover?

No. Four-wheel drive improves traction in some conditions but does not remove rollover hazards.

Does a sunshade count as ROPS?

Not unless it is part of an approved rollover protective structure for that tractor.

Can I replace a ROPS bolt with one from the hardware store?

Use the manufacturer's specified hardware and tightening procedure. Fastener grades and installation requirements matter in a safety structure.

Authoritative references

Read OSHA's tractor safety guidance, OSHA's Rollover Protection and Operating Tractors Safely guide (PDF) and University of Minnesota Extension's tractor and roadway safety reference. The requirements for particular agricultural employers, tractor models and equipment vintages can differ. Check the current rules, the exact tractor operator's manual and your local operating conditions.

records.title: Tractor PTO Shaft Safety: Guards, Shutdown Steps & Inspection Checklist
records.excerpt: How to inspect tractor PTO shields, avoid rotating-shaft entanglement, and follow safer shutdown steps before servicing implements.
records.content:
A tractor power take-off (PTO) transfers rotating power to equipment such as rotary cutters, tillers, spreaders and balers. The driveline can remain dangerous even when an attachment appears to be operating normally. Loose clothing, drawstrings, hair and tools can become entangled in unguarded rotating parts. Do not operate equipment with missing or damaged PTO guards. Inspect the tractor master shield, driveline guard and implement input shielding before use.

Know the three areas that need protection

ComponentPurposeInspection question
Tractor PTO master shieldGuards the PTO output areaIs the shield present and correctly secured?
Implement driveline guardSeparates the rotating shaft and joints from the operatorIs the full guard intact, secured and functioning as intended?
Implement input shieldProtects the connection at the implement gearboxAre the original guards fitted without gaps caused by modification?

OSHA agricultural equipment rules address PTO guarding; the exact legal requirements and exemptions depend on the equipment and working arrangement. These checks are not a substitute for the manufacturer's illustrated guard assembly and operating instructions.

Before connecting the implement

  1. Park on firm, level ground and follow the tractor operator manual's stop-and-secure procedure. Turn off the engine, remove the key where directed, and wait for all movement to cease.
  2. Confirm that the implement is supported and cannot roll or drop unexpectedly.
  3. Inspect the shaft for damaged tubing, missing fasteners, worn yokes and damaged guards. Have a qualified technician assess any suspected damage.
  4. Compare tractor and implement PTO speed requirements in their manuals. A shaft rated for one operating speed must not be assumed suitable for another.
  5. Use the exact approved driveline length, overlap and safety devices for that tractor–implement combination. Incorrect length can cause bottoming or separation through hitch travel.
  6. Check that the coupler positively locks onto the PTO stub using the manufacturer's procedure. Confirm shielding is restored before starting.

When a PTO-driven attachment stops or jams

Never reach across, step over or touch a rotating shaft. Disengage the PTO, lower and secure the attachment, stop the engine, set the parking brake, remove the key when instructed and wait for complete stop before examining a blockage. Some implements store rotational or hydraulic energy after disengagement. Follow the implement-specific lockout and stored-energy instructions rather than assuming disengaging the PTO makes the machinery safe.

Problems that mean the equipment should stay out of service

  • A missing tractor master shield or a cut-away driveline cover.
  • A cracked, broken or loose guard that exposes rotating joints.
  • A shaft or coupler that does not remain properly secured.
  • Unusual vibration, impact damage or visible twisting of the driveline.
  • Uncertain PTO speed, shaft length or the implement manufacturer's compatibility requirements.

Replace damaged components with the specified parts. Do not fabricate makeshift covers or modify an approved shaft or guard to make it fit.

Does the PTO rating tell you which implement fits?

No. PTO horsepower is only one part of implement selection. Required shaft speed, PTO rotation, driveline series, three-point hitch geometry, shaft operating angles, tractor ballast, and implement manufacturer's minimum and maximum power limits also matter. See our engine HP versus PTO HP guide and tractor rollover-safety checklist.

Official safety references

Read OSHA Agricultural Operations: Hazards and Controls and 29 CFR 1928.57, Guarding of Farm Field Equipment. Consult the tractor and implement manufacturer's latest manuals for an exact inspection and assembly procedure. This guide deliberately does not specify a generic universal driveline size, torque or service interval.

records.title: Tractor & Combine Fire Prevention: Cleaning, Leaks and Field Safety Checklist
records.excerpt: A field-focused tractor and combine fire-prevention checklist covering crop debris, hot surfaces, fluid leaks, extinguisher checks, and shutdown safety.
records.content:
Dry crop material, dust, hot exhaust components, electrical faults and leaking fluids create serious fire hazards around tractors and combines. A preventive inspection should focus on where combustible debris collects, how quickly leaks are recognized and whether the operator can stop work safely. There is no universal cleaning interval: field dust, crop type, equipment condition and manufacturer instructions determine how often a machine needs attention.

High-priority areas to inspect

AreaLook forSafer next step
Engine bay and exhaustDry chaff, leaves or crop residue near hot componentsStop, cool and clean using the machine manual's approved method
Bearings and beltsUnusual noise, friction, wear, heat or debris accumulationRemove from service and investigate before operation
Fuel and hydraulic linesWet fittings, damaged hoses or fluid sprayed onto hot surfacesShut down and repair leaks; never search for hydraulic leaks with bare hands
Electrical systemFrayed wires, damaged insulation, loose connections or unapproved repairsHave wiring defects repaired to manufacturer specification
Operator stationBlocked exit, unavailable extinguisher or unclear emergency procedureRestore safe access and check equipment before work

Before harvesting or mowing dry vegetation

  1. Read the manufacturer's fire-prevention and daily inspection sections for the exact machine.
  2. Remove accumulated combustible debris from approved cleaning points while the machine is shut down and safe to work around.
  3. Inspect fuel, hydraulic and oil lines for leaks. Never use your hand to feel for pressurized hydraulic leaks; injected fluid requires emergency medical care.
  4. Check bearings, belts, pulleys, guards and rotating assemblies for damage or abnormal conditions.
  5. Verify that the specified fire extinguisher is accessible, charged and within its inspection requirements. Know how to use it and when to evacuate.
  6. Keep communications and a clear access route available, particularly when working remotely.

What to do if you notice smoke or fire

Stop operation if it can be done safely. Move away from the machine and call emergency services when necessary. Do not open compartments or attempt firefighting if doing so could expose you to flames, smoke, pressurized fluids or an escape-route hazard. Follow the machine operator manual and your farm's emergency procedures. Life safety takes priority over protecting equipment; an extinguisher is for a small, manageable incipient fire only if you have been trained and have a safe exit.

Cleaning frequency depends on conditions

In heavy chaff, dry weeds or dusty harvesting conditions, inspect and clean more often than the minimum routine schedule where the manufacturer's guidance calls for it. Do not spray water, compressed air or cleaning chemicals into sensitive components without confirming that method is approved. Hot exhaust, moving fans and rotating components introduce additional hazards during cleaning. Some equipment may require cool-down or electrical isolation steps before service.

After-work walkaround

When the machine is safely parked and shut down, look for fresh fluid marks, burnt odor, discoloration, unusual debris collection and damaged harnesses. Record problems for repair before the next shift. Inspect nearby storage areas for combustible material and ensure that fuel containers, chargers and maintenance supplies are handled according to local fire codes and manufacturer instructions.

Related equipment checks

See our preseason compact tractor maintenance checklist for a broader walkaround and the PTO shielding checklist for rotating machinery hazards. Owners comparing smaller tractors can use our model comparison tool to review the recorded manufacturer specifications.

Sources and limitations

This preventive guide draws on University of Minnesota Extension: Reducing Fire Risk on the Farm and Iowa State University Extension fire-prevention tips republished by UMN. Machine-specific cooling, cleaning, repair and extinguishing procedures belong in the official operator and service manuals.

records.title: Compact Tractor Clicks but Won't Crank: Battery, Starter & Safety Switch Checks
records.excerpt: A safe symptom-based checklist for a compact tractor that clicks when the key turns but the starter does not crank the engine.
records.content:
You turn the key on a compact diesel tractor and hear a click, but the engine does not rotate. That symptom is different from an engine that cranks normally but will not start. The first problem concerns the starting circuit and operating interlocks; the second may involve fuel supply, air, engine management or other systems. Separating the two avoids replacing a battery, starter or fuel filter without evidence.

Quick symptom chart

What happensPossible area to investigateSafe first check
Dash lights dim dramatically; repeated clickingLow battery state of charge or excessive electrical resistanceInspect battery condition and visible cable connections
One click; engine does not turnBattery cables, starter circuit, solenoid or seized mechanical loadStop repeated attempts and consult the model's starting-system procedure
No click and no normal dash responseBattery power, connections, fuse or main electrical feedCheck the battery and accessible fuses as directed by the manual
Engine rotates normally but never firesA separate crank-but-no-start conditionUse the cranks-but-won't-start guide

These are diagnostic possibilities, not a diagnosis for any particular tractor. Some electronic control systems produce different warning patterns and may have model-specific fault codes.

Step 1: Set the machine up safely

Move controls to their specified safe positions and follow the model operator manual. Keep bystanders clear, disengage the PTO, lower implements when possible and set the parking brake. Never bypass the seat, clutch, neutral or PTO safety interlocks, and never short the starter terminals to start the tractor. Do not start an engine inside a closed building because exhaust gases are hazardous. Kubota's official tractor safety guidance specifically calls for following the operator manual and avoiding enclosed-space operation.

Step 2: Look for obvious battery and cable problems

With the engine shut off and the key removed, inspect the battery case for damage and cables for loose or corroded connections, following the machine manual and battery safety directions. A battery may operate dashboard lights while lacking sufficient capacity to turn the starter under load. Visible corrosion or a loose ground strap can also restrict current. If the battery is damaged, leaking, swollen or frozen, stop and seek appropriate service; do not attempt to charge or jump-start it.

Step 3: Understand the difference between voltage and battery health

A voltage reading by itself is not a full battery-health test. Battery chemistry, temperature, state of charge, cable resistance and load affect starting performance. Use the manufacturer-approved battery test and charging procedures. A qualified technician can perform a load or conductance test, voltage-drop tests and charging-system inspection if a visual check does not resolve the issue. Do not apply a universal voltage threshold to every machine without first verifying its electrical system.

Step 4: Check normal start-permission conditions

Many tractors require specific transmission, PTO, clutch, brake or operator-presence conditions before cranking. Consult the exact model's starting instructions, not a wiring diagram from a different model year. If the dashboard indicates a safety-interlock problem, confirm controls are positioned correctly and contact a qualified technician for electrical diagnosis. Do not bridge, unplug or defeat an interlock to force a start.

Step 5: When to stop trying

  • Smoke, overheated wiring, a burning smell or repeated fuse failures.
  • Grinding, violent impacts or other abnormal starter noises.
  • Battery leakage, severe corrosion or a damaged harness.
  • Uncertain polarity, battery voltage or correct jump-start equipment.
  • A machine that could unexpectedly move or start while being tested.

Repeated cranking can heat the starter and discharge the battery. Follow the permitted crank duration and rest periods in the operator manual. A trained technician should investigate persistent failure rather than repeatedly energizing suspect wiring.

Can you jump-start a diesel compact tractor?

Only if the exact operator manual allows it and you can follow its battery voltage, equipment and connection instructions. John Deere publishes model-specific guidance for jump-starting; incorrect connections can damage electrical components or cause dangerous battery events. Never assume an automotive jump-start sequence is suitable for an unknown tractor. If in doubt, use a professional service technician.

Find model-specific information

For a Kubota BX2380 with a no-crank symptom, see our BX2380-specific starting checks. John Deere 1025R owners can start with the 1025R model reference and the correct serial-number-specific manual. Our preseason checklist covers preventive inspections.

Official sources and limits

Consult John Deere Manuals and Training, John Deere's jump-start guidance and Kubota's tractor safety instructions. No starter motor, battery, fuse or interlock part number is claimed compatible here without a model-specific parts catalog.

records.title: Compact Tractor Daily Pre-Operation Inspection: 20-Point Owner Checklist
records.excerpt: A daily tractor walkaround covering tires, hydraulic leaks, PTO guards, ROPS, seat belt, loader fittings, cooling air and warning lights before starting work.
records.content:
A compact tractor's daily inspection is a short way to identify visible damage before the machine is driven, a loader is raised or a PTO-powered implement is started. Different tractors require different daily checks, so this is a practical 20-point reminder, not a replacement for the exact machine operator manual or its hour-meter-based service schedule.

Before you start the engine: external walkaround

  1. Ground condition: look for fresh oil, coolant or fuel marks under the parked tractor.
  2. Engine compartment: look for damage, loose parts and accumulated dry debris near hot components.
  3. Engine oil: check the level by the model's specified method, temperature and position.
  4. Coolant: check the accessible recovery-tank level as instructed; never open a hot pressurized cooling system.
  5. Fuel: confirm adequate fuel and inspect for visible leaks or damaged lines.
  6. Hydraulic hoses: inspect for abrasion, leaks, swelling and insecure routing without touching suspected pressurized leaks.
  7. Hydraulic/transmission oil: verify the level using the manual's specific check method.
  8. Tires: look for visible damage and check specified inflation pressures when appropriate.
  9. Wheel hardware: watch for loose or missing fasteners; use the manufacturer's inspection and torque instructions.
  10. Steering and linkage: inspect visible components for damage, missing retainers and unusual play.
  11. ROPS: confirm that the approved rollover protection is in the required operating position and shows no apparent damage.
  12. Seat belt: inspect webbing, latch and anchors for proper condition.
  13. PTO guards: verify the tractor master shield and implement driveline guards are in place.
  14. Three-point hitch: inspect pins, retaining clips, stabilizers and implement attachment points.
  15. Loader: examine installed loader arms, couplers and visible attachment retainers if equipped.
  16. Battery: inspect for external damage, corrosion or visibly insecure connections with the machine off.
  17. Air intake and radiator screen: check for blocked screens or debris using the approved cleaning procedure.
  18. Lighting and reflectors: inspect for damage and cleanliness, especially before road travel.
  19. Operator area: clear loose objects from pedals and controls.
  20. Manual and emergency readiness: confirm the correct operator manual and site-specific emergency arrangements are available.

After starting: stop if a critical system fails

SystemFunctional observationIf abnormal
Warning indicatorsSelf-test and warnings behave as described in the manualStop according to the warning priority and identify the fault
Service brakes and parking brakeOperate correctly under the manufacturer's safe test procedureDo not use the tractor until corrected
SteeringResponds normally without binding or unusual noisesStop and investigate
Hydraulics and loaderNo abnormal motion, leak or warningLower equipment safely and obtain service
Engine and coolingNo abnormal temperature warning, smoke or unusual noiseFollow shutdown instructions and diagnose before operation

Keep hands, feet and clothing clear of moving components. Never test a malfunctioning seat interlock by deliberately standing, dismounting or bypassing safety devices while the machine is operating.

What changes for mowing, loader use or road travel?

For mowing, pay close attention to PTO guards, debris around the radiator and operator visibility. For loader work, check attachment couplers, rear ballast and the loader operator manual's limits; never rely on the tractor's headline horsepower to determine lifting capacity. For travel on a public road, verify the legal lighting, slow-moving vehicle marking and transport requirements in your jurisdiction, and follow the machine's road travel procedure.

Inspection frequency versus scheduled maintenance

A visual walkaround does not replace oil changes, filter replacement, lubrication, bolt-torque checks or other time- and hour-based maintenance. The schedule can vary by model, year, operating conditions and component. Keep a log of operating hours, work performed and issues found. Use our preseason maintenance checklist for a broader review and the PTO safety inspection for driven implements.

Safety reminders

Park on stable ground and shut off the machine before checking service points that require engine-off inspection. Follow lockout and attachment-support procedures in the official instructions. Hydraulic fluid under pressure can penetrate skin and requires immediate medical attention. Never inspect a hot radiator by loosening its pressure cap. If a critical safety component is missing or damaged, keep the tractor out of service until properly repaired.

Manufacturer references

These owner reminders draw on Kubota Maintenance Check Points, Kubota's equipment preparation checklist and John Deere's safety and pre-operation inspection resources. Check the exact model manual for inspection intervals, fluid levels and test conditions.

records.title: John Deere 1025R PTO Won't Engage: Safe Diagnostic Checklist
records.excerpt: John Deere 1025R PTO not engaging? Check operating setup, PTO selection, guards, warning indicators and model-specific manual instructions before buying parts.
records.content:
If the PTO on your John Deere 1025R will not engage, first separate an operating-condition issue from an electrical, linkage or implement problem. This guide is a safe, non-invasive troubleshooting path for owners. It does not identify a failed part from the symptom alone: a PTO that will not engage can have more than one cause, and the correct checks depend on the tractor's serial number, installed options and attachment.

First determine what is actually failing

Observed symptomWhat it could indicateInitial action
PTO does not engage with a particular mower or implementIncorrect attachment setup, selection or implement conditionStop and check both operator manuals
Nothing happens when the control is operatedOperating prerequisites, electrical control or interlockReview proper seated starting and operating procedure
Warning indicator or unexpected engine shutdownOperator-presence or control condition, or another faultRecord the warning and stop operation
Unusual noise or vibration during engagementDriveline or implement mechanical issueDisengage, shut down safely and request inspection

1. Identify the PTO and attachment configuration

The 1025R may be used with different rear- and mid-PTO-driven equipment. Do not assume that the same switch or selector position applies to every attachment configuration. Confirm whether you are trying to use the rear PTO, mid PTO or an attachment that requires a specified operating setup. Check the 1025R operator manual and the installed implement's manual for the exact engagement sequence and speed rating.

2. Review normal safety and control prerequisites

Before testing, park on level, firm ground, keep people clear of rotating equipment, lower attachments and follow the operator manual. Some operating conditions depend on seat occupancy and the position of other controls. Do not jumper, unplug or bypass seat switches, PTO switches or safety interlocks. Never try to watch an exposed rotating shaft from close range. Use the manufacturer's prescribed functional tests only.

3. Check for visible damage with the engine off

After stopping the engine, removing the key when instructed and waiting for all motion to cease, inspect only the areas accessible without dismantling safety equipment. Look for missing PTO shields, damaged implement drivelines, loose connectors visible from normal service positions or obvious damage after attachment changes. If a shaft is damaged, a guard is missing or a coupler is not securely seated, do not operate the implement until the problem is repaired.

4. Do not order a switch based on an internet part number

John Deere's parts catalog lists PTO-related switches and other control components; availability and compatibility must be checked against the specific machine's serial number and exact assembly. A product page mentioning the 1025R is not proof that the component matches every 1025R. Consult John Deere's PTO switch product reference and have a dealer verify fitment before purchase. No interchangeability claim is made here.

5. When a dealer or qualified mechanic is needed

  • The PTO remains inoperative after the correct operating sequence is confirmed.
  • A fuse repeatedly fails, a connector overheats or there is an electrical burning smell.
  • There is grinding, abnormal vibration, uncontrolled shaft motion or unexpected engagement.
  • The machine displays an unexplained warning, or the operator-presence system behaves abnormally.
  • Access to wiring, a clutch or internal driveline components would require guard removal or specialist tools.

Ask the technician to diagnose the problem using the applicable 1025R technical manual and serial-specific wiring diagram. Do not replace an expensive PTO clutch or switch without testing.

How this differs from an engine no-start fault

A tractor that starts and drives normally but has no PTO response is not the same as a tractor that fails to crank. See our compact tractor click/no-crank checklist for the latter issue. If you need more information about rated PTO output, visit the 1025R specification page and our PTO horsepower explanation.

Official references

The John Deere US 1025R product page provides the current model overview and attachment information. For the appropriate manual and technical instructions, start with John Deere Technical Information Store. Verify the tractor model, serial number and the installed implement before applying any procedure.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Running Hot While Mowing: Radiator Screen & Cooling Checks
records.excerpt: A Kubota BX2380 that gets hot during mowing needs safe cooling-system checks. Learn what to inspect before opening a radiator or replacing parts.
records.content:
A Kubota BX2380 that runs hotter while mowing than while idling deserves attention. Dust, grass clippings and airborne chaff can restrict cooling airflow, particularly in summer. But the symptom does not prove the radiator is blocked: low coolant, a damaged fan belt, a cooling-system fault, an incorrect operating condition or another issue can produce similar signs. Treat a temperature warning as a reason to stop according to the operator manual, not as permission to continue mowing.

Cooling system facts for the BX2380

Kubota's US BX2380 detailed specification describes a pressurized liquid-cooling system with a reverse air-flow radiator design and an enclosed, screened engine compartment. Those design features make keeping the correct air paths free of debris important, but they do not establish a universal cleaning procedure or a safe operating temperature for every condition. See the official BX2380 specification PDF.

Symptom-to-check table

What you noticePossible areaFirst safe response
Temperature rises during mowing in dry grassDebris restricting intake screens or cooling airflowStop and inspect approved screen access points after safe shutdown
Coolant stain or puddleLeak from a hose, reservoir or cooling componentDo not continue; arrange an inspection
Visible fan-belt damage or abnormal noiseDrive or cooling component faultKeep hands clear and have the machine serviced
Temperature warning persists after debris removalFault not solved by external cleaningStop work and seek model-specific diagnosis

1. Stop before the cooling system becomes a hazard

Follow the BX2380 operator manual for stopping work and shutting down following a high-temperature indication. Lower attachments and park securely. Keep clothing, tools and hands away from the fan and belts. Never loosen or remove a radiator pressure cap while the system is hot. Hot pressurized coolant can cause serious burns. Do not pour cold water over a hot engine.

2. Inspect screen and radiator airflow after shutdown

Once the machine is in the safe condition specified by the manual, inspect the accessible radiator screen, hood screens and surrounding air intake areas. Kubota's maintenance check points explicitly include cleaning radiator screens and cores, panel and hood screens, and the air cleaner's primary element where applicable. Use the cleaning method approved in the BX2380 manual. Avoid bending radiator fins or forcing debris deeper into the core.

3. Check coolant only as the manual permits

After the cooling system has cooled sufficiently for a safe check, verify the specified coolant reservoir level and visually inspect accessible hoses and fittings for stains or leaks. Do not treat adding coolant as a repair for repeated loss. Use the manufacturer's approved coolant type, mixture and filling procedure; mixing incompatible products or opening a pressurized system is unsafe.

4. Look beyond debris if symptoms continue

Cooling-system problems can also involve a worn drive belt, damaged fan, faulty thermostat, blocked radiator, coolant leakage or other engine and sensor issues. An abnormal temperature display may require instrument or sender diagnosis. Those possibilities cannot be distinguished reliably from one symptom. If cleaning approved screens and the prescribed basic checks do not resolve the problem, seek a qualified technician rather than dismantling the system while hot.

Preventing repeat overheating during mowing

  1. Inspect radiator and hood screens at the frequency specified for dusty or chaff-heavy work.
  2. Keep the area around the engine compartment clear of loose dry grass and oil-contaminated material.
  3. Check fluids and inspect for leaks before work using the daily tractor walkaround.
  4. Record the operating hours, warning indication and conditions when the symptom appears.
  5. Use the correct mower, operating procedure and engine speed from the tractor and implement manuals.

Related BX2380 information

Compare engine and machine specifications on the BX2380 model page. For seasonal servicing, see the BX80 service schedule overview and the general tractor overheating checklist. Avoid interpreting general engine advice as a substitute for the exact tractor manual.

Manufacturer references

Use Kubota USA Maintenance Check Points, BX2380 Detailed Specifications, and My Kubota Support to locate the applicable operator manual. This guide intentionally gives no unverified capacity, thermostat specification or temperature threshold.

records.title: Diesel Compact Tractor Hard to Start in Cold Weather: Battery, Fuel & Preheat Checks
records.excerpt: A winter diagnostic checklist for diesel compact tractors that struggle to start: battery performance, winter fuel, preheat, coolant heaters and safe next steps.
records.content:
When a diesel compact tractor is difficult to start on a freezing morning, the cause might be a weak battery, thickened fuel, poor electrical connections, an incorrect cold-start procedure, or a mechanical condition that only becomes apparent in low temperatures. First determine whether the engine cranks slowly, cranks normally without firing, or does not crank at all. These are different symptoms. Do not buy a glow plug, starter, battery or fuel filter on the basis of the weather alone.

Cold-weather symptom guide

SymptomPossible issueSafe first step
Slow cranking and dim instrument lightsCold or discharged battery; cable resistanceInspect battery and connections according to manual
Strong cranking but engine does not fireFuel condition, cold-start/preheat system, or another engine issueCheck fuel suitability and prescribed starting sequence
Starts briefly, then loses powerPossible fuel restriction or other supply problemStop repeated starts; inspect as specified by manufacturer
