More ranges do not automatically make a tractor faster or easier to control under load; test the real pedal response and ground-speed selection for mowing, loader work and your terrain.

Buying decision by job type

Regular mowing and rotary cutter work

Compare PTO ratings with the chosen cutter's manual, then examine tractor clearance, weight, turning room, tire type and ground impact. In uneven or wet terrain, traction and safe operating technique can matter more than a narrow horsepower difference.

Loader, forks and gravel work

Compare the specific front loader, mounting and attachment package. Loader lift at a bucket pivot is different from lift measured farther forward; pallet forks extend the load center. Confirm the required ballast, tire inflation, loader operating envelope and safe travel procedure. Our quick-attach and pallet fork checklist covers common fitment pitfalls.

Serviceability and long-term ownership

Ask each local dealer about serial-specific parts, routine filter costs, maintenance access, warranty terms, included manuals and service turnaround. The cheapest purchase quote is not necessarily the best ownership value. Avoid ranking reliability without comparable long-term data.

Before signing a quote

  1. Record model year, serial identification and exact transmission configuration for all three tractors.
  2. Get an itemized quote with identical attachment functions, tires and ballast where possible.
  3. Compare PTO requirements, hitch geometry and published loader capacities at matching load centers.
  4. Verify attachments and third-function kits in the OEM fitment catalog.
  5. Try operator access, visibility, seat comfort, forward/reverse travel and service access.
  6. Confirm scheduled maintenance and current dealer support for the actual machine.

Original manufacturer references

John Deere's May 2026 factory tractor specification list, Kubota's US L02 specification PDF, and KIOTI's official CK3520H page underpin this comparison. Values were cross-checked against the site's model reference records. Product revisions and region-specific offerings require confirmation before purchasing.

records.title: 25 HP vs 35 HP Compact Tractor: PTO Power, Weight, Loader & Property Size
records.excerpt: Understand how real compact tractors around 25 and 35 engine horsepower differ in PTO power, hitch ratings, operating mass and attachment suitability.
records.content:
Is a 25-horsepower compact tractor enough, or is a 35-horsepower machine worth the increase in size and ownership cost? The answer depends more on your implements, ground conditions and tractor configuration than on acreage alone. Horsepower classes are rough labels: the practical figures are PTO horsepower, available implement flow, hitch and loader capacity, machine weight, dimensions and the exact attachment requirements.

Why the 25 HP label can be misleading

Engine horsepower is often the most prominent brochure rating, but PTO-driven mowers and rotary cutters use power delivered to the PTO shaft, not the engine's gross figure. For example, the Kubota L2502 HST 4WD in our sourced US record lists 24.8 gross engine hp but 19.0 PTO hp. The L3302 HST lists 33.0 gross engine hp and 26.1 PTO hp. They should not be described as interchangeable 25- and 35-PTO-horsepower tractors. A specific implement's operator manual gives its required PTO power range.

Example: two configurations from the same manufacturer

Manufacturer-listed valueKubota L2502 HST 4WDKubota L3302 HST 4WD
Gross engine power24.8 hp33.0 hp
PTO power19.0 hp26.1 hp
Hitch lift at 24 in1,389 lb1,433 lb
ROPS tractor weight2,833 lb2,921 lb
Rear PTO speed540 rpm540 rpm

These figures come from specific US Kubota L02 specification editions in the catalog. They show why a much larger jump in engine horsepower does not imply an equally large change in rear hitch capacity. The PTO power gap is also quite different from the engine horsepower gap. Configuration, model year, loader and tire options can affect comparison.

Questions to ask for mowing and brush cutting

Check the cutter's minimum and maximum rated PTO horsepower, recommended tractor weight, working width, hitch category, driveline shaft speed and guarding. A narrow mower may be a better choice for tight or wooded property even if the tractor could power a wider one. Consider low branches, slopes, soft soil, ground clearance and storage. Our 540 versus 1000 rpm PTO guide explains why speed and driveline requirements should not be guessed.

For front loader and pallet fork work

More engine power does not directly establish the loader's lifting capacity. Compare the specific loader's capacity at the same measured load center and height, attachment weight, rear ballast, front axle rating, tire pressure and ground conditions. A properly ballasted tractor may handle a task more safely than a more powerful one using an inappropriate attachment or setup. See tire and ballast considerations and quick-attach fork fitment.

What about tractor weight?

Weight influences traction, hauling and soil impact, but it is not a universal measure of stability or capability. Tractor weight published without attachments is not the actual transport weight with a loader, liquid ballast and rear implement. A small property with sensitive turf may favor different tires and a lighter machine, while heavy ground-engaging tasks may call for an appropriate heavier chassis and tire setup. Check the permitted loading and safety requirements.

Acreage does not choose a tractor by itself

Five acres of regularly mowed lawn and five acres of rough pasture are very different work. Consider the hours of mowing, terrain, obstacles, snow, gravel, landscaping projects and travel distance. A tractor with slightly less horsepower but better matched implements and accessible local servicing may be more valuable than a larger machine that cannot maneuver around your buildings.

Budget for the whole equipment package

Get quotes for the tractor, loader, mower, ballast, quick-hitch hardware, approved tires and needed hydraulic controls. Include maintenance consumables and dealer service. If buying used, check the model and serial number, inspect fluids and leaks, and review documented maintenance. Our used compact tractor inspection guide is a starting point.

Practical comparison checklist

  1. List every task and the exact implements you intend to use.
  2. Check each implement's PTO horsepower, hitch type and minimum tractor mass.
  3. Compare tractors using matched transmission and source editions.
  4. Verify loader capacity at equivalent load centers, not just headline numbers.
  5. Compare true storage and transport dimensions and equipped weight.
  6. Check traction, ballast, tires, local dealer coverage and ownership costs.
  7. Choose the machine whose entire configuration matches your work, not an arbitrary acreage-to-horsepower rule.

Official specification reference

Kubota USA L02 specifications provide source-edition power, hitch and weight figures for comparable HST variants. The exact owner manual and implement specifications remain the deciding references for safe equipment fitment. No universal recommendation, current price or ownership-cost estimate is claimed.

records.title: John Deere 3025E vs Kubota L2502 HST vs KIOTI CK2620H: 25 HP Tractor Comparison
records.excerpt: Compare three roughly 25-hp US compact tractors: engine and PTO horsepower, HST ranges, hitch capacity, weight, hydraulic pump figures and loader fitment limitations.
records.content:
If you are shopping in the roughly 25-horsepower compact tractor class, the John Deere 3025E, Kubota L2502 HST 4WD and KIOTI CK2620H are worth comparing. All offer hydrostatic transmission configurations for loader and property-maintenance work, but they are not identical in size, published PTO power or hydraulic reporting. This guide is built around documented US specifications for particular model editions, not unsourced owner claims or an invented ranking.

Three-way compact tractor specification chart

SpecificationDeere 3025EKubota L2502 HST 4WDKIOTI CK2620H
Published engine horsepower24.7 hp gross24.8 hp gross24.5 hp
Published PTO horsepower19.4 hp19.0 hp18.7 hp
TransmissionTwo-range hydrostaticThree-range hydrostaticThree-range hydrostatic
Rear PTO speed540 rpm540 rpm540 rpm
Rear hitch categoryCategory 1SAE Category ICategory 1
Three-point lift at 24 inches1,356 lb, older dealer-published figure; confirm serial1,389 lb in cited HST brochureNo comparable 24-inch rating established here
Hydraulic pump rating5.3 gpm implement + 4.0 steering5.2 gpm main + 3.1 steering11.7 gpm published pump capacity; circuit split not established
Published tractor weightNot established in matched source edition2,833 lb, ROPS model2,689 lb, published tractor weight

The table deliberately distinguishes manufacturer-listed implement/main pump flow from combined or unspecified pump output. The numbers in the same row are not necessarily measured at the same circuit. Deere 3025E hydraulic data are from the cited factory configuration; Kubota's figure refers to the US HST 4WD edition; KIOTI's pump figure is not a promise of available third-function flow.

Is 19.4 PTO HP meaningfully better than 18.7?

The difference between the top and bottom published PTO ratings in this set is 0.7 hp. The implement manufacturer sets the minimum PTO rating needed to operate safely and as intended. For a rotary cutter, snowblower, tiller or wood chipper, verify PTO rpm, minimum/maximum power, attachment mass, hitch geometry and ground conditions. A tractor's engine horsepower should not be substituted for PTO horsepower. See our engine vs PTO power explanation.

Two HST ranges or three?

The Deere 3025E has two hydrostatic travel ranges in its source configuration, while the Kubota and KIOTI list three. Hydrostatic pedals can simplify frequent forward/reverse direction changes, especially while using a loader. However, a third range is not automatically proof of superior travel speed or pushing performance. Ask to test each tractor with the intended work and attachment; actual ground speed, tires, gearing and usable engine torque matter.

Hydraulic flow: be careful about comparing GPM

Manufacturers do not always display hydraulic performance using the same terminology. The John Deere reference separates 5.3 US gpm of implement pump flow and 4.0 steering. The cited Kubota L2502 HST record lists 5.2 gpm main and 3.1 steering. The CK2620H catalog record lists a larger 11.7-gpm pump-capacity number but does not establish identical flow at an external hydraulic outlet. Do not declare KIOTI's third-function circuit faster solely from the 11.7 figure. Attachments also depend on operating pressure, valve restrictions, couplers and mounting configuration. See our hydraulic flow and implement circuits guide.

Hitch capacity: use the same load location

For tractor and implement fitment, published lift at the link ends can differ substantially from lift rated 24 inches behind them. Kubota documents 1,389 lb at 24 inches for the L2502 HST source configuration. Deere's 1,356 lb number appears in dealer documentation associated with other editions and should be verified for the exact 3025E year and serial number. Our CK2620H record does not substantiate a matching 24-inch rating, so it is not ranked here. A rear attachment's center of mass and top-link setup can further affect its compatibility. Read the hitch measurement guide.

Loader, forks and grapple work

Before choosing a tractor for lifting gravel or moving pallets, compare the installed loader model, not the tractor horsepower. Check the rated lift at matching load centers and lift heights, maximum loader and tractor constraints, attachment weight and required ballast. A pallet fork can shift the load farther forward than a standard bucket. Deere publishes a 300E loader compatible with the 3025E, but a loader listing is not sufficient evidence for every serial/attachment configuration. See our quick-attach attachment checklist.

Questions to ask a dealer

  1. Which exact model year, engine emission package and serial/PIN will be supplied?
  2. What is the installed loader model and its rated lift at the specified load center?
  3. What rear ballast, tire pressure and implement weight limits apply?
  4. Are the mower, rotary cutter or snowblower and PTO shaft approved for this setup?
  5. What hydraulic outlets or third-function controls are installed, and what flow is available there?
  6. Can the dealer supply the correct operator, loader and service manuals?
  7. What are the scheduled maintenance requirements and local parts-service arrangements?

Which should you buy?

None can responsibly be called the universal winner from a specification table alone. The Deere offers a documented 19.4 PTO hp for its 2026 factory configuration. Kubota's sourced L2502 HST combines a three-range hydrostatic transmission with 19.0 PTO hp. KIOTI's CK2620H offers a three-range hydrostatic transmission with its own attachment options and 18.7 PTO hp in the cited source record. Consider available dealer support, physical fit, implements, price quotes and warranty conditions before making a purchase decision.

Manufacturer sources and configuration caveats

Sources: John Deere's May 2026 factory tractor specification document; Kubota USA full-product-line brochure, L2502 HST 4WD column; and KIOTI's CK2620H model listing. Data checked against manufacturer-backed model records on November 23, 2026. Current selling configurations may differ. No current price, long-term reliability test or interchangeability claim is implied.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 1M.25 is a compact tractor listed in the manufacturer's current US M Series lineup. The official table specifies 24.8 rated engine hp, but lists different PTO horsepower values for the platform and cab configurations. That difference matters if you are sizing a powered mower, rotary cutter or other attachment. This model reference keeps those variants separate instead of inserting a misleading universal PTO horsepower figure.

MF 1M.25 US specification table

Published measureManufacturer value
Rated engine power24.8 hp
PTO power, platform18.2 hp
PTO power, cab16.9 hp
Rear three-point lift, 24 inches behind1,058 lb
Loader capacity at max height, 19.5 inches ahead of pivot852 lb, published factory configuration
ROPS machine weight2,172 lb
Cab machine weight2,502 lb
Height, ROPS97.0 in
Height, cab81.9 in

These figures are from the current US Massey Ferguson M Series comparison table and are not an independent field test. The manufacturer cautions that weight varies with tire selection and transmission choice. We do not assume the quoted loader capacity is available with every attachment, tire set or ballast combination.

Why the platform and cab PTO ratings differ

Massey Ferguson lists 18.2 PTO hp for the platform and 16.9 PTO hp for the cab. An implement manufacturer may specify a minimum shaft horsepower requirement, so compare it to the actual equipped model, not just the headline 24.8 engine horsepower. Engine and PTO ratings describe different points in the powertrain. Learn more in our engine HP versus PTO HP guide.

Hitch and loader values use different test positions

The quoted 1,058-lb three-point lift capacity is measured at 24 inches behind the hitch. The 852-lb loader figure refers to maximum height at a position 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin. Those numbers do not refer to the same lifting mechanism or test. A longer fork attachment moves the load center farther forward and changes what can be lifted safely. Read hitch lift measurement and loader quick-attach compatibility.

ROPS versus cab

The manufacturer's table identifies 2,172 lb for the ROPS tractor and 2,502 lb for the cab model, both subject to actual configuration. The cab option may help with cold-weather work and shelter from the elements, but check door clearance and overall height at your storage building. A loaded implement or front loader can increase real transport weight significantly. Do not use the listed tractor-only weight to select trailer, tiedown or tow ratings.

Which jobs make sense to evaluate?

For mowing, start with implement PTO requirements and the site's turning clearance. For loader jobs, check the precise loader and bucket option, approved ballast and tires. For snow removal, compare cab, illumination, suitable chains and attachment offerings. For quick-hitch implements, verify geometry and any required bushings; our Category 1 quick-hitch guide covers common fitment misunderstandings.

Owner and buyer checklist

  1. Identify platform versus cab and record the tractor's serial/PIN.
  2. Request the actual transmission, loader and tire configuration from the selling dealer.
  3. Use the relevant PTO rating for the specific model supplied.
  4. Verify attachment fitment, hitch geometry and loader test location.
  5. Check total equipped weight, ballast and site storage clearance.
  6. Confirm manuals, routine parts and local service arrangements.

Related Massey Ferguson models

Compare the larger MF 1M.35, whose available PTO ratings and rated hitch lift differ significantly, and the GC1725M sub-compact for a lighter class of tractor. See also the MF 1M.25 versus 1M.35 comparison.

Official US source

Massey Ferguson MF M Series specifications, reviewed November 23, 2026. Manufacturer model and equipment data are subject to revision; the operator manual and dealer fitment listing for the actual serial number control safe equipment selection.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 1M.35 is part of the current American MF M Series compact tractor range. The company's US model chart lists 36.2 rated engine horsepower, but differentiates PTO output by transmission: 27.5 PTO hp with the mechanical drivetrain and 25.7 PTO hp with the hydrostatic drivetrain. These are distinct configurations. The machine's loader and hitch figures also use stated measurement points, making this model useful for careful comparisons with other compact utility tractors.

MF 1M.35 official specifications

SpecificationPublished value
Rated engine horsepower36.2 hp
PTO horsepower, mechanical27.5 hp
PTO horsepower, HST25.7 hp
Three-point lift 24 in behind hitch2,535 lb
Max loader lift at max height, 19.5 in forward of pivot1,870 lb, manufacturer-listed configuration
Weight, ROPS3,428 lb
Weight, cab3,869 lb
Height, ROPS99.2 in
Height, cab91.3 in

These are model-table ratings from Massey Ferguson North America. The manufacturer states that weight can vary with tire selection and transmission choice. No fixed hydraulic output, fuel capacity or exact engine model is inferred where the model-specific table does not provide it.

Mechanical versus HST power

The published PTO gap between the mechanical and HST configurations is 1.8 horsepower. That matters only in context: a tractor's PTO power must match the attached implement's minimum and maximum operating requirements, and the transmission is also chosen for the work pattern. HST may be convenient for frequent reversals during loading or landscaping; a mechanical transmission may suit other duty cycles and operator preferences. Check the actual dealer configuration before selecting implements. See engine horsepower versus PTO horsepower.

Hitch lifting at 24 inches

Massey Ferguson publishes a 2,535-lb rear lift rating at 24 inches behind the hitch. That measurement is different from a capacity measured directly at the lift-arm ends. Implement geometry, stability and tractor ballast still matter. A published hydraulic lift maximum is not approval to lift or transport an arbitrary implement of the same mass. See hitch lift reference positions.

Loader capacity is not pallet-fork capacity

The 1,870-lb maximum loader number is defined at maximum lift height, 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin in the manufacturer table. If a forked pallet's center of gravity is farther out, the figure cannot be treated as the pallet's permitted weight. Confirm the actual loader assembly and attachment, approved ballast, fork rating and the manufacturer's load chart. Review our quick-attach and fork guide and tire pressure and ballast reference.

ROPS and cab planning

The table lists 3,428 lb for ROPS and 3,869 lb for cab, excluding any assumption of a specific loader or filled tires. Make sure garage door height and transport equipment accommodate the actual delivered tractor. Heating, air conditioning and weather protection options may differ with equipment packages; the dealer should confirm them in the sales quotation. Always follow the operator manual's ROPS and seat belt instructions.

Who should consider this model?

Owners needing greater published lift capacity than a smaller compact might evaluate the MF 1M.35 for approved loader and three-point attachments. However, a larger model has trade-offs in cost, size, transport mass and maneuvering. Compare actual implement dimensions and required PTO power, dealer support and service arrangements rather than selecting a winner solely from gross engine horsepower.

Inspection and dealer checklist

  1. Confirm the model name and exact mechanical or HST transmission.
  2. Verify ROPS or cab package and published dimensions for the chosen equipment.
  3. Request the approved loader and attachment list for the serial number.
  4. Compare loads using the same test distance and height.
  5. Check axle limits, proper ballast and tires for the actual use.
  6. Review owner manuals, maintenance intervals and replacement parts.

Compare related machines

Read the MF 1M.25 versus 1M.35 buying comparison or review the smaller MF 1M.25 model. Buyers considering other roughly 35-hp compact tractors can consult KIOTI CK3520H specifications and Kubota L3302 HST specifications, but must account for differing published test points.

Manufacturer documentation

Official Massey Ferguson M Series US specifications, checked November 23, 2026. Review the current manual and dealer's confirmed build sheet before making a safe purchase or attachment-fitment decision.

records.title: Massey Ferguson MF 1M.25 vs 1M.35: PTO, Lift, Weight & Cab Comparison
records.excerpt: Side-by-side official US specs for Massey Ferguson MF 1M.25 and MF 1M.35, including configuration-specific PTO power, rear lift, loader ratings and machine weight.
records.content:
Should you buy the Massey Ferguson MF 1M.25 or move up to the MF 1M.35? Massey Ferguson's current US lineup gives enough detail for a meaningful comparison, as long as platform, cab and transmission differences are not hidden. The smaller model lists 24.8 rated engine hp, while the 1M.35 lists 36.2 hp. But horsepower is not the only difference: the manufacturer publishes substantially different hitch and loader lift numbers at defined test positions.

Side-by-side US model specifications

Factory figureMF 1M.25MF 1M.35
Rated engine power24.8 hp36.2 hp
PTO output18.2 platform / 16.9 cab hp27.5 mechanical / 25.7 HST hp
Rear lift at 24 in behind hitch1,058 lb2,535 lb
Max loader capacity at maximum height, 19.5 in ahead of pivot852 lb1,870 lb
ROPS listed weight2,172 lb3,428 lb
Cab listed weight2,502 lb3,869 lb
ROPS height97.0 in99.2 in
Cab height81.9 in91.3 in

Configuration note: the PTO columns describe different variant distinctions, not a universal platform-versus-platform power test. Massey Ferguson labels MF 1M.25 values by platform versus cab, and MF 1M.35 by mechanical versus HST drive. The published loader figures are not certified pallet capacities. Manufacturer weight varies with tires and transmission, so neither the ROPS nor cab number is a guaranteed equipped transport mass.

How much additional PTO horsepower is available?

A 1M.25 platform lists 18.2 PTO hp, compared with 25.7 for the 1M.35 HST model and 27.5 for the 1M.35 mechanical version. These values may determine which powered attachment can meet an implement manufacturer's minimum requirement. They do not tell you the implement's permissible width or weight without its manual. The correct rear PTO shaft speed and driveline coupling must also match. Our PTO speed guide explains why shaft speed and power are separate.

Loader capacity is not the same as hydraulic flow

The 1M.35's official loader number is higher than the 1M.25's, at the same stated forward reference position and maximum height in the manufacturer comparison. That supports comparing the listed loader configuration, but not a claim that the same increase applies to pallet forks, grapples or different load centers. Ask the dealer for the exact attachment model, lifting height, forward reach, ballast and rated capacity. Read loader attachment compatibility.

Rear hitch capacity can change the implement choices

The MF 1M.25 lists 1,058 lb at 24 inches behind the hitch, compared with 2,535 lb for the 1M.35. Those figures refer to the rear three-point assembly, not the front loader. Check hitch category, implement length, center of gravity, required top-link geometry and safe transport with ballast. A numerical hitch rating alone does not prove any one attachment fits. See how hitch ratings are measured.

Which model fits your property?

The smaller 1M.25 may suit an owner placing high value on a lighter tractor, tighter storage and relatively modest implement requirements. The larger 1M.35 deserves attention for tasks requiring more rated PTO output and a higher published rear hitch capacity. Yet its greater base mass and height can affect transport, turf work and maneuvering. Evaluate terrain, hours of work, storage access and the actual equipment quote rather than choosing by acreage alone.

Buyer questions before ordering

  1. Is the exact 1M.25 offered as platform or cab, and which PTO rating applies?
  2. Is the 1M.35 configured with mechanical transmission or HST?
  3. What loader model is included, and at which load center are its limits published?
  4. Do the hitch category, lift geometry and required implement clearance match your tools?
  5. What is the final weight with tires, ballast, cab and attachments?
  6. Which local dealer can supply service, consumables and serial-specific parts?

Sources and limitations

All numeric values are from Massey Ferguson North America's MF M Series product specifications, checked November 23, 2026. Manufacturer ratings do not amount to an independent handling, lifting, reliability or cost comparison. Check the actual dealer configuration and machine's serial-specific operator manual before purchase.

No universal fluid, PTO rpm or circuit hydraulic flow claimed.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 1M.40 is the 39.4-horsepower member of the US MF 1M compact tractor lineup. The manufacturer lists 30.0 PTO hp for its mechanical transmission and 27.9 PTO hp for its HST configuration. Buyers need to identify which drivetrain they are purchasing before matching rotary cutters, PTO-powered snowblowers or other implements.

US published specifications

PTO output, mechanical30.0 hp

Max loader capacity, max height, 19.5 inches forward of pivot1,870 lb

Overall height, cab91.3 in

These are manufacturer's US specification-table values rather than tested figures for a particular dealership package. Massey Ferguson notes that weights vary by tire and transmission configuration. Do not use the tractor-only weight as the loaded trailer transport weight.

Mechanical transmission versus HST PTO horsepower

The mechanical model's listed PTO output is 2.1 hp higher than the HST number. This is a published configuration difference, not a reliability or fuel-consumption comparison. Consider PTO-powered implement requirements, work patterns, operator preference and service support. A hydrostatic tractor may be convenient for repeated reversing during loader work, while a mechanical transmission can suit a different duty cycle. Match implements using PTO hp rather than engine hp, and check the exact shaft speed and splines in the operator manual. For context see engine and PTO horsepower explained.

Three-point hitch rating and loader capacity

The three-point hitch lift of 2,535 lb is rated at 24 inches behind the hitch, rather than at the lift-arm ends. The separately published loader figure of 1,870 lb is rated at maximum height, 19.5 inches forward of the pivot. These are different mechanisms and measurement positions. Neither number guarantees that an arbitrary pallet, round bale or implement is safe to carry. Refer to our hitch capacity reference and loader quick-attach guidance.

Cab, size and transporting

Massey Ferguson lists 3,428 lb for ROPS and 3,869 lb for cab, before assuming the weight of added front loaders, liquid ballast or implements. The cab model's published height is 91.3 inches, and the ROPS model is listed at 99.2 inches. Garage-door height, trailer clearance, low branches and machine attachments should all be considered in advance. Check the delivered machine's true dimensions and weight.

What to compare before buying

  1. Request the actual transmission, cab/ROPS package and machine serial number.
  2. Verify the selected loader model, attachment weight and measured load center.
  3. Check the specific tractor PTO rating against the implement manual.
  4. Confirm ballast, tire type, approved 3-point hitch geometry and hydraulic options.
  5. Compare routine service items and dealer support in your area.

Related MF tractors

The MF 1M.35 shares the same manufacturer-listed rear hitch and loader ratings in the US comparison table, but has different engine and PTO power. Our MF 1M.35 versus 1M.40 comparison explains those differences. Owners comparing smaller machines can start with the MF 1M.25.

Manufacturer source

Massey Ferguson M Series, US technical specifications, checked November 23, 2026. Confirm model year and installed configuration before using any values for purchasing or implement fitment.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 2M.50 moves into a larger compact utility category than the MF 1M tractors. The current American product specification table lists a 48.8-hp rated engine and separates both PTO power and three-point hitch lift by transmission. That distinction matters when comparing implement requirements or loader-equipped configurations.

Official MF 2M.50 specifications

Rated engine horsepower48.8 hp

PTO hp, HST36.2 hp

These values refer to US manufacturer-listed configurations. Weight can vary with tires and transmission, and adding loaders, implements, ballast or fuel changes the actual equipped mass. Loader ratings require the exact measurement location and model to be applied correctly.

Why transmission choice changes more than driving style

Massey Ferguson lists 38.1 hp PTO for the mechanical configuration versus 36.2 hp PTO for HST. It also shows 3,307 lb rear lift at 24 inches for the mechanical tractor and 3,086 lb for HST. These are concrete published differences but not independent tests of either model. For a PTO-driven mower, chipper or rotary tiller, check the implement's allowed shaft horsepower, rpm, hitch and mass. For loader operations, also consider forward/reverse ease and the dealer's installed control package.

Hitch ratings: compare measurement positions

The manufacturer's three-point hitch figures use a 24-inch rearward test position. These are not equivalent to a lift rating reported at the ends of the lower arms. A long implement can move its center of mass farther rearward and affect the safe working arrangement. Read our three-point lift measurement guide for how to interpret these ratings.

Loader capacity and ballast

The manufacturer gives a loader figure of 1,880 lb at maximum height and 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin. This is a specific factory reference measurement rather than a promise that a 1,880-lb pallet can be lifted on any installed forks. Confirm bucket or tine mass, rated fork load, effective load center and the official loader chart. Approved ballast and tires are necessary for the actual work. See ballast and tire pressure explained.

Cab and ROPS weight planning

The ROPS tractor is listed at 4,035 lb; cab, 4,398 lb. Actual transport weight can be materially higher with filled tires, a loader and rear implement. The manufacturer's published heights are 102.4 inches ROPS and 92.9 inches cab. Check storage clearances, branch heights and the complete trailer and tow vehicle limitations. Do not size transport equipment by an unqualified brochure weight alone.

Questions to ask the dealer

  1. Which exact transmission and cab/ROPS variant is offered?
  2. Which PTO and rear hitch numbers apply to that machine?
  3. What loader model and factory-approved attachments are installed?
  4. Are hydraulic remotes, third-function equipment or quick-hitch options included?
  5. What is the delivery-ready weight including tires and ballast?
  6. Can the dealer provide serial-specific service, operator and parts documentation?

Related machines

The MF 1M.40 is a smaller machine in the same North American product family. Its engine rating is lower, and the published hydraulic hitch figures belong to a different class. See MF 1M.35 and the general compact tractor horsepower guide for additional purchasing context.

Manufacturer reference

records.title: Massey Ferguson MF 1M.35 vs MF 1M.40: Is More Horsepower Worth It?
records.excerpt: Compare Massey Ferguson MF 1M.35 and 1M.40 US engine and PTO horsepower, lift capacity, weight and transmission options using manufacturer measurements.
records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 1M.35 and MF 1M.40 sit next to one another in the manufacturer's US compact tractor lineup. The big difference in their published table is the available engine and PTO power. Their listed rear hitch, loader and basic ROPS/cab weight ratings are identical in the model comparison. That can make the 1M.40 worth evaluating if your intended implements require more PTO output, but it does not make the higher-horsepower machine automatically better for every job.

Side-by-side source specifications

MF US factory ratingMF 1M.35MF 1M.40
Rated engine hp36.239.4
PTO hp, mechanical27.530.0
PTO hp, HST25.727.9
Rear lift at 24 inches2,535 lb2,535 lb
Loader max at max height, 19.5 inches forward of pivot1,870 lb1,870 lb
ROPS tractor weight3,428 lb3,428 lb
Cab tractor weight3,869 lb3,869 lb
Cab overall height91.3 in91.3 in

These figures are from the manufacturer's US M Series table, not a comparison of every accessory configuration. The published weights vary depending on tire and transmission selection. No fluid capacity, price or fuel-consumption advantage is inferred from the horsepower difference.

How much PTO power does the 1M.40 add?

The mechanical 1M.40 is listed at 30.0 PTO hp, versus 27.5 for the mechanical 1M.35: a 2.5-hp published difference. For HST, the ratings are 27.9 and 25.7 hp, respectively: a 2.2-hp difference. Choose the version that matches your implement's actual rating rather than comparing the mechanical specification on one model to the HST specification on another. The engine versus PTO horsepower guide explains why these ratings matter for power-driven attachments.

Same published hitch lift does not mean every implement fits

Both models list 2,535 lb three-point hitch lift capacity at 24 inches behind the hitch. The geometry, center of gravity, hitch category, required ballast and the attachment's own requirements remain critical. The larger engine number does not increase the manufacturer-listed rear lift figure. Read our hitch lift explainer before using a seller's headline number to choose a heavy implement.

What about front loader work?

The factory comparison lists 1,870 lb at maximum loader height, 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin for both tractors. Those numbers do not authorize an arbitrary pallet or round-bale mass at a different effective load center. Loader model, bucket or fork weight, tire capacity, hydraulic options and rear ballast all matter. See quick-attach and pallet fork safety.

Mechanical or HST transmission?

HST is useful to consider when a tractor changes directions frequently; mechanical transmission may be preferred for other conditions. Neither is universally better. Compare actual test drives, field task requirements, maneuvering and operator comfort. Both models have PTO figures specific to the drivetrain. Ask for the complete build specification before ordering a PTO implement.

When does the extra power matter?

If the planned rotary cutter, tiller or snow-removal attachment has an official PTO requirement that fits 1M.40 but not 1M.35, the greater published output is relevant. If both tractors satisfy your tasks, the decision may turn on dealer support, available machine configuration, physical size, local pricing and service. Do not assume higher engine hp guarantees higher loader lifting or longer engine life.

Dealer checklist

  1. Get both quotes with the same cab/ROPS, transmission, tires and attachments.
  2. Confirm the exact rear PTO horsepower and rpm for the configurations quoted.
  3. Compare the loader models and lifting charts at the same load center.
  4. Check fitment and the actual weight of each implement.
  5. Evaluate local parts availability, maintenance intervals and warranty conditions.

Official source

Massey Ferguson M Series North America specifications, reviewed November 23, 2026. The exact model-year operator manuals and manufacturer attachment documentation take priority over generalized comparison articles.

records.title: Massey Ferguson MF 2M.50 vs John Deere 5050E: 50 HP Tractor Specs & Buying Guide
records.excerpt: Compare the US MF 2M.50 compact tractor and John Deere 5050E utility tractor using manufacturer engine, PTO, machine weight, transmission and hitch figures.
records.content:
Both the Massey Ferguson MF 2M.50 and John Deere 5050E sit near the 50-engine-horsepower mark, but their equipment classes and available configurations differ. The MF 2M.50 is positioned as a premium compact tractor; the 5050E is a utility tractor. A comparable engine horsepower headline does not mean identical lifting performance, footprint, PTO equipment or attachments. This guide uses US manufacturer references rather than owner anecdotes or dealer price guesses.

Official US specification comparison

Published specificationMF 2M.50John Deere 5050E
Rated engine horsepower48.8 hp50 hp
Rated PTO horsepower38.1 hp mechanical / 36.2 hp HST38 hp rated
Transmission informationMechanical and HST variants in the US MF tableSyncShuttle 9 forward / 3 reverse in cited Deere record
Three-point hitch lift at 24 inches behind3,307 lb mechanical / 3,086 lb HSTNot established at matching 24-inch position in cited Deere model record
Published machine weight4,035 lb ROPS / 4,398 lb cab5,335 lb base machine
Loader lifting capacity1,880 lb at maximum height, 19.5 inches ahead of pivot (MF specified setup)Requires exact loader model, lift height and load-center chart

Do not treat these as identical configurations. The MF weight figures are separated by platform/cab, while the Deere listing describes a base tractor. Deere weight, performance and available transmission selections may vary by installed equipment and edition. No brand has been assigned a made-up 24-inch hitch or loader value where the measured condition was not verified.

Which has more usable PTO horsepower?

The John Deere 5050E lists 38 rated PTO hp. The MF 2M.50 lists 38.1 PTO hp for its mechanical version or 36.2 with HST. On paper, the mechanical MF and Deere figures are extremely close. An implement's safe operation still depends on required PTO shaft speed, driveline and shielding, hitch geometry and implement power limits. For the MF, do not quote the mechanical PTO rating when discussing an HST-equipped example. See engine power versus PTO power and 540 versus 1000 rpm PTO.

Why transmission choice matters

A hydrostatic drivetrain can be convenient for frequent changes of direction during loader and property work. A mechanical shuttle transmission may be preferred for other jobs, depending on the operator and task. The MF 2M.50 is listed with mechanical and HST variants, with different factory PTO and hitch values. Deere's referenced 5050E is a SyncShuttle 9F/3R configuration. Before ordering, ask the dealer for the exact offered transmission, cab or ROPS, rear PTO equipment and any transmission-specific ratings.

Rear hitch ratings are not automatically comparable

Massey Ferguson publishes 3,307 lb of rear lift for its mechanical MF 2M.50 and 3,086 lb for HST, measured at 24 inches behind the hitch. Our source record for Deere 5050E confirms a Category 2 hitch convertible to Category 1 but does not establish a directly comparable 24-inch figure. A dealer's lift number at the lower-link ends should not be inserted into this table as if it were the same test. For guidance read three-point hitch lift: test locations and quick-hitch fitment and bushings.

Loader capacity and machine stability

MF provides a 1,880-lb loader rating at maximum height and 19.5 inches ahead of the pivot in its US model table. It is not a promise that 1,880 lb can be handled at the center of a pallet on long fork tines. Deere 5050E loader options must be compared at a matching reference distance and height. Check bucket or fork mass, maximum loader limits, axle loading, manufacturer-prescribed rear ballast, and tire specifications. See loader couplers and pallet-fork safety.

Weight, transport and tractor class

MF lists 4,035 lb for ROPS and 4,398 lb for cab in its factory table. Deere lists a 5,335-lb base machine. These are not necessarily equivalent ready-to-work configurations and cannot by themselves predict better field traction or stability. Actual transport weight rises with attachments and ballast. Verify trailer load rating, tie-down points, axle limits and storage dimensions before buying either machine.

Which machine fits your job?

Small fields and mower work

Start with required PTO horsepower, implement weight and hitch geometry, then evaluate turning room, tire options, service access and the machine's actual footprint.

Loader and materials handling

Compare dealer-quoted equipment packages with the same bucket or fork type, actual measured loader capacity, hydraulic couplers and approved ballast. Do not rank the machines by raw pump output without matching the circuits.

Utility work and multiple implements

Check hitch category, remote hydraulic valves, PTO options, drawbar requirements and compatibility with existing farm implements. A compact and a utility tractor may suit different implements even at almost identical engine hp.

Dealer comparison checklist

  1. Record model, build year, serial/PIN and transmission for both quoted tractors.
  2. Compare tractor plus loader, tires, ballast and hydraulic options, not bare MSRP alone.
  3. Request 24-inch rear hitch numbers for the exact configurations and editions.
  4. Compare loader ratings using the same forward load center and lift height.
  5. Verify attachments, PTO rpm and driveline guarding.
  6. Get maintenance schedules, warranty conditions and a local parts/service estimate.

Primary manufacturer references

Figures originate from Massey Ferguson North America's M Series model specification chart and the John Deere 5050E US specifications. Manufacturer data are subject to revisions, and this is not an independent test of reliability, pricing or performance.

records.title: Massey Ferguson MF 1M.40 vs Kubota L3902 HST: Power, Hitch & Weight
records.excerpt: US specification comparison of MF 1M.40 and Kubota L3902 HST: engine and PTO horsepower, hitch lift at 24 inches, published base weights and source-edition caveats.
records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 1M.40 and Kubota L3902 HST 4WD appeal to owners looking for compact tractors around 40 gross engine horsepower. Both can be considered for mowing, landscaping and properly matched loader tasks, but their published rear hitch capacities and PTO figures need careful interpretation. This comparison uses two manufacturer sources and distinguishes the MF's hydrostatic variant from its mechanical rating.

Compact tractor comparison table

Published ratingMF 1M.40 HSTKubota L3902 HST 4WD
Engine power39.4 hp rated37.5 hp gross
PTO power27.9 hp HST30.3 hp
Rear hitch lift, 24 inches behind lift points2,535 lb1,433 lb (US L02 brochure edition)
Rear PTO shaft speedConfirm exact variant in MF operator manual540 rpm in Kubota brochure
Hydraulic flowNot established in matched MF model table6.8 US gpm main + 4.1 steering
Listed ROPS tractor weight3,428 lb2,921 lb
Loader capacity1,870 lb at maximum height, 19.5 inches forward of pivotRequires matching Kubota loader model and measurement condition

Specification editions matter. Massey Ferguson's current US model chart and Kubota's L02 HST 4WD brochure are separate manufacturer documents. These weights are not identical equipped tractor configurations. The table intentionally leaves unmatched loader and hydraulic measurements blank rather than creating an invalid numerical ranking.

Engine horsepower versus actual PTO output

The MF 1M.40 is listed at 39.4 rated engine hp, while Kubota's L3902 HST lists 37.5 gross engine hp. Those engine values use manufacturer's stated conventions. At the PTO, however, the cited Kubota HST outputs 30.3 hp versus MF HST's 27.9 hp. The mechanical-transmission MF 1M.40 lists a higher 30.0 PTO hp, but that is not the HST configuration being compared here. Choose a cutter or tiller using its documented required PTO power, allowable tractor weight, shaft rpm and hitch category rather than engine horsepower alone. See engine hp versus PTO hp explained.

Hitch lift: compare ratings measured 24 inches back

MF's chart lists a 2,535-lb rear lift value at 24 inches behind the hitch; Kubota's L02 HST brochure lists 1,433 lb for the L3902 HST at 24 inches. These two published figures share a nominal measurement distance, but a safe implement selection still depends on link geometry, tractor ballast, actual center of gravity and other manufacturer limits. More lifting capacity does not mean every heavy attachment fits. For the measurement distinction read the 24-inch hitch lift guide.

Weight and ballast

The MF 1M.40 ROPS weight is listed as 3,428 lb, and the Kubota L3902 HST ROPS brochure figure is 2,921 lb. Loader, tires, rear attachment, ballast and cab options can change operating and transport weights. Heavier is not automatically safer: center of gravity, ground slope, speed and the manufacturer's recommended setup matter more than any single catalog number. See compact tractor tire pressure and ballast for additional checks.

What about loader work?

MF lists a loader rating of 1,870 lb at maximum height and 19.5 inches forward of pivot. Kubota's L3902 uses an appropriate factory loader configuration that must be identified by its exact model and comparable load-center rating. Do not compare the MF load-center figure to a Kubota bucket-pivot figure as though both measured the same position. A fork frame also adds its own weight and moves the load center. See why loader capacity changes with measurement points and attachment fitment.

Service and dealer considerations

Both brands have their own parts systems, service procedures and accessory catalogs. Request dealer-written confirmation for the exact tractor serial, transmission, installed loader and planned implements. Compare the cost of fluids, filters, tires and service access, as well as actual shop availability and warranty terms. A paper specification advantage may not matter if the tractor cannot fit your storage building or the dealer cannot service the installed equipment promptly.

Before purchasing

  1. Request quotes for equivalent HST, ROPS, tires, loader and ballast arrangements.
  2. Check PTO hp and shaft rpm against every implement manual.
  3. Compare rear lift at the same test location, then confirm implement geometry.
  4. Check loader lift at the same forward distance and height.
  5. Ask about auxiliary hydraulic pressure and usable flow at installed couplers.
  6. Verify equipped transport weight and physical clearances.

Official source references

See Massey Ferguson's current US M Series specifications and Kubota's L02 specifications brochure. Measurements belong to stated model editions; actual serial-specific equipment and manuals take precedence. No warranty, price or performance ranking is implied.

records.title: New Holland WORKMASTER 35 vs KIOTI CK3520H: 35 HP Tractor Comparison
records.excerpt: Compare the New Holland WORKMASTER 35 and KIOTI CK3520H using official US engine, PTO, hydraulic and rear-hitch data, including important transmission and test-point differences.
records.content:
The New Holland WORKMASTER 35 and KIOTI CK3520H both serve buyers looking for a compact tractor in the roughly 35-engine-horsepower range. They are not identical configurations: New Holland offers gear and hydrostatic choices in its WORKMASTER compact line, while the CK3520H specifically identifies the hydrostatic version of KIOTI's CK3520 family. Compare the exact build before evaluating drivetrain feel, implements or total ownership cost.

Published US specification comparison

Published valueNew Holland WORKMASTER 35KIOTI CK3520H
Gross engine horsepower35 hp34.9 hp
Rear PTO speed540 rpm540 rpm
PTO horsepowerVerify by transmission and source edition28.9 hp
TransmissionGear or HST in model familyThree-range HST
Published hydraulic flow8.2 US gpm implement hydraulic flow11.7 US gpm pump capacity; available implement flow not established
Hitch lift at 24 inchesNo verified matching 24-in measurement in referenced product pageNo verified matching 24-in measurement in referenced model page
Published tractor massConfirm chosen configuration2,734 lb in cited manufacturer model record
Fuel capacityConfirm chosen configuration9 US gal

Important measurement warning: the hydraulic numbers do not represent the same thing. New Holland explicitly identifies 8.2 gpm as dedicated implement hydraulic flow. KIOTI labels 11.7 gpm as pump capacity. Do not subtract the two values and claim that either model's loader or third-function attachment will move proportionally faster.

Engine power is nearly identical on paper

The manufacturer references list 35 gross engine horsepower for the WORKMASTER 35 and 34.9 for the CK3520H. That 0.1-hp difference is not a useful independent performance ranking. Check the type of work, engine speed at rated PTO output, actual transmission selection and implement requirements. For a PTO-driven cutter, use documented PTO power and shaft speed, not gross engine output. KIOTI lists 28.9 PTO hp for the CK3520H; a matched WORKMASTER 35 PTO figure is intentionally not supplied here without confirmation of the exact drivetrain edition. Read our engine vs PTO power guide.

Hydraulic circuit flow and loader performance

New Holland describes dedicated implement hydraulic flow of 8.2 US gpm in its WORKMASTER compact range, while KIOTI publishes 11.7 US gpm of pump capacity. The hydraulic system's usable output at a given loader or remote circuit depends on how pumps, steering, valves and pressure limits are configured. A simple catalog GPM comparison does not establish actual loader speed or force. Ask the dealer for the loader and valve specifications of the complete tractor build; see hydraulic pump versus implement flow.

Rear three-point hitch: compare like with like

New Holland and KIOTI both advertise rear hitch lifting capability, but the product pages used here do not establish a common measurement at 24 inches behind the lower-link ends. As a result, the table does not present these as directly comparable lift ratings. The actual weight, center of gravity and category of each implement matter. Review how hitch lift figures are measured before selecting a rotary cutter, box blade or other rear attachment.

HST versus gear transmission

The CK3520H uses a three-range hydrostatic drivetrain, whereas the WORKMASTER 35 model family is offered in different transmission versions. That distinction matters in loader operations with repeated direction changes. Do not assume one WORKMASTER 35 quotation includes the same transmission as a dealer's other listing. Ask to test the exact model, record the serial/PIN, and confirm service and PTO specifications for the selected version.

Which tractor fits your property?

Frequent loader work

Compare approved front loaders at the same lift height and load center; include fork or bucket weight, rear ballast and tires. Avoid using gross horsepower or unqualified pump-flow numbers as the lifting-capacity rating.

Rotary mowing and brush cutting

Compare actual PTO power, implement minimum power, safe operating width and hitch requirements. Tire selection, ground conditions and turning room may be more relevant than the nominal engine horsepower difference.

Long-term ownership

Check dealer service distances, OEM filter and wear-part availability, warranty conditions, operator manuals and your local support network. Do not invent a reliability or fuel-economy winner without controlled evidence.

Dealer quote checklist

  1. Write down the exact tractor model year, transmission, serial/PIN, tires and cab/ROPS package.
  2. Identify the loader and rear implements included in each price quote.
  3. Request rated PTO horsepower for the precise configuration.
  4. Compare hydraulics by circuit and pressure, not total pump numbers.
  5. Ask for rear hitch lift measured at the same location.
  6. Compare maintenance intervals, parts support and documented service history.

Manufacturer references

New Holland WORKMASTER 35 US product specifications identify gross horsepower, rear PTO and dedicated hydraulic flow. KIOTI CK3520H official specifications provide the model's engine, PTO, pump capacity and fuel tank figures. This is a sourced buyer comparison, not independent testing or a certification of attachment fitment.

records.title: Massey Ferguson GC1725M vs MF 1M.25: Sub-Compact or Compact Tractor?
records.excerpt: Understand the differences between the Massey Ferguson GC1725M sub-compact and MF 1M.25 compact: PTO power, rear lift at 24 in, weight and loader ratings.
records.content:
The Massey Ferguson GC1725M and Massey Ferguson MF 1M.25 have similar rated engine horsepower on paper. However, their manufacturer specifications show important differences in rear hitch lift, base machine weight and tractor class. This article explains where the published US values are comparable and where buyers must confirm the exact transmission, cab, tires and attachments before choosing between a sub-compact and a compact tractor.

Official US specification table

SpecificationGC1725M sub-compactMF 1M.25 compact
Engine horsepower24.5 hp24.8 hp
PTO horsepower18.5 hp18.2 hp platform / 16.9 hp cab
Transmission informationTwo-range hydrostaticVerify transmission/package in current MF 1M.25 build
Rear three-point lift at 24 in behind hitch661 lb1,058 lb
Published tractor weight1,477 lb base2,172 lb ROPS / 2,502 lb cab
Published implement hydraulic flow6.9 US gpmNot established in the cited US model table
Published loader lift valueRequires exact fitted loader specifications852 lb at maximum height, 19.5 in forward of pivot

Both models' rear hitch values are specifically labeled as 24-inch-behind measurements in the sources used. However, the same figures are not direct proof of safe implement fitment: geometry, hitch category, ballast and tire choices must also be reviewed. The published weights are not measured with identical accessories.

Engine HP is a poor way to classify these tractors

There is only a 0.3-hp difference between the factory engine figures, but the machines are different physical classes. The heavier MF 1M.25 offers a larger published three-point lift rating, with corresponding transport and maneuvering tradeoffs. The GC1725M's lower base mass may appeal to owners with narrow access, smaller trailers or sensitive turf, provided that the actual tire and implement setup is approved. Neither tractor can be recommended for a specific property on horsepower alone.

PTO rating and implement matching

Massey Ferguson lists 18.5 PTO hp for the GC1725M. The current MF M Series table lists 18.2 PTO hp for the platform MF 1M.25 and 16.9 for the cab version. The cab value should not be substituted for the platform specification or vice versa. For a mid-mount mower, rear rotary cutter or snowblower, confirm the actual machine's PTO shaft configuration, minimum and maximum implement power and required controls. See the engine-versus-PTO horsepower guide.

Hitch capacity: 661 versus 1,058 lb at the same nominal test distance

The GC1725M table lists 661 lb at 24 inches behind the hitch; the MF 1M.25 table lists 1,058 lb at the same stated nominal location. That can help identify a meaningful functional difference in manufacturer hitch ratings. Yet the 397-lb numerical gap is not a license to lift a specific attachment of equal mass, since its center of gravity, category, top-link geometry and stability could impose a lower practical limit. Read how rear hitch lifting specifications work.

What about the loader?

For the MF 1M.25, the manufacturer lists 852 lb at maximum lift height and 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin in its current US table. The GC1725M requires the actual loader specification to provide a comparable number. Comparing one tractor's loader-pivot lift rating with the other's forward load-center rating would be misleading. If your main task is moving pallets, compare the selected fork and loader combination, check rear ballast and pay attention to attachment weight and the effective load center. See our front-loader attachment checklist.

Weight, storage and property maintenance

GC1725M's published base mass is 1,477 lb. The MF 1M.25 ROPS tractor is listed at 2,172 lb, while its cab variant is 2,502 lb. These are factory values for different configurations and should not be treated as full operating weights. Think about garage clearance, yard gates, soft lawns, tire selection and available trailer capacity. A front loader, ballast, backhoe or mower deck can materially change the delivered mass and dimensions.

What to ask before signing a quotation

  1. Compare the same intended equipment package: loader, bucket, mower, rear ballast and tires.
  2. Confirm GC1725M model-year availability and correct serial/PIN.
  3. Check platform versus cab and actual transmission on the MF 1M.25.
  4. Request rear and loader lift figures measured at matching reference points.
  5. Review PTO rpm and implement certification for the actual supplied machine.
  6. Include maintenance costs, local parts and dealer support in the decision.

Manufacturer documentation

Massey Ferguson's US sub-compact model table reports the GC1725M figures. Massey Ferguson's US M Series specifications list MF 1M.25 platform/cab data. Check the equipment's individual operator manuals for any safe compatibility decision. Specifications are not a current inventory or price offer.

specs.fms_engine_make: Massey Ferguson M Series four-cylinder Iseki diesel (exact engine model verify by serial)
specs.fms_configuration_notes: MF 2M.60 US manufacturer table: 60.3 rated engine HP; PTO 47.0 mechanical / 44.6 HST; rear lift measured 24 inches behind 3,307 lb mechanical / 3,086 HST; loader max lift at max height 19.5 inches forward of pivot 1,880 lb; weight 4,255 lb ROPS / 4,641 lb cab. Manufacturer cautions variation by tires and transmission. PTO and hitch single-value fields omitted because values vary by drivetrain.

records.content:
The Massey Ferguson MF 2M.60 is a North American M Series compact tractor. Its official manufacturer chart reports 60.3 rated engine horsepower and distinguishes the published PTO and lifting capabilities by the exact version. This page does not present an unspecified loader option or an alternative transmission's PTO output as a universal rating.

US technical specifications

<
Factory-listed measurementPublished MF 2M.60 value

Engine power versus PTO output

The factory chart separates 47.0 PTO hp for the mechanical transmission from 44.6 PTO hp for hydrostatic drive. The mechanical-versus-HST distinction can affect the suitability of PTO-powered mowers, tillers and other implements. Engine horsepower alone cannot establish usable PTO output. Confirm the implement's minimum and maximum shaft power, the exact PTO operating speed, its coupling and driveline guards. See our engine horsepower vs PTO horsepower guide and PTO speed and shaft compatibility checklist.

Rear hitch lift: understand the 24-inch measurement

The manufacturer's listed rear hitch rating is MECH 3,307 lb; HST 3,086 lb, measured 24 inches behind the lift points. The mechanical and HST tractors have different listed lift figures, so match this number to the exact transmission. A heavy implement with a long center of mass, poor hitch geometry or inadequate ballast can be unsafe even if its static mass appears below a published lift value. See our 24-inch hitch rating explanation.

Front loader and pallet fork work

The US table gives a maximum loader rating of 1,880 lb at maximum lift height and 19.5 inches ahead of the pivot pin. This is a stated test condition, not permission to handle a load of the same mass on long pallet forks or with arbitrary attachments. Ask the dealer which loader, fork frame, coupler and ballast configuration is supplied. Check the full lifting chart, center of gravity, tires and stability requirements. Use our loader quick-attach and fork fitment guide before buying attachments.

Weight, cab and storage clearance

The manufacturer lists 4,255 lb with ROPS and 4,641 lb with cab. ROPS overall height is 102.4 inches; cab height is 92.7 inches. Tire choice and transmission can change the listed base mass, and an installed loader, filled tires or rear implement will change transport weight. Verify the delivered machine's actual dimensions before selecting a garage opening, trailer, tie-down arrangement or transport route.

Practical ownership considerations

Compare the complete dealer package rather than a horsepower headline. If you need repeated forward/reverse movement, evaluate available transmission choices for the exact model. If you plan rotary mowing, confirm rear PTO power and the implement's specifications. For rear-mounted tools, check hitch geometry, hydraulic connections, transport position and the installed ballast. For winter property work, cab equipment and suitable attachments can be more important than small horsepower differences. Review our tractor winter preparation guide.

Questions to ask before purchase

  1. Confirm the tractor's full model, year, serial and transmission configuration.
  2. Get the manufacturer-approved loader and implement fitment list.
  3. Ask for measured hydraulic implement flow and pressure at any installed remotes.
  4. Check actual PTO power, shaft speed and guarding for the configuration.
  5. Verify delivered weight, tire package, approved ballast and height clearance.
  6. Request manuals, maintenance intervals and local OEM parts support.

Related equipment

See the MF 2M.50 and MF 2M.65 model records. Our MF 2M family comparison explains when the published differences may matter.

Original manufacturer documentation

Massey Ferguson US M Series specifications, reviewed November 24, 2026. Manufacturer values may change; always confirm the serial-specific manual and complete dealer build before making a safety-critical decision.
