For winter property work, cab equipment and suitable attachments can be more important than small horsepower differences. Review our tractor winter preparation guide.

Questions to ask before purchase

  1. Confirm the tractor's full model, year, serial and transmission configuration.
  2. Get the manufacturer-approved loader and implement fitment list.
  3. Ask for measured hydraulic implement flow and pressure at any installed remotes.
  4. Check actual PTO power, shaft speed and guarding for the configuration.
  5. Verify delivered weight, tire package, approved ballast and height clearance.
  6. Request manuals, maintenance intervals and local OEM parts support.

Related equipment

See the MF 2M.50 and MF 2M.60 model records. Our MF 2M family comparison explains when the published differences may matter.

Original manufacturer documentation

Massey Ferguson US M Series specifications, reviewed November 24, 2026. Manufacturer values may change; always confirm the serial-specific manual and complete dealer build before making a safety-critical decision.

records.title: Massey Ferguson MF 2M.50 vs 2M.60 vs 2M.65: Specs and PTO Comparison
records.excerpt: Compare official US MF 2M.50, 2M.60 and 2M.65 tractor horsepower, PTO, hitch capacity, loader measurements and cab/ROPS weights in a configuration-aware chart.
records.content:
Which Massey Ferguson 2M tractor is best suited to your work: the MF 2M.50, MF 2M.60 or MF 2M.65? Their North American manufacturer specification table reveals a meaningful increase in engine and PTO power, while some published loader capacities remain unchanged. There are also differences in transmission-specific hitch ratings and machine weight. This comparison identifies exactly which numbers can be compared and which require a particular configuration.

MF 2M Series specifications, US manufacturer table

Factory measureMF 2M.50MF 2M.60MF 2M.65
Rated engine horsepower48.8 hp60.3 hp65.7 hp
PTO power38.1 mechanical / 36.2 HST hp47.0 mechanical / 44.6 HST hp50.0 hp, cab listing
Rear lift at 24 inches behind hitch3,307 mechanical / 3,086 HST lb3,307 mechanical / 3,086 HST lb3,483 lb, published value
Loader at maximum height, 19.5 in ahead of pivot1,880 lb1,880 lb1,880 lb
ROPS tractor weight4,035 lb4,255 lbNot listed in this model row
Cab tractor weight4,398 lb4,641 lb4,608 lb
Cab height92.9 in92.7 in92.9 in

These are published manufacturer model-table values, not an independent head-to-head test of identical equipment builds. Massey Ferguson notes that weights may vary depending on tire choice and transmission. Its MF 2M.65 row displays a cab PTO rating rather than the mechanical/HST split listed for the other two models.

What changes as horsepower increases?

Moving from MF 2M.50 to 2M.60 raises the manufacturer-listed engine rating from 48.8 to 60.3 hp. The mechanical PTO figures increase from 38.1 to 47.0 hp; the HST figures increase from 36.2 to 44.6 hp. Those differences may be relevant when selecting a rotary mower, tiller or other PTO-driven attachment whose official minimum power requirement is close to the lower model's rating. Do not compare the 2M.65 cab PTO number to an imagined mechanical or HST version that the cited table does not specify. Read our PTO versus engine power reference.

Why loader capacity remains the same in the chart

All three models list 1,880 lb at maximum loader height and 19.5 inches forward of the pivot pin. A more powerful engine does not necessarily raise the front loader's published structural or hydraulic rating. That number also does not mean that a 1,880-lb pallet can be safely carried on fork tines, where the load center may sit farther forward. The approved loader assembly, fork rating, tire setup, ballast, lifting height and travel conditions govern actual handling. See our quick-attach and pallet fork guide.

Hitch capacity and drivetrain variants

For MF 2M.50 and 2M.60, Massey Ferguson publishes 3,307 lb at 24 inches behind the hitch for the mechanical variant and 3,086 lb for HST. The 2M.65 row lists 3,483 lb. These are not measurements directly at the link ends and do not guarantee compatibility with a long or heavy attachment. Check the exact drivetrain, hitch category, center-of-mass location and rear ballast before selecting equipment. Our hitch rating guide explains the measurement position.

Cab and transport planning

The MF 2M.50 is listed at 4,398 lb in cab configuration; the MF 2M.60 at 4,641 lb; and the MF 2M.65 at 4,608 lb. These are not guaranteed delivered weights with loaders, full fuel, wheel ballast and rear implements installed. Garage height, turning radius and transport platform also affect a purchase. The listed cab height differences are small, but door clearance should be checked on the actual tractor and tires. Do not select a trailer using the catalog number alone.

Buying checklist for commercial and property owners

  1. Get written dealer quotes identifying model, transmission and cab/ROPS variant.
  2. Match the required implement PTO power and shaft speed to the delivered machine.
  3. Check loader and rear lift ratings at comparable test positions.
  4. Confirm auxiliary hydraulic flow, pressure, couplers and compatible attachments.
  5. Verify actual width, height, operating weight and ballast configuration.
  6. Compare dealer service coverage, OEM parts availability and warranty conditions.
  7. Arrange a test drive involving realistic maneuvering and the intended implements.

Manufacturer source

The figures in this article come from the official US Massey Ferguson MF M Series model comparison table, reviewed November 24, 2026. Exact model-year documentation and installed configurations take priority over general comparisons.

records.title: John Deere M805011 Water Pump V-Belt: 1025R Fitment & Inspection
records.serial_scope: John Deere's US parts listing includes the 1025R as a generally compatible model, but does not establish a universal production serial range on the referenced page. Verify the exact tractor serial/PIN and its fitted belt-drive arrangement in the official parts diagram.
records.excerpt: OEM John Deere M805011 water-pump V-belt: published effective length 952.5 mm (37.5 in), general 1025R application and serial-specific verification checklist.
records.content:
John Deere M805011 is identified by John Deere's US parts store as a water-pump V-belt with a published effective length of 952.5 mm (37.5 inches). The store's general model-application list includes the John Deere 1025R. That list is a starting point for parts research, not proof that the belt fits every tractor carrying the 1025R name or that an owner's installed belt has never been changed.

Published OEM identification

FieldManufacturer reference
OEM part numberM805011
Part typeWater-pump V-belt
Effective belt length952.5 mm (37.5 in), per Deere's listing
General model listingJohn Deere 1025R included among compatible-model references
Verified 1025R serial-number rangeNot supplied by the cited public listing; check official serial-filtered catalog
Installation and adjustmentFollow the correct engine/tractor operator or technical manual

What the belt does

On applicable engine arrangements, a V-belt transmits rotation to the water-pump drive and associated accessories as designed by the manufacturer. A slipping, damaged or missing belt can affect cooling-system operation and may produce abnormal noises or overheating. But a hot-running engine can also result from a blocked radiator screen, coolant loss, faulty components or excessive workload. Do not assume belt replacement alone will correct overheating without first identifying the fault.

Safe symptoms to document

  • Visible cracking, frayed belt edges, missing sections or obvious contamination.
  • Persistent squeal or a new noise near the belt-driven accessory area.
  • An abnormal engine-temperature warning or signs of inadequate coolant circulation.
  • Evidence that a previous repair installed the wrong belt routing or pulley hardware.

These observations are not a diagnosis. With the engine shut down, key removed and rotating components fully stopped, follow the operator manual for accessible inspection points. Never reach near a running belt or fan. Do not touch a hot cooling system or open a pressurized radiator cap.

Checking exact fitment before buying

  1. Record the complete machine model and serial/PIN from its identification plate.
  2. Confirm the fitted engine and any changed accessory or pulley assembly.
  3. Look up the OEM belt-drive diagram for that serial number.
  4. Verify whether M805011 is the currently specified part or if the catalog notes a supersession.
  5. Confirm the mounting and belt routing in the applicable service documentation.

Belt length does not establish interchangeability

A second aftermarket belt may share a stated nominal length but differ in cross-section, angle, width, construction or manufacturer-approved application. Do not choose replacements from length alone. The quoted 952.5-mm figure is the manufacturer's effective length, not a generic outside circumference measurement to transfer blindly between brands.

Related service references

Before troubleshooting overheating, read coolant testing and corrosion guidance and the general radiator-screen overheating example (which describes a different tractor and is not an M805011 fitment claim). A further cooling-system part reference is John Deere MIU800071 water-pump gasket. Both parts require independent serial-specific verification.

Original manufacturer source

John Deere US parts catalog: M805011. Consult the current Deere dealer catalog for the exact serial/PIN, installed engine and supersession notes. No torque, belt-tension setting, part substitution or universal installation procedure is asserted here.

records.title: John Deere MIU800071 Water Pump Gasket: 1025R OEM Parts Reference
records.serial_scope: John Deere's official US product listing names 1025R in its general equipment application list for MIU800071. The public result does not establish a comprehensive production-serial range or every engine variant; validate machine serial/PIN and water pump assembly in OEM parts catalog.
records.excerpt: John Deere MIU800071 water-pump gasket: OEM part identity, general 1025R listing, cooling-system leak checks, and serial-number-based purchase checklist.
records.content:
John Deere MIU800071 is listed in the official John Deere US parts catalog as a water-pump gasket. The manufacturer includes the 1025R sub-compact tractor in its general compatible-equipment listing. The public listing does not tell you which production serial numbers, installed engine changes or water-pump assemblies are covered, so verify those details in the correct serial-filtered OEM diagram before ordering.

At-a-glance OEM details

FieldWhat is documented
OEM part numberMIU800071
Component descriptionWater-pump gasket
General listed modelJohn Deere 1025R
Exact 1025R production serial rangeNot established in public model listing
Compatible pump assemblyConfirm in serial-specific exploded parts diagram
Sealant and installation torqueUse technical manual; not specified by the cited product page

What is a water-pump gasket?

The gasket seals a joint in the engine cooling system according to the manufacturer's pump assembly design. It must match the intended mating surfaces, coolant system and gasket orientation. A coolant leak near the front of the engine does not prove that the gasket is faulty: hoses, clamps, drain points, a pump seal and other connections can leak. Before replacing anything, identify the leak source by the safe inspection method described in the tractor's service instructions.

Safety before cooling-system inspection

Stop the tractor on safe level ground, lower equipment, switch off the engine and allow it to cool completely. Never remove the cap of a hot pressurized cooling system. The cooling fan and belt system have moving pinch points; do not place hands or tools near rotating accessories. Clean up coolant spills immediately, keep coolant away from pets and dispose of used fluid according to local requirements.

How to verify MIU800071 fitment

  1. Locate the tractor's serial plate and record the complete model and product identification number.
  2. Identify the fitted engine and current water-pump assembly.
  3. Look up the pump's exploded OEM parts illustration for that serial range.
  4. Confirm the gasket part number, any manufacturer supersession and the number of required pieces.
  5. Use the appropriate technical manual for coolant draining, surface preparation, reassembly and leak testing.

Why a similar-looking gasket is not enough

A gasket can appear to match a housing outline while having different openings, thickness, construction or material requirements. Those differences may affect sealing or coolant flow. The gasket in this listing should not be represented as a universal replacement for every Yanmar diesel engine or other Deere tractor. Verify installed pump hardware rather than assuming a match from engine horsepower, model marketing name or an aftermarket cross-reference alone.

Related cooling and belt references

The M805011 water-pump V-belt is a separate part used on a generally listed 1025R application, not automatically included with this gasket. Review diesel tractor coolant testing for manufacturer-specific chemistry and safety checks, and how to identify OEM parts by tractor serial number before ordering.

Primary reference

John Deere official US store: MIU800071 water-pump gasket. The seller's general equipment list is not a warranty of fitment for an individual modified or differently equipped machine. Confirm with a dealer when the serial-filtered parts diagram is inconclusive.

records.title: John Deere 1025R Cooling System: Belt, Water Pump Gasket & Leak Checks
records.excerpt: A safe owner-level guide to possible cooling-system issues on the John Deere 1025R, with OEM M805011 belt and MIU800071 gasket identification and serial checks.
records.content:
If your John Deere 1025R runs hotter than expected, loses coolant or shows a new noise around its front engine accessories, do not order a water pump or gasket based on one symptom. A dirty radiator screen, incorrect coolant level, loose or damaged hose, belt wear, sensor issue or other fault can produce overlapping signs. The first steps are safe shutdown, documenting the exact symptoms, and checking the parts diagram for the machine's model and serial/PIN.

Symptom-first cooling checklist

ObservationPossible areaFirst safe check
Temperature warning while mowingAirflow restriction, coolant condition or another cooling faultStop and allow cooling; inspect external screen after shutdown
Visible dried coolant depositHose, connection, pump or gasket areaInspect visually only with the system cool and engine off
New squeal near engine accessoriesDrive belt, pulleys or related componentsPark and inspect accessible belt condition, not while running
Coolant repeatedly below indicated levelLeak, cap, expansion system or other faultUse prescribed cold-engine level check; seek diagnosis
Steam or fluid sprayPotential overheating or pressurized cooling failureMove away, stop operation and avoid opening hot caps

Step 1: distinguish airflow and coolant problems

Inspect external radiator screens and louvers using the operator manual's instructions after the tractor is safely stopped. Grass, chaff and dirt can reduce cooling airflow during mowing. This does not establish a failed water-pump belt or gasket. If the engine continues to overheat after manufacturer-approved checks, stop work and arrange service rather than repeatedly driving a hot engine.

Step 2: examine belt condition safely

John Deere's parts catalog identifies M805011 as a water-pump V-belt with a published 952.5-mm (37.5-in) effective length, and includes 1025R in its general model listing. Do not reach into rotating fan or belt assemblies, and do not adjust tension by guesswork. A similar-looking or equally long aftermarket belt may have a different section and construction. Verify the OEM diagram for your serial number before replacement.

Step 3: understand the water-pump gasket

The manufacturer also lists MIU800071 as a water-pump gasket with general 1025R applicability. It is a different component from a hose, radiator cap, belt or complete pump. A puddle under a parked tractor does not prove that the gasket needs replacement. If repair would involve removing the pump, draining coolant or opening the pressure system, follow the complete technical manual or have a qualified mechanic perform the work.

Step 4: do not guess the coolant formulation

Coolant protection against freezing and corrosion depends on the approved chemistry and prescribed test. Color is not a reliable specification. Never open a hot pressurized cooling system; allow it to cool fully as required. Do not introduce unapproved supplemental additives, plain water or a random automotive antifreeze into a system without following the engine maker's instructions. Read our diesel tractor coolant testing guide.

What to record for the dealer

  1. Machine model, complete serial/PIN, engine serial and hour-meter reading.
  2. Symptoms, warning messages and conditions that triggered the issue.
  3. Whether the radiator screen was blocked and whether the cooling fan area was dirty.
  4. Photographs of accessible leak residue and belt wear with the tractor off.
  5. Coolant type and service history if documented.
  6. OEM diagram confirmation for any belt, gasket, hose or pump being ordered.

When to stop work

Stop when the tractor reports severe engine temperature, coolant escapes rapidly, steam appears, the belt drive visibly fails or a warning persists despite allowed owner-level checks. Keep people away from hot pressurized coolant. Continued operation can cause engine damage or burns. The presence of an OEM part number in a general model listing is not a reason to replace that part without diagnosing the actual problem.

Manufacturer parts references

John Deere M805011 water-pump V-belt and John Deere MIU800071 water-pump gasket both list 1025R as general compatible equipment. Confirm actual fitment through the current serial-specific official parts catalog and repair instructions before purchasing or performing a repair.

records.excerpt: Kubota 77700-03362 BX2380 filter maintenance kit: oil, hydraulic, air and inline fuel filter numbers, supersession warnings and dealer-fitment checks.
records.content:
The Kubota 77700-03362 filter maintenance kit is listed by US Kubota dealer Messick's for numerous BX, GR and ZD machines, including the BX2380. The dealer identifies four filter types in the kit. However, the kit's original component numbers are not necessarily the newest individual replacement numbers. When ordering for a particular tractor, identify the full model and product identification number (PIN) and confirm the current contents or factory supersession notices with the Kubota parts desk.

Listed contents of Kubota 77700-03362

ComponentNumber shown in dealer kit listingImportant check
Engine oil filterHH150-32430Dealer's individual filter pages show later replacements, including HH1J0-32430 and HH1J0-32432; verify currently supplied item
Inline fuel filter12581-43012 (2 pieces)Verify fuel plumbing and number of filters for exact tractor configuration
Hydraulic filterHHK20-36990Individual listings show replacement part-number chains; consult serial-filtered diagram
Outer air filter elementK1211-82320Verify engine air cleaner housing and current part-number listing

These are the contents advertised in the dealer's published kit description, not a guarantee that the seller will ship the historical part number printed in this table after a manufacturer supersession. There is no claim that each kit item is due for replacement during every service visit.

Why kit fitment and filter fitment are different

One kit number can be offered for a range of equipment, but an individual machine's engine, HST configuration, air cleaner and fuel plumbing can vary by model edition. The dealership's application list includes BX2380, yet only a serial/PIN-specific lookup can confirm exact fit. For instance, the dealer explicitly lists an oil-filter update from HH150-32430 toward newer numbers. Ordering a legacy part by the kit label without checking the current diagram risks buying an outdated or incorrect item.

Oil filter supersession: which number should be ordered?

The dealer's HH1J0-32430 listing says that part replaces older HH150-32430 and has itself been replaced by HH1J0-32432. That information should be used as a prompt to verify current fitment and availability, not as a blanket interchangeability statement for every engine. See our BX2380 filter and service checklist for the relevant system-by-system approach.

Maintenance is not always an all-filters-at-once job

Changing engine oil, HST filter, fuel filter and air filter may occur at different engine-hour or calendar intervals depending on machine edition and operating conditions. Consult the tractor operator manual and the actual filter condition. A plugged air cleaner or contaminated fuel supply can cause symptoms that are not resolved by indiscriminately replacing unrelated filters.

Ordering checklist

  1. Record the complete model, serial/PIN and engine identity.
  2. Inspect the applicable BX2380 parts diagram and confirm the kit number's current application.
  3. Ask the dealer to confirm the current shipped components and their supersessions.
  4. Verify the count of inline fuel filters and actual engine/HST filter locations.
  5. Buy only the filters due under the appropriate maintenance schedule.
  6. Keep the receipt, hour-meter reading and service date with the machine records.

Related Kubota model and reference

Use the Kubota BX2380 specification page for the tractor baseline and Kubota 12581-43012 fuel filter reference for one component listed in the kit. Our OEM parts identification guide explains why model names alone are insufficient.

Source and scope

Messick's Kubota 77700-03362 kit listing, accessed November 24, 2026. Messick's is a Kubota parts dealer; this is dealer evidence, not a direct statement that Kubota corporate guarantees kit applicability to every tractor serial. Confirm through Kubota's serial-specific electronic parts catalog before purchase.

records.serial_scope: Messick's US Kubota dealer product listing explicitly names BX2380 among models using inline fuel filter 12581-43012 and lists two such filters in kit 77700-03362. records.excerpt: Kubota 12581-43012 inline fuel filter for listed BX2380 applications, with identification, kit quantity notes, contamination symptoms and serial-specific verification.
records.content:
Kubota 12581-43012 is an inline fuel filter listed by the US Kubota parts dealer Messick's for multiple BX tractors, including BX2380. The same dealer lists two 12581-43012 filters as components of Kubota filter kit 77700-03362. This is useful evidence for parts research, but a general model list is not enough to identify the precise position, required quantity or current replacement part for every BX2380 serial.

OEM part reference

FieldPublished dealer information
Part number12581-43012
CategoryInline diesel fuel filter
Model named by dealerKubota BX2380 among other models
Kit that lists this part77700-03362
Count in referenced kit2 filters
Serial/PIN rangeNot confirmed by the general product listing
Service intervalSee exact tractor operator manual

What an inline fuel filter does

An inline fuel filter removes certain contaminants from the fuel supply, helping protect downstream components as intended by the engine fuel system. A filter can become restricted by debris or contaminated fuel, but hard starting, loss of power or stalling also have other potential causes. Avoid treating any one symptom as proof that 12581-43012 is the failed component.

Potential symptoms to discuss with a mechanic

  • Unexpected loss of power or intermittent stalling under load.
  • Contaminated fuel discovered during documented maintenance.
  • Leaks or damaged accessible fuel-line connections.
  • An overdue fuel filter service confirmed from the owner's manual.

If fuel leaks, stop the engine and follow the manufacturer service procedure. Diesel fuel is combustible and hot engine surfaces introduce fire risks. Keep ignition sources away and do not loosen high-pressure fuel-system connections to diagnose a restriction.

Why two filters may appear in the kit

The dealer's 77700-03362 kit listing names two instances of part 12581-43012. A kit content count is not a substitute for tracing the exact installed machine's fuel supply and confirming each serviceable location in the serial-specific parts diagram. Do not assume an older or different BX model has identical plumbing.

Verify the part before ordering

  1. Confirm BX2380 or its variant from the tractor identification plate.
  2. Record full machine serial/PIN and engine details.
  3. Open the relevant OEM fuel-system illustration or ask a Kubota dealer.
  4. Confirm current 12581-43012 applicability, supersessions and quantity.
  5. Verify service interval and any required priming or air-removal procedure in the correct manual.
  6. After professional or manufacturer-prescribed replacement, inspect safely for leaks.

Related service information

See our BX2380 filter maintenance guide and diesel fuel contamination checks. For other Kubota models, including BX2680, do not assume identical filtration or quantities without checking its own engine and parts catalog.

Source

Messick's Kubota 12581-43012 listing and the dealer's filter-kit contents, checked November 24, 2026. These listings establish dealer-supplied applications, not a blanket Kubota manufacturer fitment guarantee for every serial number.

records.title: Kubota BX2380 Filter Guide: Oil, Fuel, Hydraulic & Air Filter Numbers
records.excerpt: A BX2380 owner reference for dealer-listed Kubota filter kit 77700-03362, four filter types, current number changes, serial-number verification and maintenance planning.
records.content:
Finding the right filters for a Kubota BX2380 is more complicated than copying a kit contents list into an online cart. Kubota dealer Messick's lists maintenance kit 77700-03362 for the BX2380, but several individual filter numbers have since appeared in supersession chains on the dealer's product pages. This guide separates what the dealer has actually listed from what still needs confirmation using the tractor's serial/PIN.

BX2380 filter reference table

SystemNumber in dealer-listed kitBuying note
Engine oilHH150-32430Look up current individual part: dealer identifies newer HH1J0-32430 and HH1J0-32432 chain
Diesel fuel, inline12581-43012 (two pieces)Confirm fuel-system layout and quantities by serial
Hydraulic/HSTHHK20-36990Confirm later replacement part number and current filter specification
Engine air, outerK1211-82320Confirm housing and model-specific element fit

Do not assume all filters in this table are simultaneously due. The engine oil/filter schedule, hydraulic transmission service, air filter condition and fuel service are governed by the exact operator manual and use conditions. The table records a dealer's original kit description, not an OEM-issued maintenance interval for each component.

Engine oil filter: why the number may change

The kit listing names HH150-32430 as its engine oil filter. Messick's separate HH1J0-32430 product page states that it replaces HH150-32430 and has been replaced by HH1J0-32432. Parts supersessions can be genuine catalog changes, but they need checking against the exact engine and serial before ordering. Do not replace a manufacturer's serial-filtered selection with a guessed cross-reference or a visually similar oil filter.

Fuel filtration: account for multiple locations

The listed kit contains two inline 12581-43012 fuel filters; our individual fuel filter reference describes how to verify that number. Water or dirt in diesel fuel may cause performance problems, but symptoms can have other causes. Do not open pressurized fuel lines or work near hot engine parts. Refer to diesel fuel contamination checks for safe owner-level observations.

Hydraulic/HST filter versus hydraulic fluid

The HHK20-36990 number in the dealer kit is described as a hydraulic filter. An HST oil-filter service is not the same as an automatic complete transmission fluid replacement. Use the appropriate filter and Kubota-approved lubricant for the transmission's configuration, and follow the manual's hour-meter and temperature instructions. Consult the dealer for current HHK20-36990 supersession notices before ordering a stand-alone replacement.

Air cleaner service in dusty conditions

The dealer kit lists K1211-82320 as an outer air cleaner element. A filter that looks dirty is not always due for replacement using an arbitrary schedule; follow the manual's restriction indicator, service interval and safe inspection procedure. Cleaning a dry element with improper compressed air can damage its filtering media. Read our tractor air filter maintenance guide.

Safe service checklist

  1. Identify your tractor as BX2380 or BX2380-1 and record the full serial/PIN.
  2. Consult the exact operator manual for engine-hour service intervals and filter replacement instructions.
  3. Cross-check the oil, fuel, hydraulic and air filter references in the OEM parts diagram.
  4. Ask the dealer to identify current filter numbers, including documented supersessions.
  5. Safely park, lower attachments, switch off the engine and let hot equipment cool before any allowed inspection.
  6. Keep oil and diesel fuel away from drains and dispose of used consumables properly.
  7. Log the hour-meter reading, filter numbers, fluid specifications and service date.

Other BX maintenance guides

Visit our BX2380 technical specifications or read the daily pre-operation checklist. If engine temperature climbs during mowing, a clogged radiator screen or a coolant-system issue may be involved; check the manual rather than assuming a fuel or oil filter fault.

Parts references and limitations

Dealer sources: Messick's Kubota 77700-03362 kit, Kubota 12581-43012 individual fuel filter, and oil filter supersession details. Reviewed November 24, 2026. Serial-specific Kubota documentation and current dealer verification take precedence over a generalized application list.

records.excerpt: Kubota HH1J0-32432 oil filter: US dealer-listed BX2380 and BX2380-1 application, predecessor part numbers and serial-specific purchase checklist.
records.content:
Kubota HH1J0-32432 is a engine oil filter cartridge listed by the US Kubota parts dealer Messick's for the Kubota BX2380. It is one of the service parts worth identifying by part number rather than by appearance. The published dealer listing includes model applications and a parts-number history, but a universal fitment promise would be misleading: always confirm the machine's serial/PIN and current Kubota parts illustration.

OEM part identification

FieldCatalog information
Part numberHH1J0-32432
Part descriptionEngine oil filter cartridge
Dealer-listed applicationKubota BX2380
Documented earlier part referenceHH150-32430 and HH1J0-32430 as documented in dealer replacement listings
Exact serial compatibilityConfirm with manufacturer serial-filtered catalog
Service intervalUse your model-specific operator manual

What the filter does

The oil filter removes particles from engine lubricant as intended by the diesel engine's lubrication system. Its media, sealing gasket, thread and bypass characteristics have to match the approved application. An oil filter with similar outside dimensions may not be functionally equivalent. Use the correct component and follow the equipment manual for all servicing.

Part-number supersession versus guaranteed interchangeability

The seller's public catalog documents the preceding part reference: HH150-32430 and HH1J0-32430 as documented in dealer replacement listings. That is useful for understanding older service receipts or kit instructions. A supersession shown in one dealer listing is not, by itself, proof that every historical engine or air-cleaner configuration accepts the latest part without checking serial/PIN and any installation notes. The dealer's model application section explicitly names both BX2380 and BX2380-1, but equipment revisions and engine changes still require serial-based verification.

Safe inspection and service considerations

Park and secure the tractor on level ground, shut down the engine, lower all attachments and allow hot oil and engine components to cool as prescribed. Do not guess tightening torque, oil grade, filter prefill method or service intervals from a generic online article. Verify the oil level and inspect for leaks using the engine manual's procedure after the prescribed service. Collect spent oil and the old filter for proper disposal.

How to verify the correct replacement

  1. Record tractor model BX2380 or BX2380-1 and the complete product identification number.
  2. Locate the relevant engine oil-filter assembly in the correct Kubota parts diagram.
  3. Check whether HH1J0-32432 is the currently supplied part and whether there are notes on previous numbers.
  4. Confirm that any kit package contains the approved component for the exact machine.
  5. Follow the operator manual for service intervals and safe replacement.
  6. Record the installed part number and hour-meter reading for future maintenance.

Related Kubota filter information

See the Kubota 77700-03362 filter-kit reference, BX2380 filter identification guide, and BX2380 fuel-filter record. These documents explain why kit contents and updated individual component numbers must be reconciled. For model data, use BX2380 specifications.

Dealer source and limitation

records.content:
Kubota K1211-82320 is a engine air cleaner element listed by the US Kubota parts dealer Messick's for the Kubota BX2380. It is one of the service parts worth identifying by part number rather than by appearance. The published dealer listing includes model applications and a parts-number history, but a universal fitment promise would be misleading: always confirm the machine's serial/PIN and current Kubota parts illustration.

What the filter does

The air filter helps prevent airborne dust and debris entering the engine intake system. An improper element or poorly seated seal can let contaminants pass through, especially in dusty mowing and landscaping conditions. Filter shape alone is not a reliable cross-reference. Use the correct component and follow the equipment manual for all servicing.

Part-number supersession versus guaranteed interchangeability

The seller's public catalog documents the preceding part reference: K2581-82310, according to the dealer catalog. That is useful for understanding older service receipts or kit instructions. A supersession shown in one dealer listing is not, by itself, proof that every historical engine or air-cleaner configuration accepts the latest part without checking serial/PIN and any installation notes. Air cleaner housings and filter service conditions can differ between versions; a dirty exterior is not proof that an element is unserviceable.

Safe inspection and service considerations

Shut down and secure the engine before opening any air-cleaner cover. Avoid letting loose dust fall into the clean side of the intake. Follow the operator manual's guidance on whether and how an element may be cleaned; aggressive compressed air or incorrect washing can damage filter media. Ensure the correct seal and cover are seated before returning the machine to operation.

How to verify the correct replacement

  1. Record tractor model BX2380 or BX2380-1 and the complete product identification number.
  2. Locate the relevant air-cleaner assembly in the correct Kubota parts diagram.
  3. Check whether K1211-82320 is the currently supplied part and whether there are notes on previous numbers.
  4. Confirm that any kit package contains the approved component for the exact machine.
  5. Follow the operator manual for service intervals and safe replacement.
  6. Record the installed part number and hour-meter reading for future maintenance.
